data.title: RSyncUI – A SwiftUI based macOS GUI for rsync
data.author: mickelsen
data.article_summary: RsyncUI 是一个基于 SwiftUI 的 macOS 应用程序，为命令行工具 rsync 提供图形用户界面（GUI），适用于 macOS Sonoma 及更高版本。它帮助用户组织同步任务和设置 rsync 参数，简化了 rsync 的使用。虽然 GUI 用于任务管理，但实际的同步任务是由 rsync 命令行工具执行的外部任务，RsyncUI 会监控其进度和终止状态，用户可以随时中止任务。RsyncUI 可通过 Homebrew 安装，并且已获得 Apple 的签名和公证。项目文档基于 Hugo 主题 Docsy，并使用 MIT 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 macOS 上的 rsync 工具及其图形界面（GUI）替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持 Carbon Copy Cloner (CCC)**：watersb 提到 Mike Bombich 的 Carbon Copy Cloner (CCC)，它是一个商业软件，但其对 rsync 的补丁是开源的，能够处理 Mac 特有的扩展属性。这提供了对 Mac 用户有用的功能，尤其是在处理历史遗留特性时。
  
• **推荐 Unison 工具**：mhw 认为 Unison 是一个不错的选择，它允许用户交互式地调整同步算法，并且能够存储文件的前一次运行状态，从而提高同步效率。Unison 提供了 GUI 和 TUI，适合在多台设备之间同步目录。

• **使用旧工具的经验**：lproven 提到了自己使用过的多个 rsync GUI 工具，包括 RSyncOSX 和 ARsync。这些工具各有优缺点，其中 ARsync 已经不再维护，而 RSyncOSX 也在不断更新。

• **偏好命令行工具**：dmarinus 偏好使用命令行工具，并开发了一个简单的 cli 前端 rzn，用于 rsync 和 rclone，类似于 git 的 pull/push 操作。

• **对安全性的关注**：w10-1 关注应用的安全性问题，尤其是 XPC 代码和应用的沙盒化问题，建议开发者总结如何识别和解决这些风险。

• **希望增加更多功能**：Bender 和 joshstrange 希望该工具能够支持更多的功能或前端集成，例如 LFTP 和 Rclone，从而扩展工具的应用场景。

• **跨平台需求**：MortyWaves 询问是否有好的 Windows 平台上的 rsync GUI，显示出对跨平台工具的需求。

• **UI 设计的批评**：nesarkvechnep 对 SwiftUI 应用的 UI 设计提出批评，认为表格和侧边栏的填充有问题，建议改进侧边栏的导航结构。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如 AnonC）提到在使用 rsync 时需要反复查阅手册或进行试错，以确定正确的参数，因此认为这些工具能提供更好的用户体验。
  
• 关于工具安装的讨论中，AnonC 建议在文档中加入通过 Macports 安装 rsync 的选项，而不仅仅通过 Homebrew。

• ctippett 提到了 Transmit 这一工具的同步功能，认为它也是一个不错的选择，尤其是在 SFTP/远程文件浏览场景下。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工具的安全性（w10-1 的评论）和 UI 设计（nesarkvechnep 的评论）上，部分用户对应用的实现细节和界面设计提出了质疑和改进建议。

This is the repository for RsyncUI, a SwiftUI based macOS application. RsyncUI is released for
macOS Sonoma and later
.
RsyncUI is a GUI on the Apple macOS platform for the command line tool
rsync
. It is
rsync
which executes
the synchronize data tasks. The GUI is
only

rsync
and make it easier to use
rsync
.

data.title: Car Physics for Games (2003)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了用于游戏中的汽车物理建模，重点是将纵向力和横向力分开处理。纵向力包括车轮驱动力、刹车力、滚动阻力和空气阻力，它们共同影响汽车的加速、减速和速度。空气阻力与速度的平方成正比，在高速时尤为显著；滚动阻力则与速度成正比，在低速时影响较大。总纵向力是这些力的矢量和，当汽车匀速行驶时，合力为零。

汽车的加速度由合力与质量通过牛顿第二定律计算，速度和位置通过加速度和时间的积分计算。利用这些力，可以准确模拟汽车的加速和最高速度，且最高速度自然由方程决定，无需额外设定。横向力则影响汽车的转向能力。文章还介绍了符号表示、单位以及数值积分方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏中车辆物理表现的发展及其技术探讨

不同观点：
• [gattilorenz] 认为 Timberwolf 的 YouTube 视频系列非常值得推荐，这些视频展示了游戏中车辆物理效果的发展历程，并提供了相关视频链接，帮助观众理解不同游戏如何实现车辆物理效果。

• [rypskar] 分享了个人经验，提到在2005年的学校项目中制作简单赛车游戏时，参考了相关文章，并发现由于动力不足，车辆在四档时的最高速度比五档高，这提供了实际游戏开发中的一个具体案例。

• [absurdo] 提到了飞行模拟类游戏的对比，引用了《Flights of Fantasy》一书，暗示车辆物理与飞行物理在模拟游戏中的类似发展和探讨。

• [sjezewski] 提供了另一个视频链接，暗示该视频与当前讨论相关，并幽默地提到自己因观看该视频而花费了大量时间，指出视频内容可能因现实中的速度设置而有所不同。

• [TacticalCoder] 分享了自己在八十年代的技术实践，通过录音和快速傅里叶变换分析车辆引擎声音以计算引擎转速，进而绘制扭矩曲线，并提到当时一些汽车厂商提供的技术手册包含详细的齿轮比和扭矩曲线信息，这为理解游戏中车辆物理提供了实际的技术背景。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体技术细节包括齿轮比、扭矩曲线、轮胎变形等，展示了车辆物理在游戏中实现的复杂性。
• [TacticalCoder] 的评论特别提到了历史背景，指出八十年代汽车厂商提供的技术资料对游戏开发和物理模拟的帮助，强调了实际数据对模拟准确性的重要性。
• 不同评论者提供的视频和文章链接展示了车辆物理效果从过去到现在的演变，为有兴趣的读者提供了丰富的参考资料。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并无明显争议，但[rypskar]的经验分享揭示了实际游戏开发中可能遇到的物理问题（如动力不足导致的速度异常），这与其他评论中对技术实现的理想化描述形成对比。

Car
Physics for Games
by
Marco Monster
Level:
Advanced
Abstract:
An introduction to car physics modelling for
games.
version 1.9
November, 2003
Introduction
This tutorial is about simulating cars in games, in other words
vehicle physics.
One of the key points in simplifying vehicle physics is to handle
the longtitudinal and lateral forces separately.  Longtitudinal
forces operate in the direction of the car body (or in the exact
opposite direction).  These are wheel force, braking force, rolling
resistance and drag (= airresistance).  Together these forces
control the acceleration or deceleration of the car and therefore the
speed of the car.  Lateral forces allow the car to turn.
These forces are caused by sideways friction on the wheels.  We'll
also have a look at the angular moment of the car and the torque caused
by lateral forces.
Notation and conventions
Vectors are shown in
bold,
we'll be using 2d vectors.  So the
notation
a
= -
b
would translate to the following code
snippet:
a.x = -b.x
a.y = -b.y
Throughout this tutorial I'll be assuming that the rear wheels
provide all the drive (for four wheel drives apply the neccesary
adaptations).
I'll be mainly using S.I. units (meters, kilograms, Newtons, etc.),
but I've included a handy conversion table at the end for those readers
more familiar with imperial measures (pounds, feet, miles, etc.)
Straight line physics
First let's consider a car driving in a straight line.  Which
forces are at play here?  First of all there's what the tractive
force, i.e. the force delivered by the engine via the rear wheels.
The engine turns the wheels forward (actually it applies a torque on the
wheel), the wheels push backwards on the road surface and, in reaction,
the road surface pushes back in a forward direction.  For now,
we'll just say that the tractive force is equivalent in magnitude to
the variable Engineforce, which is controlled directly by the user.
F
traction
=
u
*
Engineforce,
where
u
is a unit vector in the direction of
the car's heading.
If this were the only force, the car would accelerate to infinite
speeds.  Clearly, this is not the case in real life.  Enter
the resistance forces.  The first and usually the most important
one is air resistance, a.k.a. aerodynamic drag.  This force is so
important because it is proportional to the square of the velocity. When
we're driving fast (and which game doesn't involve high speeds?) this
becomes the most important resistance force.
F
drag
= - C
drag
*
v
* |v|
where C
drag
is a constant and
v
is
the velocity vector and the notation
|v|
refers to
the magnitude of vector
v
The magnitude of the velocity vector is more commonly known as the
speed. Note the difference of data type: speed is a scalar, velocity is
a vector. Use something like the following code:
speed =   sqrt(v.x*v.x + v.y*v.y);
fdrag.x = - Cdrag * v.x * speed;
fdrag.y = - Cdrag * v.y * speed;
Then there is the rolling resistance. This is caused by friction
between the rubber and road surface as the wheels roll along and
friction in the axles, etc.etc.. We'll approximate this with a force
that's proportional to the velocity using another constant.
F
rr
= - C
rr
*
v
where C
rr
is a constant and
v
is
the velocity vector.
At low speeds the rolling resistance is the main resistance force,
at high speeds the drag takes over in magnitude. At approx. 100 km/h (60
mph, 30 m/s) they are equal ([Zuvich]). This means C
rr
must be
approximately 30 times the value of C
drag
The total longtitudinal force is the vector sum of these three
forces.
F
long
=
F
traction
+
F
drag
+
F
rr
Note that if you're driving in a straight line the drag and rolling
resistance forces will be in the opposite direction from the traction
force.  So in terms of  magnitude, you're subtracting the
resistance force from the traction force.  When the car is cruising
at a constant speed the forces are in equilibrium and
F
long
is zero.
The acceleration (a) of the car (in meters per second squared) is
determined by the net force on the car (in Newton) and the car's mass M
(in kilogram) via Newton's second law:
a
=
F
/ M
The car's velocity (in meters per second) is determined by
integrating the acceleration over time.  This sounds more
complicated than it is, usually the following equation does the
trick.  This is known as the Euler method for numerical
integration.
v
=
v
+ dt *
a
,
where dt is the time increment in seconds between
subsequent calls of the physics engine.
The car's position is in turn determined by integrating the velocity
over time:
p
=
p
+ dt *
v
With these three forces we can simulate car acceleration fairly
accurately.  Together they also determine the top speed of the car
for a given engine power. There is no need to put a maximum speed

data.title: U.S. sanctions cloud provider 'Funnull' as top source of 'pig butchering' scams
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 美国财政部对位于菲律宾的Funnull Technology Inc.实施经济制裁，因其为涉及“杀猪盘”诈骗的数十万网站提供基础设施。这些诈骗通过诱骗受害者投资虚假加密货币平台，导致美国人损失超过2亿美元。Funnull还被发现与大量 scam网站有关，并通过美国云服务提供商传输恶意流量。中国籍管理人刘立志也被制裁。尽管亚马逊和微软承诺清理Funnull的恶意活动，但亚马逊仍未完全移除相关服务器。同时，欧洲联盟也于2025年5月对另一家涉及网络犯罪的ISP实施制裁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加密货币、诈骗、网络安全及相关法律和责任

不同观点：
• **naet**：认为加密货币的主要用途是投机和非法活动，如诈骗和犯罪。虽然加密货币使得国际转账更加便捷，但也让诈骗变得更加容易，且转账不可逆。
• **duxup**：通过朋友的经历说明了加密货币诈骗对个人的影响，提到一位亲友因网上恋爱而陷入加密货币骗局，难以劝阻。
• **infecto**：批评美国在处理诈骗和网络犯罪方面的执法不力，尤其是对企业的惩罚不足，导致老年人容易成为受害者。
• **mmooss**：提醒大家警惕政府在没有正当程序的情况下惩罚私营公司，认为即使是令人反感的公司也应享有正当程序，否则会为腐败和滥用权力提供机会。同时指出，处理跨国案件时可以通过外国政府或美国公司资源进行追踪。

补充讨论：
• **shoo**：分享了一个关于“杀猪盘”诈骗的播客系列，提到前三集免费，鼓励大家了解相关诈骗手段。
• **aziaziazi**：引用了国际刑警组织（INTERPOL）的建议，认为应停止使用“杀猪盘”一词，改用“恋爱诱骗”，以避免对受害者造成二次伤害，并鼓励受害者寻求帮助。
• **stevenwoo**：提到诈骗组织利用美国的AWS服务器来规避封锁，并分享了一个播客链接，该播客讲解了利用Tether加密货币进行“杀猪盘”诈骗的机制。
• **BLKNSLVR**：建议互联网服务提供商（ISP）提供增值安全服务，以过滤恶意活动，并分享了自己使用的防火墙规则和自动化阻止恶意IP地址的经验。还提到阻止新注册域名（RRDs）的可能性。
• **est**：指出一些不知名的网络服务提供商从事可疑业务，如为非法活动提供保护，例如2000年代的东亚地下市场。
• **billyhoffman**：提到一个名为“Funnull”的组织再次发动供应链攻击，认为该组织明知故犯，从事恶意活动。
• **ksenzee**：好奇未来老年人群体可能会遭遇的骗局类型，并表示会依靠聪明可靠的年轻人来帮助防范。

争议焦点：
• 加密货币的主要用途是否是投机和非法活动。
• 政府在打击网络犯罪中是否应采取更严厉的措施，以及如何在执法中平衡正当程序和效率。
• 如何有效防止和应对跨国网络诈骗，特别是在涉及外国个体和公司的情况下。

这些观点共同构成了关于加密货币、网络诈骗和网络安全的广泛讨论，涵盖了技术、法律和社会多个层面。

44132075.article_content:
Image: Shutterstock, ArtHead.
The U.S. government today imposed economic sanctions on
Funnull Technology Inc.
, a Philippines-based company that provides computer infrastructure for hundreds of thousands of websites involved in virtual currency investment scams known as “
pig butchering
.” In January 2025, KrebsOnSecurity detailed how Funnull was being used as a content delivery network that catered to cybercriminals seeking to route their traffic through U.S.-based cloud providers.
“Americans lose billions of dollars annually to these cyber scams, with revenues generated from these crimes rising to record levels in 2024,” reads
a statement
from the
U.S. Department of the Treasury
, which sanctioned Funnull and its 40-year-old Chinese administrator
Liu Lizhi
. “Funnull has directly facilitated several of these schemes, resulting in over $200 million in U.S. victim-reported losses.”
The Treasury Department said Funnull’s operations are linked to the majority of virtual currency investment scam websites reported to the FBI. The agency said Funnull directly facilitated pig butchering and other schemes that resulted in more than $200 million in financial losses by Americans.
Pig butchering is a rampant form of fraud wherein people are lured by flirtatious strangers online into investing in fraudulent cryptocurrency trading platforms. Victims are coached to invest more and more money into what appears to be an extremely profitable trading platform, only to find their money is gone when they wish to cash out.
The scammers often insist that investors pay additional “taxes” on their crypto “earnings” before they can see their invested funds again (spoiler: they never do), and a shocking number of people
have lost six figures or more through these pig butchering scams
.
KrebsOnSecurity’s
January story on Funnull
was based on research from the security firm
Silent Push
, which discovered in October 2024 that a vast number of domains hosted via Funnull were promoting gambling sites that bore the logo of the
Suncity Group
, a Chinese entity named in
a 2024 UN report
(PDF) for laundering millions of dollars for the North Korean state-sponsored hacking group
Lazarus
.
Silent Push found Funnull was a criminal content delivery network (CDN) that carried a great deal of traffic tied to scam websites, funneling the traffic through a dizzying chain of auto-generated domain names and U.S.-based cloud providers before redirecting to malicious or phishous websites. The FBI has released a
technical writeup
(PDF) of the infrastructure used to manage the malicious Funnull domains between October 2023 and April 2025.
A graphic from the FBI explaining how Funnull generated a slew of new domains on a regular basis and mapped them to Internet addresses on U.S. cloud providers.
Silent Push
revisited Funnull’s infrastructure
in January 2025 and found Funnull was still using many of the same
Amazon
and
Microsoft
cloud Internet addresses identified as malicious in its October report. Both Amazon and Microsoft pledged to rid their networks of Funnull’s presence following that story, but according to Silent Push’s
Zach Edwards
only one of those companies has followed through.
Edwards said Silent Push no longer sees Microsoft Internet addresses showing up in Funnull’s infrastructure, while Amazon continues to struggle with removing Funnull servers, including one that appears to have first materialized in 2023.
“Amazon is doing a terrible job — every day since they made those claims to you and us in our public blog they have had IPs still mapped to Funnull, including some that have stayed mapped for inexplicable periods of time,” Edwards said.
Amazon said its Amazon Web Services (AWS) hosting platform actively counters abuse attempts.
“We have stopped hundreds of attempts this year related to this group and we are looking into the information you shared earlier today,” reads a statement shared by Amazon. “If anyone suspects that AWS resources are being used for abusive activity, they can report it to AWS Trust & Safety using the report abuse form
here
.”
U.S. based cloud providers remain an attractive home base for cybercriminal organizations because many organizations will not be overly aggressive in blocking traffic from U.S.-based cloud networks, as doing so can result in blocking access to many legitimate web destinations that are also on that same shared network segment or host.
What’s more, funneling their bad traffic so that it appears to be coming out of U.S. cloud Internet providers allows cybercriminals to connect to websites from web addresses that are geographically close(r) to their targets and victims (to sidestep location-based security controls by your bank, for example).
Funnull is not the only cybercriminal infrastructure-as-a-service provider that was sanctioned this month: On May 20, 2025, the
European Union
imposed sanctions
on
Stark Industries Solutions
, an ISP that materialized at the start of Russia’s invasion of Ukrai

data.title: Practical SDR: Getting started with software-defined radio
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 《Practical SDR》是一本由David Clark和Paul Clark编写的指南，旨在帮助读者掌握软件定义无线电（SDR）的基础知识和实际应用。本书适合无线电爱好者、学生以及希望原型化RF设计的工程师。书中通过逐步指导构建虚拟无线电接收器，提取AM和FM信号音频，讲解幅度调制和信号滤波，以及处理复杂的IQ采样数据。读者将学习操作1 MHz到6 GHz的无线电频率，使用滤波器和增益控制提取清晰信号，选择合适的天线和RF硬件提升SDR性能，并设计自己的无线电发射器。本书理论与实践结合，涵盖GNU Radio使用、无线系统原理及实际项目，如需SDR硬件，建议使用HackRF One及兼容天线。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SDR（软件定义无线电）的使用、资源推荐及相关技术挑战

不同观点：
• _whiteCaps_ 警告说，SDR 可能会导致过度投入，例如为了进行特定的通信（如地球月亮地球反射通信）而购买昂贵的设备，提醒新手注意避免过度消费。
• 0xEF 强调了市场上存在许多劣质设备，建议新手在购买前仔细阅读指南，并提供了一个入门网站链接，帮助避免购买到不合适的设备或产生干扰的设备。
• net01 分享了个人使用 SDR 录制教授讲课内容的实际应用，认为 SDR 在某些情况下比手机或专用录音设备更好。
• darthcloud 推荐了一个免费的学习资源（pysdr.org），该资源侧重于数字信号处理的基础，并涵盖了流行的 SDR 硬件使用。
• ash-ali 对一本 SDR 相关书籍的内容和结构持怀疑态度，认为其内容可能不如 GNU Radio 的在线教程有价值，尤其是因为书中未包括对创建 Python Blocks 的详细介绍。

补充讨论：
• focusedone 提供了一个在线 SDR 地图链接，方便用户在等待实体设备时先进行在线体验。
• abhisek 提到在 Linux 系统上找到合适硬件的困难，这是 SDR 初学者可能面临的实际问题。
• Havoc 询问是否存在自动信号检测技术，以帮助识别频谱中的有效信号，尤其是廉价 SDR 设备接收窗口较窄的情况下。
• sorenjan 提供了一个具体应用案例，即 KrakenRF 用于查找无线电发射器，为 SDR 应用提供了新的视角。
• nickledave 推荐了一个新的 Python 库（sdr），认为其设计和开发非常出色。
• rsync 提到以前有一个针对树莓派的全功能启动镜像（pisdr-image），但该项目似乎已被废弃。
• Jimmc414 以幽默的方式提到通过 SDR 赚钱的可能性，引用了一个虚构角色 Russ Hanneman 的例子。
• rramdass 提供了 Michael Ossmann 的教程链接，该教程专注于 HackRF 和 SDR 的使用，是另一个推荐资源。
• JoeDaDude 提醒大家一本适用的教科书《Communication Systems Engineering with GNU Radio》，适用于使用 SDR 进行通信系统工程的用户。

争议焦点：
• ash-ali 对 SDR 相关书籍的内容价值提出质疑，尤其关注其是否涵盖了 GNU Radio 中最有价值的部分（如创建 Python Blocks）。

Contents
Download Chapter 4: Creating an AM Receiver
Look Inside!
Whether you’re a hobbyist interested in exploring the airwaves, a student learning about wireless communications, or an engineer looking to prototype RF designs,
Practical SDR
will help you master the fundamentals of software-defined radio.
You’ll build virtual radio receivers on your computer, then extract audio from real AM and FM signals; learn how amplitude modulation works by building an AM radio; understand signal filtering by crafting clean FM reception; and grasp complex topics like IQ sampling. You’ll use the intuitive GNU Radio Companion interface to create working radio systems piece by piece, then move on to building functional AM and FM receivers, and even design your own radio transmitter.
Along the way, you’ll learn how to:
•    Manipulate radio frequencies from 1 MHz to 6 GHz
•    Use filters and gain control to extract clear signals from noise
•    Maximize your SDR’s performance by choosing the right antennas and RF hardware
•    Process complex, real-time IQ data to demodulate actual radio signals
•    Build a flexible, virtual radio testing environment on your computer
This isn’t just another theory book.
Practical SDR
bridges the gap between basic tutorials and advanced applications, providing a solid foundation for diving into modern wireless systems like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular communications.
Some projects require SDR hardware, such as a HackRF One, and a compatible antenna.
Author Bio
David Clark
is an engineer interested in how things work, and enjoys sharing what he learns. He’s been working with radio technology since the late 1980s and was using SDRs before they were cool.
Paul Clark
is the owner and chief engineer at Factoria Labs, an organization dedicated to the propagation of software defined radio. He has experience ranging from chip design to firmware development to RF reverse engineering. He teaches classes and workshops on SDR in the U.S. and abroad.

data.title: Triangle splatting: radiance fields represented by triangles
data.author: ath92
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为"Triangle Splatting"的方法，用于实时渲染光辐射场（Radiance Field）。该方法通过使用三角形作为基本图元，结合可微渲染器，实现了高效的高质量新视角合成。与基于2D或3D高斯图元的方法相比，Triangle Splatting能够更好地保留锐利边缘和细节，避免模糊问题。该方法利用三角形的简单性和与标准图形硬件的兼容性，实现了高帧率渲染（如Garden场景中达到2400 FPS）。实验表明，Triangle Splatting在视觉 fidelity 和渲染速度上优于现有的非体积图元方法，并在Mip-NeRF360数据集上超过了Zip-NeRF的室内场景效果。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **rossant**：对使用Datoviz GPU渲染库渲染演示数据集表示满意，并计划将其加入官方画廊，认可该技术的视觉效果和速度。

• **jplusequalt**：对Gaussian splatting的用例和目标表示困惑，更熟悉传统3D图形，希望了解该技术的方向和解决的问题。

Triangle Splatting achieves high-quality novel view synthesis and fast rendering by representing scenes with triangles.
In contrast, the inherent softness of Gaussian primitives often leads to blurring and a loss of fine details, for example, beneath the bench or at the room’s door, whereas Triangle Splatting preserves sharp edges and accurately captures fine details.
Abstract
The field of computer graphics was revolutionized by models such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting, displacing triangles as the dominant representation for photogrammetry. In this paper, we argue for
a triangle come back.
. We develop a differentiable renderer that directly optimizes triangles via end-to-end gradients. We achieve this by rendering each triangle as differentiable splats, combining the efficiency of triangles with the adaptive density of representations based on independent primitives. Compared to popular 2D and 3D Gaussian Splatting methods, our approach achieves higher visual fidelity, faster convergence, and increased rendering throughput. On the Mip-NeRF360 dataset, our method outperforms concurrent non-volumetric primitives in visual fidelity and achieves higher perceptual quality than the state-of-the-art Zip-NeRF on indoor scenes.
Triangles are
simple
,
compatible
with standard graphics stacks and GPU hardware, and
highly efficient
: for the Garden scene, we achieve over 2,400 FPS at 1280×720 resolution using an off-the-shelf mesh renderer. These results highlight the efficiency and effectiveness of triangle-based representations for high-quality novel view synthesis. Triangles bring us closer to mesh-based optimization by combining classical computer graphics with modern differentiable rendering frameworks.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Methodology
Our rendering pipeline uses
3D triangles
as primitives, each defined by three learnable 3D vertices, color, opacity, and a smoothness parameter \( \sigma \). The triangles are projected onto the image plane using a standard pinhole camera model with known intrinsics and extrinsics.
Instead of binary masks, we introduce a
smooth window function
that softly modulates the triangle's influence across pixels. This function is derived from the 2D
signed distance field (SDF)
of the triangle, which measures the distance from a pixel \( \mathbf{p} \) to the triangle’s edges.
The signed distance field \( \phi(\mathbf{p}) \) is defined as the maximum of three half-plane distances:
\( \phi(\mathbf{p}) = \max\left( L_1(\mathbf{p}),\; L_2(\mathbf{p}),\; L_3(\mathbf{p}) \right) \)
where each half-space function is defined as:
\( L_i(\mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{n}_i \cdot \mathbf{p} + d_i \)
with \( \mathbf{n}_i \) denoting the outward-facing unit normal of the \( i \)-th edge, and \( d_i \) its signed offset from the origin.
The final
window function
is:
\( I(\mathbf{p}) = \text{ReLU}\left( \frac{\phi(\mathbf{p})}{\phi(\mathbf{s})} \right)^\sigma \)
where \( \mathbf{s} \) is the triangle’s incenter, i.e., the point where \( \phi \) is minimized. This function satisfies:
Maximum opacity at the triangle incenter
Zero influence at and beyond the triangle boundary
Adjustable sharpness via the parameter \( \sigma \)
The figure above illustrates how the window function behaves in 1D and 2D. As \( \sigma \to 0 \), the function approximates a binary triangle mask. As \( \sigma \) increases, the transition becomes smoother, and in the limit \( \sigma \to \infty \), it becomes a delta function centered at \( \mathbf{s} \).
To render an image, we accumulate contributions from all projected triangles using
alpha blending
in
front-to-back depth order
. Since all steps are differentiable, we can optimize the triangle parameters using gradient-based learning.

Triangle Splatting produces sharper and more detailed images. Notably, it renders the flowers and the background with greater realism and captures finer details compared to 3DGS or 3DCS. (If the videos appear out of sync, please reload the page to ensure proper alignment.)

data.title: The radix 2^51 trick (2017)
data.author: blobcode
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在现代CPU上加速大整数加减运算的方法。传统的手算加法从最低位开始，逐位相加并处理进位，这种方法类似于我们通常的编程实现。然而，由于进位依赖于前一位的计算结果，这种方法难以并行化，导致在现代CPU上的效率较低。

现代CPU可以通过并行执行多个简单的加法指令（如`add`）来提高性能，但处理进位的`adc`指令更为复杂且依赖前一个指令的结果，导致无法并行执行，性能下降。

文章进一步探讨了通过避免进位来提升性能的可能性，提出了类似于“无进位加法”的方法，这种方法在理论上可以通过预处理数字来减少对进位的依赖，从而提升并行计算的效率。

最终，通过重新设计算法以减少或消除进位依赖，可以在现代CPU上显著加速大整数的加减运算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用AVX和相关技术优化加法运算以及处理进位的不同方法和观点

不同观点：
• [ashdnazg] 认为使用AVX512和AVX2可以高效实现256位加法，并且能够将更多数字装入寄存器。他提供了一段代码示例，展示了如何通过掩码操作处理进位，并指出这种方法在512位加法中效果更显著。
• [addaon] 质疑为何不将最高位设置为64位而是52位，并建议通过分配更多位数给高位，可以积累更多加法操作，从而优化性能。他还提到这样做可以利用指令集的某些特性进行对齐和分割。
• [e4m2] 提出使用ADX指令可以在某些现代x86 CPU上获得更快的速度，尤其是在处理传统上使用2^51表示法有优势的情况下，例如Curve25519。
• [nine_k] 强调更多的独立操作可能会更快，因为它们可以并行执行，而较少的操作如果因为数据依赖性必须串行执行可能会更慢。这个观点具有更广泛的适用性。
• [smcin] 批评文章标题具有点击诱饵性质，认为标题应该更准确地反映内容，比如应突出该技巧仅适用于某些x86架构，并且是为了解决进位问题以避免流水线减速。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了一些相关的讨论链接，包括2022年11月和2020年5月的讨论，提供了更多背景信息。
• [hdjrudni] 分享了自己在处理缓冲区编码和解码时的经验，通过留出一些未使用的位来处理进位，从而在计算上节省了资源。
• [brucehoult] 指出在x86_64上工作的人证明了RISC-V省略进位标志是正确的。
• [eru] 提到“基数技巧”也适用于数据结构，并引用了Okasaki的书《Purely Functional Data Structures》中的例子。
• [Dwedit] 误以为2^51是关于将整数存储到双精度浮点数中，但后来澄清在此情境下应为2^53-1。
• [t0010q] 提到无进位二进制加法是异或操作，而带有进位的子集和问题是NP完全的，这揭示了进位对并行化的影响。
• [foota] 询问C/C++编译器是否可以合法地实现这种优化。
• [russdill] 对adc指令在现代CPU上是否必然比add指令慢表示怀疑，但承认文章的重点是数据依赖性。
• [alwahi] 询问如何将这种方法应用于大数乘法。

争议焦点：
• 关于如何分配最高位的位数以优化性能存在不同看法，[addaon] 建议64位而[ashdnazg] 使用了52位。
• 点击诱饵标题引发了[smcin] 的不满，他认为标题应该更准确地反映内容。

总结：讨论主要围绕使用AVX指令优化加法运算、处理进位的不同方法以及这些技巧在不同架构和情境下的适用性展开。同时，也涉及到了编译器优化和标题准确性的问题。

When implementing addition for large integers (e.g. 2

Interestingly, thereâs a straightforward trick that can speed up this

But first, a question: why do we start long addition with the âonesâ?
Why not start on the left?
The answer, of course, is the carries.
We canât figure out for sure what a given digit of the answer will be
until weâve completed all of the additions to the right of that digit.
Imagine if we tried to add left-to-right instead:
6 + 3 = 9. So the first digit is 9.
8 + 4 = 12. OK, the second digit is 2â¦ but carry a 1, so the first digit
was actually 9 + 1 = 10â¦ now carry back
that
1â¦
For mental math, this isnât too bad (and some people actually prefer it
when working with small enough numbers).
As an algorithm, however, this approach has some fundamental limitations that
become clear when working with larger numbers.
Most importantly, because the later parts of the computation rely on
information from the earlier parts of the computation,
itâs hard to split up and parallelize the work.
What about computers?
Computers donât work in base 10, of course.
Instead, modern desktop and server CPUs expose an interface for operating on
(for the most part) 64-bit integers.

The second reason is more interesting.
Letâs look at the Intel Haswell microarchitecture as an example.
On a Haswell CPU, a single

However, in ideal conditions, Haswell CPUs can execute up to 4

How is this possible? Parallelism.
Modern processors look ahead at what instructions are coming up and try to

The processor has no choice but to execute the instructions serially, one after

vpaddq

• [e4m2] 提出使用ADX指令可以在某些现代x86 CPU上获得更快的速度，尤其是在处理传统上使用2^51表示法有优势的情况下，例如Curve25519。
• [nine_k] 强调更多的独立操作可能会更快，因为它们可以并行执行，而较少的操作如果因为数据依赖性必须串行执行可能会更慢。这个观点具有更广泛的适用性。
• [smcin] 批评文章标题具有点击诱饵性质，认为标题应该更准确地反映内容，比如应突出该技巧仅适用于某些x86架构，并且是为了解决进位问题以避免流水线减速。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了一些相关的讨论链接，包括2022年11月和2020年5月的讨论，提供了更多背景信息。
• [hdjrudni] 分享了自己在处理缓冲区编码和解码时的经验，通过留出一些未使用的位来处理进位，从而在计算上节省了资源。
• [brucehoult] 指出在x86_64上工作的人证明了RISC-V省略进位标志是正确的。
• [eru] 提到“基数技巧”也适用于数据结构，并引用了Okasaki的书《Purely Functional Data Structures》中的例子。
• [Dwedit] 误以为2^51是关于将整数存储到双精度浮点数中，但后来澄清在此情境下应为2^53-1。
• [t0010q] 提到无进位二进制加法是异或操作，而带有进位的子集和问题是NP完全的，这揭示了进位对并行化的影响。
• [foota] 询问C/C++编译器是否可以合法地实现这种优化。
• [russdill] 对adc指令在现代CPU上是否必然比add指令慢表示怀疑，但承认文章的重点是数据依赖性。
• [alwahi] 询问如何将这种方法应用于大数乘法。

争议焦点：
• 关于如何分配最高位的位数以优化性能存在不同看法，[addaon] 建议64位而[ashdnazg] 使用了52位。
• 点击诱饵标题引发了[smcin] 的不满，他认为标题应该更准确地反映内容。

总结：讨论主要围绕使用AVX指令优化加法运算、处理进位的不同方法以及这些技巧在不同架构和情境下的适用性展开。同时，也涉及到了编译器优化和标题准确性的问题。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由Mathias Bynens创建的GitHub项目，该项目收集了多种编程、脚本和标记语言的最小有效文件。这些文件都是各自类型中语法上有效的最小可能文件，涵盖了从压缩档案、音频、文档、可执行文件到图形和各种编程语言的示例。项目起始于一篇关于最小HTML/XHTML文件的博客文章，并欢迎用户提交拉取请求。作者放弃了这些作品的版权，以便尽可能广泛地分享和使用。项目中包含的文件类型多样，例如：bzip2、gzip、MP3、PDF、HTML、PNG、EXE、SWF等。

data.title: Show HN: templUI – The UI Kit for templ (CLI-based, like shadcn/UI)
data.author: axadrn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用不同前端技术栈（如Datastar、HTMX、Templ、Tempo等）的开发体验和工具易用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [pst] 认为使用Fiber、Templ和Datastar让前后端保持一致性，总体满意，但指出Datastar试图同时处理AlpineJS和HTMX的功能，导致组件功能重叠。他还提到将Tailwind UI组件转换为Tempo耗时较多，并表示Datastar目前仍处于实验阶段，其信号概念不完全适用于Kubernetes风格的API资源。不过，Datastar在处理服务器发送事件（SSE）方面表现出色，总体上更偏好hypermedia而非React。

• [crowdyriver] 更偏好daisyui，认为其易用性高，只需在HTML中添加两行代码即可使用，非常适合原型设计。虽然其JS大小超过100kb，但后续可以优化。相比之下，他认为像shadcn/ui这样的库不如daisyui简洁。

• [andrewingram] 提到在查找Templ的相关信息时遇到困难，认为项目文档中缺乏对Templ实际构建内容或目的的明确说明。

• [ale] 认为"HTMX支持"的概念没有实际意义，因为HTMX是一个可以嵌入的库，任何HTML文件都可以“支持”HTMX。

• [ipsum2] 对Templ（在Go中的JSX）项目的受欢迎程度表示惊讶，并询问其使用场景。

• [preisschild] 提到曾使用过Templui的图标，但自从这些包变为内部包且需要安装自己的CLI进行依赖管理后，就不再更新了，表达了对这种变更的不满。

• [avithedev] 对整个技术方案表示赞赏。

• [lyu07282] 提到Checkbox/Radio Card在移动端上无法正常工作，指出其兼容性问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于Datastar的争议焦点在于其功能的冗余性（同时处理AlpineJS和HTMX的功能）以及其在处理Kubernetes API资源时的局限性。
• 不同开发者对UI库的偏好不同，有的偏好daisyui的简洁（如[crowdyriver]），有的则可能更喜欢其他库的功能（如[pst]对Templ的偏好）。
• 项目文档和工具链的变更（如[preisschild]提到Templui的依赖管理变更）对开发者体验有直接影响。
• 部分开发者（如[andrewingram]和[ipsum2]）对某些项目（如Templ）的定义和用途感到困惑，表明项目文档可能需要改进。
• 移动端兼容性问题（如[lyu07282]提到的情况）也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

data.title: Radio Astronomy Software Defined Radio (Rasdr)
data.author: zeristor

data.title: On eval in dynamic languages generally and in Racket specifically (2011)
data.author: swatson741
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了动态语言中的`eval`函数，它看似强大，但有经验的程序员通常避免使用，因其不当使用会引发问题。作者通过一个比喻解释了`eval`的本质：一种是直接给出明确指令（如将画布涂成红色），另一种是让其他人执行包含指令的句子。前者可被编译和优化，而后者类似于`eval`，无法很好地编译且执行结果依赖于环境。`eval`在某些情况下是必要且有用的，例如当指令来自外部（如施工经理），但多数情况下应避免，因其使程序更难理解和优化。关键在于区分何时真正需要动态执行代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言中 `eval` 函数的差异及其使用场景，特别是 Lisp 语言中的 `eval` 特性及其相关讨论。

不同观点：
• **taeric 的观点**：Lisp 中的 `eval` 与大多数其他语言的 `eval` 不同，它接受的不是字符串，而是代码即数据（code is data）的理念。这使得 Lisp 的 `eval` 可以带来一些显著的差异，尤其是在元编程（metaprogramming）方面。他通过个人探索展示了这一特性。

• **neilv 的观点**：反对新手在未充分理解的情况下滥用 `eval`。他指出，许多新手在阅读学术教材后会立即尝试使用 `eval`，而往往这是不合适的。他还提到，在 Racket 社区中，他曾尝试 discourage 误用 `eval`。他认为 `eval` 应作为最后的、危险的工具来使用，且在教学中应尽量延后介绍。

• **kazinator 的观点**：认为 `eval` 不应被阉割，主张保留完整的语言功能。他提出可以通过多种方式对 `eval` 进行沙盒化，包括验证代码和在限制环境中执行代码。他还强调，不应让 `eval` 的功能因为安全问题而被削弱。

• **programLyrique 的观点**：通过引用学术文章，展示了 `eval` 在其他语言（如 JavaScript 和 R）中的使用情况，提供了一些背景信息和实例，但没有深入展开讨论。

• **behnamoh 的观点**：提出了 Lisp 的强大宏系统是否源于能够用 Lisp 自身实现 `eval` 函数的问题。他认为 Lisp 通过少量原语和特殊形式构建了 `eval` 函数，并通过此机制扩展出新的语法规则，这与 Lisp 宏系统有相似的核心思想。

• **TOGoS 的观点**：总结了 `eval` 函数在不同层次上的语义定义。他认为，`eval` 的语义定义越复杂，其行为就越不明确。他将 JavaScript 的 `eval` 视为不明确的一端，Lisp 宏则处于中间，而经过解析和编译的 lambda 表达式则处于定义明确的另一端。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是 `eval` 的使用场景及其潜在的危险性。neilv 强调新手容易误用 `eval`，而 kazinator 则认为应通过沙盒化等手段来安全地使用 `eval`，而不是简单地避免使用。
• 另一个讨论点是 Lisp 的 `eval` 与宏系统的关系，behnamoh 和 TOGoS 提供了对 Lisp 元编程能力的深入理解，并探讨了 `eval` 在其中扮演的关键角色。
• 不同语言中 `eval` 的实现和使用差异也被提及，如 JavaScript 和 R 中的 `eval`，提供了跨语言的比较视角。

通过这些观点，可以看出 `eval` 函数在不同语言和场景中的复杂性和潜在问题，以及 Lisp 在元编程方面的独特优势。

44120480.article_content:
18 Oct 2011
posted by Matthew Flatt
The
eval
function is at the heart of a dynamic language, and it strikes many newcomers as an amazingly powerful tool. At the same time, experienced programmers avoid
eval
, because unnecessary use creates trouble. It’s not easy to explain why
eval
should be avoided or when it"s appropriate to use
eval
, but I’ll take another stab at it here.
What is
eval
?
Consider the following “program” in English prose:
Assume that your favorite color is red. Now imagine a balloon that is  your favorite color. Paint a canvas the same color as the balloon.
As English goes, that’s a fairly clear program with a fairly well-defined result. When I follow those instructions, at least, I will always produce a red canvas (assuming that I have a canvas and some red paint, but a potential lack of art supplies is not the point here).
I would come up with a red canvas even if I read the instructions when surrounded by people who speak only Chinese, obviously, since I’m the one reading the instructions. Furthermore, it would be straightforward to translate the program to Chinese, and then a person who reads Chinese would produce a red canvas.
A translator might even take the liberty of simplifying the program to just
Paint a canvas red.
The translation loses some of the poetry of the original, but the result is the same.
In Racket terms, the paragraph corresponds to a module. It can be compiled (i.e., translated) and optimized (i.e., simplified). A program can be made up of multiple modules that are written in different languages, but since each module can be reliably translated, they can all be compiled into some common language to run the program.
Here’s a different program:
Tell the person next to you “Assume that your favorite color is red.” Tell the person “Now, imagine a balloon that is your favorite color.” Tell the person “Paint canvas the same color as the balloon.”
Getting a red canvas back may be a little trickier in this case. If the person next to me speaks only Chinese, then my program may fail with a message-not-understood error.
If I want to translate the program to Chinese, then it’s not clear whether the parts in quotes should be translated. Maybe I mean for a person who can read Chinese but only sound out English to run the program when surrounded by English speakers, or maybe I mean for a Chinese person to run the program when surrounded by Chinese people. Either way, I have to be a lot more specific to a translator. For more complex programs, the instructions to the translator can become complex and fragile.
Finally, a translator probably won’t feel comfortable simplifying the program to
Tell the person next to you “Paint a canvas red.”
because there could be all sorts of environmental conditions that make the result different—such as people who are willing to paint but unwilling to accept assumptions about their favorite colors.
The paragraph with “tell the person…” is a program that uses
eval
. It can’t be compiled and optimized as well as the earlier paragraph, and the language context in which it is run may change the result. The quotes around sentences correspond to the quote in front of an expression passed to
eval
in Racket; there’s no particular reason that the language for
eval
will match the language of the program that has the quoted text. The issues become even more complex if you try to implement different parts of the program in different languages.
If the analogy to multiple spoken languages seems strange—maybe your language is Javascript, period—the problem of translation to another language is really a proxy for program understanding. There’s a direct connection to performance and optimization (i.e., translation to efficient machine code), but using
eval
also makes a program more difficult to understand for the same reasons that it makes the program more difficult to translate. For example, a reader of your program may not be able to tell whether “assume your favorite color is red” is just a rhetorical device to get to a red canvas or whether some new instructions will arrive that will ask for your favorite color.
When is
eval
Good?
The program with “tell the person next to you” above uses
eval
in a bad way. The task could just as well be performed by the person reading the instructions, instead of getting another nearby person involved.
Some other uses
eval
are both good and necessary. For example, consider the following program:
Ask the construction manager for instructions. Walk to the building  site and convey those instructions to the construction crew.
This program uses
eval
when it conveys instructions to the construction crew, but no quoted forms appear in the program. The absence of quoted code is one sign that
eval
may be appropriate. Note that the program could work no matter what language the manager and crew speak, although there is an implicit (and sometimes non-trivial) assumption that the manager and crew speak the same language.

data.title: Show HN: W++ – A Python-style scripting language for .NET with NuGet support
data.author: sinisterMage
data.article_summary: W++ 是一个实验性、过度设计的编程语言，旨在教育、娱乐和制造 meme。它由 Ofek Bickel 创建，具有异步lambda、伪OOPSIE原则（有时不优秀的面向对象编程），并与自定义VSCode扩展完全集成。该项目包含完整的C#解释器、语法解析器、支持async/await、lambda表达式、控制流结构等功能，还提供了语法高亮和代码片段。尽管在VSCode市场获得超过33,000次下载后被下架，项目源码现已公开，并采用MIT许可证。W++ 的存在旨在通过构建真实语言来传授编程技能，即使是玩笑性质的语言。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个新语言项目的技术实现、语法设计及其与Python和C#等语言的比较

不同观点：
• bob1029认为在.NET环境下，更倾向于使用内部DSL（领域特定语言）方式，如通过C#构建流畅接口（fluent interfaces）和方法如`ConfigureDomainServices(Action<DomainBuilder>)`。他认为这种方法在处理现代web服务器配置和复杂数据转换时表现良好，并分享了自己在IronPython项目中的经验教训，如内存泄漏问题。
• csto12质疑该项目的原创性，暗示项目可能是由LLM（大型语言模型）生成的，并认为这使得项目显得奇怪。
• osigurdson则探讨了未来是否可能通过LLM生成新语言的编译器、LSP（语言服务器协议）以及常见库，并认为这可能是语言开发的未来趋势。
• zerkten关注脚本语言启动速度和JIT（即时编译）延迟问题，并建议去除分号以避免与Python的直接比较，同时指出针对不同开发者群体（C#或Python）的语法偏好应更明确。
• e-master分享了自己从C#转向F#的经历，表达了对C#语法中使用大括号和分号的反感，倾向于使用像F#和Python那样的基于缩进的语法。
• gabrielsroka认为该语言更像JavaScript而非Python，并对README中未明确说明这一点表示疑惑。
• pansa2同样质疑“Python风格语法”的描述，指出语法文件显示出更多JavaScript和类C语言的影响。
• noworriesnate对项目表示兴趣，并询问数据流分析的实现情况，表示自己有兴趣参与贡献。
• actuallyalys对“像Python”的描述感到困惑，指出变量声明、对象创建和lambda语法都与Python不同，建议提供更明确的示例。
• frabert提到Boo语言与该项目有相似之处，提供了一个参考案例。
• jarrell_mark表示无法接受分号作为语法的一部分，个人不会使用这种语言。
• giancarlostoro对项目名称提出建议，认为“W++”容易引起误解，建议使用与Python相关的名字如“Cobra”以更好传达项目特点。
• airstrike则简单提到IronPython，暗示其已经实现了“在.NET上运行Python”的需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括该项目的原创性以及其语法描述的准确性。部分开发者认为项目描述不准确，尤其是与Python的比较，引起了混淆。
• 另一个讨论点是关于语法设计，尤其是分号和大括号的使用，一些开发者倾向于更像Python的缩进为基础的语法。
• 项目名称和其与LLM生成内容的关系也是讨论的重点，部分开发者对项目名称和可能的LLM生成背景持保留意见。

W++ 🦥
At least we’re better than Visual Basic.
W++
is a fun, experimental, and completely over-engineered programming language designed for learning, chaos, and memes.
It includes async lambdas, pseudo-OOPSIE principles (Object-Oriented Programming Sometimes Isn’t Excellent), and full integration with a custom-built VSCode extension.
This repo contains the full source code of W++ after it reached over
33,000 downloads
on the VSCode Marketplace — and was mysteriously flagged and removed.
✨ Features
✅ Full tokenizer, parser, and interpreter written in C#
✅ Async/await support
✅ Lambda expressions (single and multi-param)
✅ Control flow:
if
,
else
,
while
,
for
,
switch
✅ Try/catch +
throw
and
return
✅ Custom syntax highlighting and snippets in VSCode
✅ The
OOPSIE
model of development (trust us, it’s revolutionary)
🧠 Why does W++ exist?
This project was created by
Ofek Bickel
as an educational challenge — to build a real, working language from scratch and share it with the world.
We believe that even joke languages can teach serious skills.
🧪 Example
wpp
let greet = (name) => {
print "Hello, " + name;
};
greet("world");
📁 Project Structure
WPlusPlus/ — Core C# interpreter and AST
IngotCLI/ — CLI wrapper for testing/running .wpp scripts
wpp-vscode/ — VSCode extension with:
Syntax highlighting
Snippets
Icon & metadata
📜 License
This project is licensed under the MIT License.
Sloth-powered and chaos-approved.
🙏 A Note to Reviewers
This source code is now public and fully open.
If there were any issues leading to its takedown, feel free to open a GitHub issue or contact the author. We're happy to clarify and work toward reinstatement.

data.title: Systems Correctness Practices at Amazon Web Services
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary: 亚马逊云服务（AWS）通过形式化方法确保其系统的高可靠性、安全性和正确性。AWS主要使用TLA+语言进行形式化验证，帮助在开发早期发现和消除潜在缺陷，并支持激进的性能优化。然而，由于TLA+学习曲线陡峭，AWS引入了P编程语言，这是一种基于状态机的语言，更易于开发者使用，尤其适合建模和验证分布式系统。P已被应用于AWS的多项核心服务，如S3存储的强一致性迁移。P帮助开发团队在早期发现设计缺陷，并确保优化后的系统正确性。2023年，AWS推出了PObserve工具，用于在测试和生产中验证系统正确性，进一步提升了服务可靠性。通过结合形式化和半形式化方法，AWS在确保系统正确性的同时加快了开发速度，并提升了服务性价比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：分布式系统测试方法及工具

不同观点：
• **amazingamazing**：支持在单线程模拟器上进行确定性模拟测试，认为通过控制随机性（如线程调度、时间、消息传递顺序）来测试特定失败或成功场景是有效的。同时提到目前没有发现开源的、语言无关的工具库，但认为这种方法是可行的。此外，对AI在测试中的潜在应用持乐观态度，希望AI能推动软件工程的严谨性。

• **simonw**：赞赏AWS的S3系统，特别是其在强一致性读写方面的工程成就，认为这是令人难以置信的软件工程案例。

• **osigurdson**：质疑TDD（测试驱动开发）的有效性，认为其缺乏形式化基础，并将之与“宗教”类比，批评其在实际应用中的局限性。

• **furkansahin**：支持在基础设施控制平面中使用状态机，但对使用P语言的必要性表示怀疑，指出Ruby在其实践中同样效果良好。

• **severusdd**：关注系统中潜在的、不易察觉的失败（如“无害”的重试泄漏状态），认为应投入更多工程时间处理这些隐性问题。

• **chubot**：对P语言的历史及应用感兴趣，特别是其在微软和Windows USB栈中的使用情况，并质疑其在生产代码生成中的当前应用状态。

• **ctkhn**：对TLA+和P语言的实用性表示怀疑，认为缺乏具体示例使其看起来像额外的负担，除非有好的设计和测试流程支持。

• **EGreg**：赞赏TLA+和PlusCal的创建者Leslie Lamport，认为这些工具在分布式系统设计中至关重要，特别是在大型系统中验证正确性。

• **abeppu**：质疑将运行时监控视为“半形式化方法”的合理性，认为与其他方法（如基于属性的测试和模糊测试）相比，运行时监控似乎不太符合这一类别。

• **purpleidea**：对TLA+等工具的可接近性表示关注，认为C#作为实现语言可能不够友好，建议使用golang或java来吸引更多开发者。

• **ahalbert4**：询问FIS（故障注入服务）在实际分布式服务中的使用经验，表示正在考虑使用但缺乏实际案例。

• **sylware**：对AWS的网络安全措施表示担忧，质疑其是否拥有足够的反应性安全团队来应对潜在威胁。

• **Marazan**：比较Promela和SPIN与文章中描述的方法，认为前者可能更高级。

• **sebstefan**：对文章中描述的确定性模拟测试方法表示高度赞赏，认为这是一种令人惊叹的实践。

• **mlhpdx**：强调文章中的关键统计数据，即92%的灾难性失败是由非致命错误的错误处理引发的，呼吁更好地处理失败情况。

补充讨论：
- 讨论涉及多个工具和语言的比较与选择，如TLA+、P语言、C#、Ruby、golang和java，反映出对工具链和语言选择的关注。
- 对AI在测试中的潜在应用有期待，认为AI可能推动软件工程的严谨性和形式验证的可行性。
- 关注隐性系统失败和安全措施，强调在系统设计和测试中应更加重视这些不易察觉的问题。

Amazon Web Services (AWS) strives to deliver reliable services that customers can trust completely. This requires maintaining the highest standards of security, durability, integrity, and availability—with systems correctness serving as the cornerstone for achieving these priorities. An April 2015 article published in
Communications of the ACM
, titled “How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods,” highlighted the approach for ensuring the correctness of critical services that have since become among the most widely used by AWS customers.
21
Central to this approach was TLA+,
14
a formal specification language developed by Leslie Lamport. Our experience at AWS with TLA+ revealed two significant advantages of applying formal methods in practice. First, we could identify and eliminate subtle bugs early in development—bugs that would have eluded traditional approaches such as testing. Second, we gained the deep understanding and confidence needed to implement aggressive performance optimizations while maintaining systems correctness.
Moreover, 15 years ago, AWS’s software testing practice relied primarily on build-time unit testing, often against mocks, and limited deployment-time integration testing. Since then, we have significantly evolved our correctness practices, integrating both formal and semi-formal approaches into the development process. As AWS has grown, formal methods have become increasingly valuable—not only for ensuring correctness but also for performance improvements, particularly in verifying the correctness of both low- and high-level optimizations. This systematic approach toward systems correctness has become a force multiplier at AWS’s scale, enabling faster development cycles through improved developer velocity while delivering more cost-effective services to customers.
This article surveys the portfolio of formal methods used across AWS to deliver complex services with high confidence in its correctness. We consider an umbrella definition of formal methods that encompasses these rigorous techniques—from traditional formal approaches (such as theorem proving,
7
,
10
deductive verification,
18
and model checking
8
,
14
) to more lightweight semi-formal approaches (such as property-based testing,
6
,
19
fuzzing,
9
and runtime monitoring
11
).
The P Programming Language
As the use of formal methods was expanded beyond the initial teams at AWS in the early 2010s, we discovered that many engineers struggled to learn and become productive with TLA+. This difficulty seemed to stem from TLA+’s defining feature: It is a high-level, abstract language that more closely resembles mathematics than the imperative programming languages most developers are familiar with. While this mathematical nature is a significant strength of TLA+, and we continue to agree with Lamport’s views on the benefits of mathematical thinking,
15
we also sought a language that would allow us to model check (and later prove) key aspects of systems design while being more approachable to programmers.
We found this balance in the P programming language.
8
P is a state-machine-based language for modeling and analysis of distributed systems. Using P, developers model their system designs as communicating state machines, a mental model familiar to Amazon’s developer population—most of whom develop systems based on microservices and service-oriented architectures (SOAs). P has been developed at AWS since 2019 and is maintained as a strategic open source project.
22
Teams across AWS that build some of its flagship products—from storage (for example, Amazon S3, EBS), to databases (for example, Amazon DynamoDB, MemoryDB, Aurora), to compute (for example, EC2, IoT)—have been using P to reason about the correctness of their system designs.
For example, P was used in migrating Simple Storage Service (S3) from eventual to strong read-after-write consistency.
1
A key component of S3 is its index subsystem, an object metadata store that enables fast data lookups. To achieve strong consistency, the S3 team had to make several nontrivial changes to the S3 index protocol stack.
25
Because these changes were difficult to get right at S3 scale, and the team wanted to deliver strong consistency with high confidence in correctness, they used P to formally model and validate the protocol design. P helped eliminate several design-level bugs early in the development process and allowed the team to deliver risky optimizations with confidence, as they could be validated using model checking.

data.title: Automated Verification of Monotonic Data Structure Traversals in C
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种自动化验证工具Shrinker，用于验证C语言中单调数据结构遍历（MDSTs）的正确性。MDSTs是指那些在数据结构中单调迭代的操作，如`strlen`函数和二叉搜索树插入操作。Shrinker采用了一种名为“替罪羊大小下降”（scapegoating size descent）的程序分析策略，利用了MDSTs在处理大输入和其缩减版本（如删除第一个元素的列表）时产生相似轨迹的特点。实验表明，Shrinker在验证字符串和列表遍历方面比其他先进工具更有效，并通过包含上百个实例的新 benchmark 集验证了Linux、NetBSD、OpenBSD、QEMU、Git和Musl等主要C代码库中的数十个MDSTs的正确性、等价性和内存安全性。

Computer Science > Programming Languages

Title:
Automated Verification of Monotonic Data Structure Traversals in C
Authors:
Matthew Sotoudeh
View a PDF of the paper titled Automated Verification of Monotonic Data Structure Traversals in C, by Matthew Sotoudeh
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Bespoke data structure operations are common in real-world C code. We identify one common subclass, monotonic data structure traversals (MDSTs), that iterate monotonically through the structure. For example, strlen iterates from start to end of a character array until a null byte is found, and a binary search tree insert iterates from the tree root towards a leaf. We describe a new automated verification tool, Shrinker, to verify MDSTs written in C. Shrinker uses a new program analysis strategy called scapegoating size descent, which is designed to take advantage of the fact that many MDSTs produce very similar traces when executed on an input (e.g., some large list) as when executed on a 'shrunk' version of the input (e.g., the same list but with its first element deleted). We introduce a new benchmark set containing over one hundred instances proving correctness, equivalence, and memory safety properties of dozens of MDSTs found in major C codebases including Linux, NetBSD, OpenBSD, QEMU, Git, and Musl. Shrinker significantly increases the number of monotonic string and list traversals that can be verified vs. a portfolio of state-of-the-art tools.

data.title: De Bruijn notation, and why it's useful
data.author: blueberry87
data.article_summary:
De Bruijn索引和层级是一种用于解决lambda演算中变量捕获问题的命名方案。传统变量替换可能导致内部变量意外捕获外部同名变量，而De Bruijn索引通过使用自然数来表示变量绑定的深度，避免了这一问题。具体来说，索引0表示最近的绑定，1表示次近的绑定，以此类推。当进行变量替换时，通过增加自由变量索引来避免新绑定器的干扰。

De Bruijn层级类似，但数字越小表示绑定越早。索引方案更“本地化”，适合创建新绑定器，而层级方案在移动绑定器时更方便，因为无需修改自由变量。

此外，De Bruijn表示法简化了项的比较，消除了α-等价（变量重命名）的复杂性，使两个功能相同的项可以直接比较。

总结：
- **De Bruijn索引**：数字表示绑定深度，避免捕获问题。
- **De Bruijn层级**：数字表示绑定顺序，移动绑定时更方便。
- **优点**：简化项比较，避免α-等价问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：De Bruijn 索引在 λ 演算中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• tromp：De Bruijn 表示法的一个优势是它能提供非常简单的二进制 λ 项编码，这在国际模糊C代码大赛（IOCCC）的提交中得到了展示。

• marvinborner：De Bruijn 索引使得书写大型 λ 项更快、更直观，尤其是在纯索引的 λ 演算中。此外，使用这些索引的语言似乎对大型语言模型（LLMs）有免疫力，因为它们依赖内部栈/图结构而非仅文本简化。
• kccqzy：质疑是否可以在解析器层面解决变量命名冲突问题，通过让解析器维护一个环境栈来避免后续过程中的命名冲突。

• matheist：提到 Faust 编译器内部使用 De Bruijn 索引来重用计算，询问其他例子。

• De Bruijn 索引的优点包括简化编码、避免变量命名冲突、提高书写和理解大型 λ 项的效率。
• 争议焦点在于是否可以通过解析器层面的处理来避免复杂的 De Bruijn 索引机制，以及使用全局唯一变量名是否是更实际的解决方案。
• 不同用户分享了 De Bruijn 索引在具体项目和工具中的应用实例，如 Faust 编译器和 Plumb 语言。

44137439.article_summary:
De Bruijn索引和层级是一种用于解决lambda演算中变量捕获问题的命名方案。传统变量替换可能导致内部变量意外捕获外部同名变量，而De Bruijn索引通过使用自然数来表示变量绑定的深度，避免了这一问题。具体来说，索引0表示最近的绑定，1表示次近的绑定，以此类推。当进行变量替换时，通过增加自由变量索引来避免新绑定器的干扰。

De Bruijn层级类似，但数字越小表示绑定越早。索引方案更“本地化”，适合创建新绑定器，而层级方案在移动绑定器时更方便，因为无需修改自由变量。

此外，De Bruijn表示法简化了项的比较，消除了α-等价（变量重命名）的复杂性，使两个功能相同的项可以直接比较。

总结：
- **De Bruijn索引**：数字表示绑定深度，避免捕获问题。
- **De Bruijn层级**：数字表示绑定顺序，移动绑定时更方便。
- **优点**：简化项比较，避免α-等价问题。

data.title: Beating Google's kernelCTF PoW using AVX512
data.author: anematode
data.article_summary: 2025年5月，Timothy Herchen及其团队Crusaders of Rust发现了Linux包调度器中的一个释放后使用（use-after-free）漏洞，并开发了相关利用。他们的目标是向Google的kernelCTF提交该漏洞以获取5.1万美元的奖金。然而，提交过程竞争激烈，需在限定时间内完成一系列步骤，包括解决工作量证明（proof of work）和运行漏洞获取标志。由于专业团队的优化，某些队伍能以极快速度提交。Herchen的团队怀疑这些队伍使用了现场可编程门阵列（FPGA）来加速计算。Herchen受队友请求，试图优化团队的工作量证明速度。该证明采用一种名为“sloth”的延迟函数（VDF），其计算是序列化的，无法通过增加核心数来加速。最终，Herchen的团队成功在竞争中胜出，赢得了奖金。

44137715.article_content:
Authors
Name
Timothy Herchen
Twitter
Introduction
In May 2025, my
Crusaders of Rust
teammates William Liu (
FizzBuzz101
) and Savy Dicanosa (
Syst3mFailure
) discovered and developed an exploit of a use-after-free bug in Linux's packet scheduler.
The bugfix patch
contains additional details. William found this bug while fuzzing Linux for his master's thesis, which I will link here upon its publication. (Congratulations, William!)
They wanted to submit the bug to Google's
kernelCTF
competition for an anticipated $51,000 bounty.
1
Unfortunately, finding the bug and writing the exploit was only the first part of the battle. This post documents my small but unique contribution to our ultimately winning the bounty.
Setting the stage
To avoid paying out lots of money, kernelCTF organizers limit the number of submissions eligible for a bounty. Every two weeks at noon UTC, the submission window opens. Only the first team who is able to connect to and exploit the server, and submit the flag to a Google Form, receives a payout; any subsequent submissions are marked as duplicates. Furthermore, to prevent excessive submissions, the connecting to kernelCTF server requires solving a "proof of work"—a function which, by design, takes a few seconds to evaluate.
In summary,
the submission process has these steps
:
At 12:00:00 UTC, connect to the kernelCTF server.
Solve the proof of work, which takes roughly 4 seconds.
Wait for the instance to boot. (Roughly 2.5 seconds.)
Upload the exploit and run it to secure the flag. (Time elapsed depends on the exploit. Savy optimized this one to take roughly 0.55 seconds without sacrificing reliability. Wow!)
Submit the flag to a Google Form. The submission timestamp determines the winner of the "slot".
Our goal was to complete all these steps in sequence, faster than all the other teams.
Enter the sweats
Because of the large bounties, over time professional vulnerability research teams have aggressively optimized their submission process. For the May 2, 2025, submission window preceding ours, the first team to submit the flag
did so 4.5 seconds after noon
!
The numbers don't seem to add up: even assuming an instant exploit and form submission, the VM boot time and proof of work already take 6.5 seconds. Looking closer, we see that the time at which the winning submission's flag was generated (highlighted in red) is one second
before
noon UTC. Yet, the timestamp is generated
after
the proof of work is solved. Did sweaty CTFers invent time travel?
Alas! Because of a rounding quirk in the kernelCTF server code (
here
), the VM instance actually boots at 11:59:59—so no time travel. Still, the timestamp indicates that the winning team solved the proof of work in less than a second! How could this be?
We don't know for certain, but one kernelCTF organizer postulated that they were using
field-programmable gate arrays
(FPGAs). FPGAs are custom silicon that can perform specific tasks extremely quickly, to the exclusion of general-purpose tasks. They are not only fairly expensive, but also tricky to program. If the professional team had access to an FPGA programmed to perform the proof of work, a sub-second proof of work time was conceivable.
On May 13, William messaged me on Discord seeking advice on how to optimize the proof of work so that we could preempt the competition. I had to act fast: The next submission window would open at 5 a.m. PST, May 16.
2
The proof of work: The "sloth" VDF
The proof of work (
implemented here
) is a certain
verifiable delay function
(VDF) known as "sloth". VDFs are cryptographic primitives which prove that a nontrivial amount of time has passed by requiring a long, serial computation. This computation outputs a proof which can be (relatively) quickly verified. Because the computation is serial, scaling to more computational resources (such as more CPU or GPU cores) does not reduce the runtime.
3
The sloth VDF was introduced by
Lenstra and Wesolowski (2015)
. I won't reproduce the number theory behind sloth (see page 4 of the paper for that), but to summarize matters, the function we must optimize boils down to:

where

Google's reference implementation uses gmpy, which is a Python binding to the venerable
GNU Multiprecision Library
(GMP). GMP's addition and multiplication kernels are handwritten in assembly for each target platform (
example
). The loop-carried dependency of
x

主要讨论点：Markdown编辑器及其相关工具的应用与开发

不同观点：
• [thangalin] 支持使用 KeenWrite，这是一个基于 CommonMark 的免费开源 Markdown 编辑器，能够调用 R 函数，并通过 knitr 语法嵌入 CSV 文件内容，创建“活”文档。他认为这种方法可以使数据的变化直接反映在输出文档中。

• [its_down_again] 分享了自己开发的 Streamlit 应用，该应用将 Excel 追踪器中的内容提取为 Markdown wikis，以便于矢量数据库的摄入。他提到目前可以通过 UI 选择本地文件的 QA 部分，但尚未解决如何持久化设置以重复运行的问题，并寻求其他人的建议。

• [iaad] 提供了技术建议，指出可以通过捕获粘贴事件中的 HTML 内容来保留 Excel 的多列单元格格式，并建议使用 DOMParser 进行解析。

• [jamesgill] 推荐了两个工具：一个 VS Code 插件和 markdowntools，认为这些工具可以很好地完成相关任务。

• [speakspokespok] 提出了功能请求，希望能够将 Google Sheets 数据直接转换为 Mermaid.js 图表或 PNG 格式的 Markdown 表格，以便在演示中插入表格图片。

• [haberdasher] 推荐使用 Table Capture 工具，可以从 HTML 表格转换为 Markdown。

• [ornel] 分享了自己多年前开发的工具版本，该工具受 MailChimp 启发，能够将表格内容转换为 Markdown 和简单文本，特别适用于发送表格数据的纯文本邮件。

• [jquaint] 询问是否有适用于 Linux 的命令行解决方案。

By
Ruth Emery
last updated
21 May 2025
in
Features
Marks & Spencer has warned that its online services will continue to be disrupted until July following last month's cyberattack.
Shoppers have not been able to place orders on the M&S website or app since 25 April, and it had been unclear when online orders would resume.
Today, as part of the retailer’s financial results that confirmed an
estimated £300 million hit to its 2025/26 operating profit
as a result of the attack, M&S revealed that customers would not be able to order via its website or app for the next few months.

"We expect online disruption to continue throughout June and into July as we restart, then ramp up operations," said M&S.
Shares in M&S, one of the
most popular stocks
in the UK, have fallen more than 10% over the past month.
M&S's problems began over the Easter weekend, with customers unable to use contactless payments, gift cards or scan their M&S Sparks loyalty card. The company confirmed it was dealing with a
"cyber incident"
and although those services have resumed, on 25 April, it stopped taking online orders.
The high-street giant later revealed that some customer data, including contact details and dates of birth, was also stolen during the hack.
M&S says the personal information taken could include online order histories, but no useable payment or card details, or account passwords, were stolen.
Martyn James, a consumer expert, says the “ongoing problems show just how dangerous
cyberattacks
can be”, and that the empty shelves and suspension of online orders will be hugely damaging to
M&S’s profits
.
Bank of America estimates that M&S has lost £40 million in sales every week since the attack began.
We look at what’s happening with online orders, what customers should do, and whether it’s still worth investing in M&S.
When will M&S start taking online orders again?
On 12 May,
MoneyWeek
asked M&S when it would start accepting online orders again. We were told there was no update on this, and that customers can still browse the website and put items in their online basket, they just can’t check out at the moment.
Online orders have been suspended since 25 April. On 2 May, M&S put out a note on its
social media channels
saying it was “working day and night to manage the current cyber incident and get things back to normal for you as quickly as possible”.
The retailer has now said that the “online disruption” will continue during June and July. Customers can expect a gradual return to normal.
Stuart Machin, chief executive of M&S, commented on 21 May about the cyberattack: “It has been challenging, but it is a moment in time, and we are now focused on recovery, with the aim of exiting this period a much stronger business.
“There is no change to our strategy and our longer-term plans to reshape M&S for growth and, if anything, the incident allows us to accelerate the pace of change as we draw a line and move on.”
In addition, Sparks offers have been suspended; M&S says “they will be back shortly and shared in the normal way”.
What customer data has been taken and what should I do?
M&S has written to all customers that it has email addresses for, informing them that some personal data has been taken.
This could include their name, date of birth, telephone number, home address, household information, email address and online order history.
M&S said in an update on 13 May: “Importantly, there is no evidence that this data has been shared and it does not include useable card or payment details, or account passwords, so there is no need for customers to take any action.”
However, it added that for “extra peace of mind”, customers will be prompted to reset their password the next time they visit or log onto their M&S.com account on the website or app.
Jayne Wall, operations director at M&S, said in an email to customers: “You might receive emails, calls or texts claiming to be from M&S when they are not, so do be cautious.
“Remember that we will never contact you and ask you to provide us with personal account information, like usernames, and we will never ask you to give us your password.”
‘I’ve been impacted by the M&S problems. What are my rights?’
M&S says customers should get in touch with customer service if they have a query or complaint. The customer service number is 0333 014 8555, or you can visit the
help and support webpage
.
You can also send a message to
M&S’s X account
.

data.title: Vrs: Personal Software Runtime inspired by Emacs, Plan 9, Erlang, Hypermedia
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
**vrs** 是一个个人软件运行时环境，受 Emacs、Erlang、Unix、Plan 9 和超媒体系统的启发，旨在打造一个从编程语言、执行环境到工具链的全方位软件开发平台。其核心原则包括 joy（愉悦）、uniformity（统一性）、simplicity（简洁性）、practicality（实用性）和 interactivity（交互性）。目前该项目仍在开发初期，具有实验性质，包含不稳定性。

**结构**：
- **lyric**：嵌入式 Lisp 方言及虚拟机。
- **vrsd**：作为系统守护进程的运行时实现。
- **libvrs**：运行时和客户端共享的库。
- **vrsctl**：基于 libvrs 的轻量级 CLI 客户端。
- **vrsjmp**：GUI 启动栏客户端。

**Lyric 语言示例**：
- 使用 `def` 定义变量，`set` 更新变量。
- 支持基本数据类型如整数、列表、关键词和布尔值。
- 函数声明使用 `defn`，支持高阶函数和条件操作。
- 进程以绿色线程运行，支持非阻塞 I/O 和多核调度。

**状态**：项目仍在建设中，存在不完善之处。

不同观点：
• [leoshimo] 作为作者，介绍了 "vrs" 项目的目标和灵感来源。该项目是一个个人编程运行时环境，旨在创造一个让作者感到愉悦的计算环境，灵感来自于 Emacs、Erlang、Unix、Plan 9 和 Hypermedia 等系统，并结合了这些系统的强大思想。项目在 Recurse Center 构建。

• [superdisk] 表示自己也一直在收集关于“梦想语言”和运行时的想法，认为 "vrs" 项目与自己的想法有很多相似之处，并对项目表示赞赏。

In the multiverse, you can live up to your ultimate potential. We discovered a
way to temporarily link your consciousness to another version of yourself,
accessing all of their memories and skills.
It's called verse jumping.
— Alpha Waymond
What is this?
vrs
is a personal software runtime - an
opinionated take on my own "endgame" software platform.
It considers every aspect of programming - language, execution, environment,
editing, tooling, and more - designing across the end-to-end process of building
software.
Its inspirations are Emacs, Erlang, Unix, Plan 9, and Hypermedia systems.  It
hopes to combine powerful ideas from those projects into one cohesive whole for
an empowering, joyful, holistic programming experience.
The key principles are: joy, uniformity, simplicity, practicality, and
interactivity.
Status
🚧 Under heavy construction
🐉 Here be dragons
vrs is a sandbox project, focused on play and experimentation in a pure-fun,
pure-utility environment. While I live-on vrs everyday, the platform is very
volatile in both concepts and implementation.
This software has rough edges
. Be warned!
Structure
lyric
: Embedded Lisp Dialect and Virtual Machine
vrsd
: A runtime implementation as a system daemon
libvrs
: The
vrs
library crate shared by runtime and client implementations
vrsctl
: A thin CLI client over
libvrs
vrsjmp
: A GUI launch bar client
A Tour of VRS
Introduction to Lyric
The runtime runs software written in Lyric lang:
# Use `def` to define new bindings
# e.g. "hello lyric!" string to symbol `msg`
(def msg "hello lyric!")
# Update bindings with `set`
(set msg "goodbye lyric!")
# Basic Primitives - integers, lists, keywords, and more
42                                # integers
:my_keyword                       # keywords start with colon (:)
true                              # booleans are `true` or `false`
(list msg var_number var_keyword) # create new lists with `list` function
'("a" "b" "c")                    # quote expression with '
# Function declarationes use `defn`
# Lyric is expression-oriented - last form is returned as value to caller
(defn double (x)
(+ x x))
# Call functions by using bound symbol names within parens, followed by arguments
(double 10) # => 20
# List Operations
(def l '(1 2 3))
(def first (get l 0))       # get 0th item in `l`
(def last (get l -1))       # get last item in `l`
(contains? l 3)             # check if `l` contains `3`
# Association Lists
(def item '(:title "My Title" :subtitle "My Subtitle"))
(get item :title)      # => "My Title"
(get item :subtitle)   # => "My Subtitle"
# Functions (Lambdas) are first class
(defn apply (x fn)
(fn x))
(apply 41 (lambda (x) (+ x 1)))        # => 41
(map '(1 2 3) (lambda (x) (+ x x))     # => '(2, 4, 6)
# Conditionals with `if` - equality with `eq?`
(if (eq? msg "Hello")
"msg was hello"
"msg was not hello")
# and flip conditions with `not?`
(if (not? false)
"it was not true")
# Catch error with `try`. Introspect result with `err?` or `ok?`
(if (err? (try (not_a_function)))
"failed to call not_a_function")
# Pattern match with `match`. `_` is a wildcard pattern.
(def result '(:ok "Successful data"))
(match result
((:ok msg) msg)
((:err err) (:err err))
(_ '(:err "Unrecognized result")))
# Destructuring bindings can be used to pattern match against forms:
(def result '(:ok "Success"))
(def (:ok status) result)      # matches :ok, binds status to string "Success"
# As a Lisp, Lyric has `eval` and `read`:
(eval (read "(+ 40 2)")) # => 42
# and there are more builtins and symbols in environment, introspectable via `ls_env` and `help`
(ls_env)           # see all symbols defined in environment
(help recv)        # see documentation via `help`

processes

These processes are implemented as
green threads
,
and are lightweight compared to OS processes. Processes are scheduled on
multiple cores using nonblocking IO.
Each process has a single logical thread of execution. CPU-bound and IO-bound
work is transparent at process level, but the run

data.title: Toxic Origins, Toxic Decisions: Biases in CEO Selection
data.author: marojejian
data.article_summary: 本文研究了CEO选拔中的选择偏差如何放大风险承担行为。作者利用出生前接触污染这一外生冲击来衡量个人的风险偏好，发现出生于未来超级基金地点的CEO更有可能获得内部晋升。这些“超级基金CEO”在内部职位上表现出色，但在晋升后倾向于采取更冒险的外部政策，导致公司业绩波动更大且整体表现较弱。研究表明，企业在晋升决策中可能错误地将运气视为技能，从而筛选出高风险承担者，其特质在不可逆决策领域中显现出问题。简言之，超级基金CEO的业绩具有较低平均值但较高波动性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于污染区域（Superfund站点）与CEO特质之间相关性研究的评论和争议

不同观点：
• marojejian对研究结果持怀疑态度，认为相关性结果不可靠，但同时认为选择性偏差（幸运的风险承担者更易成为领导）可以解释一些不好的领导现象。他还提到，原标题虽然有诱导性，但更有效地传达了研究的结论，而新的标题则显得学术化且不够吸引人。
• m463引用了感官处理敏感度的概念，提出污染可能通过影响神经效率导致更多的风险承担行为，并引用了2015年的一项研究支持其观点。
• LarsDu88结合自身在硅谷的经历，提到谷歌园区位于一个超级基金站点上，并指出相关污染可能对健康有影响，暗示在研究中看到的相关性可能有实际依据，但同时也承认这种相关性不一定有因果关系。
• dcre对研究的大样本量表示惊讶，暗示这可能增加了研究的可信度。
• ashoeafoot使用比喻说明高风险承担的CEO对公司可能是致命的，但对更大环境或系统来说是有信息价值的，且低风险承担的CEO也有其存在的必要性。
• ada1981误解了研究，以为研究说的是出生在超级基金站点的人因环境毒素导致基因变化，从而更具风险性。
• CommenterPerson以讽刺的口吻评论，暗示对研究结果的不信任，认为在有毒废物上开发房地产可以造就更多CEO，暗指研究的荒谬性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是相关性与因果关系的区别，部分评论者质疑研究是否能证明污染直接导致更多风险承担的CEO出现。

Toxic Origins, Toxic Decisions: Biases in CEO Selection
HKU Jockey Club Enterprise Sustainability Global Research Institute Paper No. 2025/052
90 Pages
Posted: 27 May 2025
See all articles by P. Raghavendra Rau
P. Raghavendra Rau
University of Cambridge; European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI)
YiLin Wu
National Taiwan University - Department of Economics
Richard Lok-Si Ieong
City University of New York, Baruch College - Zicklin School of Business - Department of Economics and Finance
Date Written: May 01, 2025
Abstract
We examine how selection bias in CEO promotion amplifies risk-taking, using prenatal exposure to pollution as an exogenous shock to individual risk preferences. CEOs born in future Superfund sites are more likely to be promoted internally, suggesting firms reward observed success without recognizing underlying risk tolerance. These "Superfund CEOs" excel in internal roles but pursue riskier external policies once promoted-leading to greater volatility and weaker performance. Our results suggest firms may systematically mistake luck for skill in promotion decisions, filtering for high-variance risk-takers whose traits only become problematic when decision-making shifts to exposed, irreversible domains. In short, Superfund CEOs display performance with essentially lower mean but higher variance.

data.title: Adam Riess and the Hubble tension
data.author: samizdis
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了诺贝尔物理学奖得主亚当·里斯（Adam Riess）的科学贡献与心路历程。里斯在27岁时开始研究宇宙膨胀，并通过精确的观测发现了宇宙加速膨胀的现象，这导致了“暗能量”概念的提出。暗能量被认为是一种遍布宇宙的排斥力，推动星系彼此远离，最终可能导致宇宙陷入冷寂。尽管里斯帮助确立了被称为“宇宙学标准模型”的理论，但近年来他开始怀疑该模型的正确性。许多宇宙学家认为该模型可能需要被取代，因为暗物质和暗能量尚未被直接探测到，这表明现有理论仍存在重大缺失。里斯选择继续从事研究，而不是转向行政管理，以期解开宇宙的更多谜团。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对宇宙学研究中的一些关键问题和理论的讨论，特别是与Adam Riess的研究和超新星1a相关的争议。

不同观点：
• amai认为Adam Riess的研究及其获得的诺贝尔奖主要依赖于超新星1a作为标准烛光来测量宇宙距离。但如果超新星1a并非标准烛光，且其亮度变化范围更大，那么Riess等人的距离测量结果可能有误。amai认为这种情况的可能性高于其他替代理论，但Riess由于个人原因无法正视这一点。
• tshaddox对文章中将宇宙膨胀的发现归功于1998年Adam Riess的描述感到困惑，指出这是Edwin Hubble在1920年代的发现。
• hn_acc1解释了距离与宇宙膨胀速度的关系，认为更远的星系看起来更快是因为我们看到的是更早期的宇宙状态，而不是现在的状态。
• zvorygin建议记者询问领域内的顶尖科学家，在得知Hubble张力之前和之后，他们对标准模型正确性的看法，以便更清晰地了解情况。
• pavel_lishin对宇宙学研究感到兴奋，将其与19世纪和1930年代的科学突破相提并论。
• gaoshan将宇宙膨胀比作爆炸扩展，认为这可能是最接近的类比。
• jgalt212认为暗能量和暗物质像是“修补因素”，对其持怀疑态度。
• daedrdev提醒大家注意，尽管诺贝尔奖得主有很高的学术声望，但有些人也会有偏离主流科学观点的情况，因此不能完全依赖诺贝尔奖得主的观点。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了对超新星1a作为标准烛光的可靠性的质疑，这是讨论的核心争议点。
• 对宇宙膨胀的理解和描述存在不同解释，例如爆炸扩展的类比。
• 对科学研究中的权威性和怀疑态度的讨论，特别是诺贝尔奖得主的观点是否应被无条件接受。
• 对具体研究结果和测量方法的技术性讨论，例如距离与速度的关系。
• 对文章内容的技术性细节和表述方式的关注，如tshaddox对文章时间线的困惑。

这些观点反映了科学界内外的不同声音，既有对具体科学问题的深入探讨，也有对科学权威性和研究方法的反思。

dam Riess was 27 years old
when he began the work that earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics, and just 41 when he received it. Earlier this year, Riess, who is now in his early 50s, pulled a graph-paper notebook off a bookshelf in his office at Johns Hopkins University so that I could see the yellowing page on which he’d made his famous calculations. He told me how these pen scratches led to a new theory of the universe. And then he told me why he now thinks that theory might be wrong.
For nearly a century, astronomers have known that the universe is expanding, because the galaxies that we can see around us through telescopes are all rushing away. Riess studied how they moved. He very carefully measured the distance of each one from Earth, and when all the data came together, in 1998, the results surprised him. They were “shocking even,” he told his colleagues in a flustered email that he sent on the eve of his honeymoon. A striking relationship had emerged: The farther away that galaxies were, the faster they were receding. This “immediately suggested a profound conclusion,” he said in his Nobel Prize lecture. Something is causing the expansion of the universe to accelerate.
Riess’s genius lies in making precise observations, but the task of explaining the accelerating expansion that he discovered fell to theorists. They proposed the existence of dark energy: a faint, repulsive force that pervades all of empty space. The amount of dark energy that fits inside your bedroom, say, isn’t very strong. It won’t blow the walls out. But when dark energy’s power sums across truly cosmic volumes of space, it can drive galaxy clusters apart. And as this process puts more space between those galaxies, the repulsive force only strengthens, speeding up the expansion of the universe. Telescopes can see hundreds of billions of galaxies today, but trillions upon trillions of years from now, dark energy will have driven them all out of sight. Eventually, it will dilute every last bit of matter and energy into a cold equilibrium, a thin gruel of nothingness.
By doing the work that led to the discovery of dark energy, Riess had helped add the final piece to what has since come to be called the “standard model of cosmology.” Indeed, few people played a larger role in establishing the standard model as the field’s dominant theory of how the universe began, how it organized itself into galaxies, and how it will end. But in recent years, cosmologists, the people who study the universe on the largest scales of space and time, have begun to worry that this story, and particularly its final act, might be wrong. Some talk of revolution. A growing number now say that the standard model should be replaced.
Adam Riess is among them.
W
henever a big theory
of the universe is teetering, the old guard tends to close ranks; hence, the classic joke about science progressing one funeral at a time. Riess easily could have joined the old guard. He could have been its commanding officer. When he returned from Stockholm with his prize in 2011, he found that his academic life had changed. People around him started to behave oddly, he told me. Some clammed up. Others argued with him about trivial things, he said, perhaps so they could boast of having dunked on a Nobel laureate. Riess was besieged with invitations to sit on panels, give talks, and judge science fairs. He was asked to comment on political issues that he knew nothing about. He told me he was even recruited to run major scientific institutions.
Riess wondered about that path—being the big boss of a NASA mission or gliding around a leafy university as its chancellor. He could see the appeal, but he hated fundraising, and unlike other, older Nobel laureates, he said, Riess still felt that he had scientific contributions to make, not as an administrator, but as a frontline investigator of capital-
n
Nature. “Scientists sometimes tell themselves this myth:
I’ll go lead this thing, and then I’ll come back and do research
,” he told me. But then, by the time they’ve finished up with their administrative roles, they’ve lost touch with the data. They become clumsy with the latest software languages. “The science passes them by,” Riess said.
Riess decided to stick with research. There was plenty to do. The standard model had not solved cosmology. Even in 2011, people knew that the theory was lacking some important details. For one, 96 percent of the standard model’s universe is made up of dark energy and dark matter—and yet no scientist had ever detected either one directly. Cosmologists had good reasons to believe that both exist in some form, but any intuitions about how one might find either in the actual universe had not proved out. Something major seemed to be missing from the picture.

data.title: Show HN: Public transportation departure board
data.author: sschueller
data.article_summary: Station Display是一款显示瑞士公共交通时刻表的设备，具备实时数据更新功能，可显示当前站点的下次发车时间及延误信息。设备采用铝制外壳和染色有机玻璃，设计现代。其192 x 64像素的LED显示屏在日夜均清晰可见，并提供多种主题选择。设备支持壁挂或桌面摆放，可通过Android或iOS应用配置，并具备开放API供自定义数据源。需要2.4 GHz Wi-Fi和电源支持，适用于室内环境。
data.comments_summary:

data.title: Surprisingly fast AI-generated kernels we didn't mean to publish yet
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了意外生成的非常快速的AI生成CUDA内核，这些内核在某些情况下甚至超过了PyTorch中专家优化过的生产内核。关键结果包括：Matmul (FP32) 性能达到torch.matmul的101.3%；Conv2D性能达到torch.nn.Conv2D的179.9%；Softmax性能达到torch.softmax的111.8%；LayerNorm性能达到torch.nn.LayerNorm的484.4%；以及Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool的性能达到参考值的290.1%。这些内核是使用简单的合成数据生成方法意外获得的，该方法通过自然语言推理优化想法并行生成多个代码变体，从而避免了传统顺序修正中的局部最小问题。文章强调了这种方法在性能内核生成方面的潜力，并视为未来探索的第一步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理（AI agents）的运行模式、性能优化、LLM生成代码的实际效果及应用场景

不同观点：
• **AI代理的运行模式应被重新思考**：
  - [miki123211] 认为传统上人们对AI代理的理解类似于人类员工，限制了其并行处理能力。LLM可以无限生成代理，并行执行任务，类似于任务队列系统（如Celery）的工作方式。
  
• **性能优化的讨论**：
  - [ekelsen] 指出FP32在现代ML工作负载中不再常见，且未经过优化，因此通过FP32内核获得性能提升并不意外。真正的挑战在于优化常用的FP16和BF16内核。
  - [vessenes] 对实验方法表示兴趣，尤其是通过语言推理步骤来促进搜索的多样性，认为这种方法非常有趣且有效。
  
• **生成代码的有效性和应用**：
  - [FL33TW00D] 尝试复现结果时发现LayerNorm内核不够数值稳定，但随后生成了一个数值稳定的版本。
  - [bgwalter] 认为PyTorch代码库并非由性能专家编写，因此将其作为基准不合适。AI生成代码的过程仍需大量人工指导。
  - [poltomo] 提到自2018年以来，通过ML编译器优化内核已成为常见做法，应该将生成的内核与Apache TVM等编译器生成的内核进行比较。
  
• **LLM生成代码的本质**：
  - [klingenm] 认为LLM作为遗传算法中的一小步，利用其输出的随机性实现算法，而非完全由AI生成。
  
• **对AI生成内核的未来展望**：
  - [brrrrrm] 期待AI生成的代码能够处理更复杂的融合内核任务，如gemm + relu + gemm + norm组合，这类任务人工编写和调优非常繁琐。
  
• **LLM的潜力与局限**：
  - [adityamwagh] 将LLM视为一种“蜂巢思维”，认为其通过大量人类知识和上下文的压缩，具备了执行复杂任务的能力。
  - [userbinator] 调侃自己被标题误导，以为文章讨论的是AI生成操作系统内核。
  
补充讨论：
• **硬件选择的争议**：
  - [MangoToupe] 认为使用Nvidia L40S这样的企业级硬件不贴近消费者实际，建议使用消费者硬件进行测试。

争议焦点：
• **基准选择的合理性**：
  - [bgwalter] 认为PyTorch代码库并非性能优化的理想基准，应选择更具代表性的基准进行比较。

• **生成代码的实际优化效果**：
  - 部分评论者如[ekelsen]和[poltomo]对实验结果的实用性提出质疑，认为应在更常用的内核和硬件上进行测试。

• **AI生成方法的实际贡献**：
  - [klingenm] 认为生成代码的方法更接近于遗传算法，而非完全由AI生成，其实际贡献需进一步验证。

总体来看，讨论围绕AI代理的运行模式、性能优化的实际效果、生成代码的应用潜力以及LLM的未来发展方向展开。

44139454.article_content:
Surprisingly Fast AI-Generated Kernels We Didn’t Mean to Publish (Yet)
Authors:
Anne Ouyang and
Azalia Mirhoseini and
Percy Liang
TL;DR
We have some very fast AI-generated kernels in pure CUDA-C without using libraries and DSLs such as CUTLASS and Triton. They are performing close to or in some cases even beating the standard expert-optimized production kernels shipped in PyTorch. Some of our highlighted results:
Matmul (FP32): 101.3%
performance of FP32 torch.matmul; problem size: 4096x4096 square matrices
Conv2D: 179.9%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.Conv2D; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2)
Softmax: 111.8%
performance of FP32 torch.softmax; problem size: (4096, 65536) input tensor
LayerNorm: 484.4%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.LayerNorm; problem size: (16, 64, 256, 256) input tensor
Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool: 290.1%
performance of FP32 torch reference, 189.0% performance of FP32 torch.compile() reference; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2), maxpool(kernel_size=3, stride=2)
(Our results are benchmarked on an Nvidia L40S GPU, and % performance is defined as reference time divided by generated kernel time)
“Untiled” by DALL·E (2025). (Digital pigment on virtual canvas)
From the MMA collection
Intro
We started with the goal of generating synthetic data to train better kernel generation models. Somewhere along the way the unexpected happened: the test-time only synthetic data generation itself started producing
really
good kernels beating or performing close to human expert optimized PyTorch baselines, utilizing advanced optimizations and hardware features, which were previously thought to be challenging. As a result, we decided to write this blog post early and share our findings. The point of this blog post isn’t about a novel methodology; in fact, our synthetic data generation design is simple, and what’s surprising is that it is already showing promise.
In this post, we’re sharing the method, five optimized kernels (4 foundational ML operators + 1 fused kernel of an AlexNet block), an example optimization trajectory, and some takeaways and thoughts on what this might mean for performant kernel generation. Consider this a first step in what’s next.
Method
We’re using the
KernelBench
(a benchmark for AI based kernel generation that we released in December 2024) task setup: given torch code, the LLM writes custom kernels to replace the torch operators with the goal of getting a speedup. Consistent with the original KernelBench design, the reference code is in the default FP32, and given a tolerance threshold (1e-02), using lower precision solutions is valid. In addition, each problem in KernelBench has specific sizes since there are many size-specific optimizations, so the benchmark tests for the fastest kernel for the specific problem size, not necessarily a generally fast kernel for any arbitrary problem size. We run both the torch reference code and the generated code, and test for correctness by checking the numerical equality of the two outputs over many random inputs.
The most common way people scale test-time compute for this problem of optimizing kernels today is through sequential revision, a multi-turn loop where a model incrementally edits a kernel, checks for correctness and performance, then tries again based on the result, either fixing the kernel or try to improve its performance. This loop is intuitive and easy to implement. The model fixes broken kernels, tweaks working ones, and gradually climbs toward something faster.
The main limitation of this approach is the lack of optimization idea diversity. Sequential loops often fall into local minima, revisiting the same classes of transformations or endlessly refining unpromising trajectories. The result is inefficient use of test-time compute and little pressure on the model to generate fundamentally new optimization ideas.
We introduced two key changes to address this:
Reasoning in natural language about optimization ideas: rather than directly generating new kernels in each step, we generate optimization ideas in natural language conditioned on previously attempted ideas, and realize those ideas into new code variants.
Branching at each optimization step: instead of refining a single candidate per step, we fan out such that each idea spawns multiple implementations, and the highest-performing kernels are used to seed the next round (we also keep a bank of good existing kernels for seeding). This unlocks massive parallelism allowing us to explore radically different directions at each turn, rather than getting stuck in a narrow optimization path.
The result is a test-time loop that looks less like “chat with a compiler” in the case of sequential revision, and more like structured exploratory search, guided by explicit optimization hypotheses and aggressively parallel evaluation

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对文章中乐器内部图片的反应及相关技术、艺术性讨论

不同观点：
• [susam] 提议了一个小游戏：通过开发者工具隐藏文本，尝试猜测图片代表的乐器，并分享了自己的得分（5/8）。这个评论引发了对图片内容的关注。
• [izzydata] 对图片中乐器内部看起来很大的现象提出疑问，认为缺乏参照物导致对大小的误解。
• [pimlottc] 分享了更多照片的链接，将讨论引向照片的来源和摄影师的作品网站。
• [HarHarVeryFunny] 对乐器内部的不规则性提出疑问，认为这些不规则可能影响音色，并提出是否对称的设计会更好。
• [rwmj] 将乐器内部结构与船的甲板相比较，提供了视觉上的类比。
• [ErigmolCt] 认为照片看起来像外星建筑或反乌托邦城市，强调了照片的艺术冲击力。

补充讨论：
• [ubj] 表达了对照片的喜爱，并提议设计一个类似照片风格的音乐厅。
• [hinkley] 提出了一种技术性建议，讨论了拍摄乐器内部照片的设备和方法，提供了具体的操作步骤。
• [yard2010] 赞赏了照片的美感，同时批评了页面上的广告，形成了对比。
• [e40] 提到了对dpreview网站关闭的误解，并对网站的存续表示高兴。
• [gnabgib] 提到了之前类似的讨论和来源链接，提供了历史讨论的参考。
• [coreyp_1] 分享了自己购买过这些照片的经历，并表示可能会再次购买。
• [righthand] 幽默地提议拍摄手风琴或六角手风琴的内部照片，将讨论扩展到其他乐器。
• [sandspar] 表达了对昆虫视角的有趣感受，虽然与主要讨论点不完全相关，但增加了趣味性。
• [wilfredk] 表示看到乐器内部时可以“听到”音乐，强调了视觉与听觉的联觉感受。

争议焦点：
- 主要在[HarHarVeryFunny]提出的乐器内部不规则性是否影响音色，以及是否对称设计会更好。这引发了对乐器设计和音质关系的讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕乐器内部照片的视觉效果、技术拍摄手段及其艺术性和科学性展开，用户们分享了各自的猜测、技术建议和个人感受。

data.title: Irritation Is Inspiration
data.author: j4mehta
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了 irritability（易怒或易烦躁）作为发现问题和创造机会的工具，特别是在创业和产品开发中。作者指出，许多让他感到烦躁的小问题，如糟糕的设计、拼写错误或低质量的产品，实际上是市场中的“ gaps”或未被解决的问题。这些 irritations 可以成为创业者的“超能力”，因为它们指向了需要改进的地方。文章强调，发现问题是创造新事物的关键，许多成功的产品和项目正是源于对现状的不满和解决这些问题的动力。作者通过自身经历说明， irritation 是灵感来源，鼓励大家不要忽视这种感受，而是利用它来推动创新和变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人在日常生活、技术使用和工作流程中遇到的烦恼和如何处理这些烦恼

不同观点：
