• [CommenterPerson] 对有人为解决回复邮件问题而开发软件感到不满，特别是当该软件还存在明显的错误（如讲稿中的错别字）。这反映出对开发质量和细节关注的批评。

• [pedalpete] 提出了一种更深层次的反思，认为人们常常被社会中根深蒂固的问题所困扰，但往往意识不到这些问题的存在。他通过自身长期失眠的经历，强调找到真正烦恼的根源并采取行动的重要性，建议通过探索他人如何处理类似问题来寻找解决方案。

• [PaulHou]le 分享了一个与技术细节有关的烦恼，提到有人对他儿子在模拟器上玩游戏的显示比例错误表示不满，以及他自己在演讲中犯的Excel图表错误。这体现出技术细节错误或不完美可能引发不满和争议。

• [hinkley] 提出了一种应对烦恼的策略，即把烦恼当作信息来处理。建议在遇到烦恼时停下来思考，是否能绕过问题而不是直接面对，或者找到一劳永逸的解决方案。

• [Daisywh] 提到微小的用户体验（UX）问题（如不关闭的下拉菜单）会让她感到烦恼，但她也意识到这些烦恼可以转化为有用的产品创意，并通过记录这些烦恼形成产品改进的思路。

• [esilverman] 提到了“怨恨驱动开发”（spite driven development）的概念，暗示有些开发行为可能是出于对某些问题的不满或怨恨而产生的。

• [bobrobpr] 表示对阅读Hacker News上“愚蠢的评论”感到厌烦，认为这是一个充满负面内容的平台，并对人性表示失望。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是对AI生成内容的信任问题。chankstein38基于个人经验对AI的可靠性提出质疑，而其他人可能认为AI能提供便利和创新机会。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何有效处理日常生活中的小烦恼，有人选择记录并转化为创意，有人建议通过反思和寻找替代方案来解决问题。
• pedalpete的反思提供了一种更深层次的解决问题的方法，即通过自我反思和探索他人的经验来找到真正有效的解决方案。

总的来说，评论中反映了人们对技术问题、产品质量和日常生活中的小烦恼的不同态度和处理方法。

44139286.article_content:
Be irritable
Your frustration is not a flaw. It’s a radar. And if you're a builder, it might just be your greatest asset.
Little things bother me.
Bad font choices. Typos. Weirdly aligned pixels. Push handles for pull doors. Pull handles for push doors. Low contrast photos. Apps that ask for notification access or a review without having delivered any value. Low quality packaging. A buggy app. Sloppy writing. A slow app. I can go on.
The fact that so many things bother me
also
used to bother me. But having spent enough time building my own products, I’ve come to realize something:
My irritation is my superpower.
Why?
Because these irritations are gaps.
They’re glitches in the Matrix — eye-opening,
if
we’re willing to take the red pill and look through them.
They’re problems — some small, some big. Some aren’t worth solving. Others are unsolvable.
But they’re problems.
And my job as an entrepreneur is to find problems and solve them.
It sounds simple in theory, but practically it’s very difficult.
Most people think that
solving
the problem is the hard part. And sure, that has its challenges.
But what happens if you don’t
spot
the problem in the first place?
If the way things are — the status quo — doesn’t strike you as problematic, then how do you ever build toward the future?
It reminds me of one of my favourite stories from
David Foster Wallace’s famous speech, This is Water
:
Two fish were casually swimming downstream in a river.
Eventually they come across another fish, who’s whistling and travelling upstream against the current.
As he swims by, he smiles and says: “How’s the water, boys!” and continues past them.
A few moments pass. The two fish keep swimming in silence.
Eventually, one of them looks at the other and says:
“What the hell is water?
As a creator, builder, or thinker — if you accept reality as-is, it'll become impossible to create something new.
Irritation is your way out.
If something irritates you or surprises you, it likely represents an opportunity.
An opportunity to solve. To build. To create. To publish. To invent.
This has played out so many times in my own life:
It irritated me that I didn’t know enough about Indian history, despite those being my roots. All the existing podcasts were built for an Indian audience — none catered to Western second-generation immigrants. So I created an AI-powered podcast called
The Other Side
that does exactly this.
It irritated me that I had to manually reply to 20+ emails every day from reporters just to get some press for my startup. So I built
a software
to do it for me.
It irritated me that AI research was moving so fast, and my job relied on staying on top of it — but I had no system. So I built
a platform
to filter and curate new papers.
And the list goes on…
My current startup,
Swift
only exists because an irritated sports facility owner came to us, looking for help.
Irritation is inspiration.
Don’t let it go.

data.title: Jerry Lewis's "The Day the Clown Cried" discovered in Sweden after 53 years
data.author: danso
data.article_summary: 喜剧演员杰瑞·刘易斯（Jerry Lewis）1972年拍摄的争议性电影《The Day the Clown Cried》因未公开发行而被视为“遗失影片”。该片讲述了一名德国马戏团小丑因 mocking 希特勒被关入纳粹集中营，并被迫诱骗儿童走向死亡的故事。多年以来，人们认为该片没有完整版本存在。然而，瑞典演员Hans Crispin近日透露，他于1980年从制作公司的档案中秘密取走了一份完整的影片工作拷贝，并一直私下放映。Crispin表示他打算将此拷贝交给下一代，并希望通过修复使其公开。尽管刘易斯曾于2015年将部分影片素材捐赠给美国国会图书馆，并规定2024年6月前不得公开，但完整影片至今未见天日。Crispin的发现引发了关于该片是否应公之于众的讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一部有争议的电影作品《The Day the Clown Cried》的保存、传播和道德问题。

不同观点：
• al_borland 认为，这部电影应该卖给一个认真的制作人，要么恢复它，要么妥善保存，或者为了研究目的展示它。他质疑将电影锁起来不让人看的选项，并建议将电影上传到archive.org以供保存和研究。

• ilamont 分享了自己作为前35毫米放映员的经验，提到类似被私藏的电影胶片可能广泛存在，并描述了自己在工作中接触到的被不当保存的电影资料。
• ocschwar 指出这部电影可能受Janusz Korczak的故事启发，提供了相关的维基百科链接。
• autoexec 认为电影应该免费在线发布，以避免因金钱和贪婪再次失去它，并批评可能的AI“增强”版本和商业化操作。

• labrador 提到一个朋友在私人放映后情绪崩溃的经历，暗示电影可能具有强烈的情感冲击。
• iwanttocomment 提到这部电影在纪录片和媒体上仍有讨论，并对其持续受到关注表示惊讶。
• I-M-S 推荐了一个探讨文化谜团的播客，认为该电影是其中一个有趣的主题。
• jfengel 认为这部电影应该继续保持“丢失”状态，因为它听起来非常糟糕。
• neuroelectron 详细描述了电影的情节，并引用相关评论指出电影的错误和情感错位，以及导演的尴尬和不愿公开展示。

• DrNosferatu 和 NKosmatos 都表现出对电影泄露和公开传播的兴趣，甚至索要种子链接。
• legitster 指出这部电影从未真正“丢失”，原始素材已经捐赠给国会图书馆，并提到目前流传的是一个工作样片，而非最终版本。

补充讨论：
- 电影的保存和传播方式引发了关于私藏、商业化、在线公开和道德责任的广泛讨论。
- 有人担心电影可能因商业利益再次失去，并批评可能的AI“增强”版本。
- 评论中还提到了类似被时间锁定或私藏的电影案例，以及实际工作中电影资料的不当保存和传播问题。
- 部分评论表现出对电影内容和情节的强烈情感反应，暗示其可能具有较大的心理影响。

44139592.article_content:
One of cinema's most sought-after
lost films
has been discovered after having been kept secretly in the collection of a Swedish actor for 45 years.
Comedian
Jerry Lewis
's controversial holocaust film
The Day the Clown Cried,
shot in 1972 but never released, was thought to
not exist in finished form
.
But Hans Crispin, star of the beloved 1980s Swedish TV series
Angne & Svullo
, claims he stole a complete workprint of the film from the archives of its production studio in 1980 – and has been screening it for guests in his apartment ever since.
“I have the only copy,” Crispin told
Swedish state news broadcaster SVT.
“I stole it from Europafilm in 1980 and copied it to VHS in the attic where we copied other films at night.
“I've kept the copy in my bank vault,” Crispin added.
Swedish actor Hans Crispin has a complete workprint of The Day The Clown Cried, SVT has reported. AFP
Crispin recently screened a full copy to journalists from SVT and Sweden's
Icon
magazine to prove his claim was true.
“You're the 23rd and 24th people I've shown it to,” he told
Icon
and SVT.
The actor also revealed that his initial copy was missing the opening six-minute sequence of the film shot in Paris, which was mailed to him anonymously in 1990, along with a note saying that the sender knew he possessed a copy of the rest of the film.
Will The Day The Clown Cried be released to the public?
Now that he has come out into the open, Crispin intends to make his copy available for the world to see, saying: “It must be seen!”
Crispin added: “I think I want to hand it over to the next generation. With today's technique, it can be restored. I want to sell it to a serious producer who either restores it or keeps it locked away, or restores it and shows it to people for studying purposes.”
The film tells the story of a German circus clown who is imprisoned in a Nazi concentration camp for mocking
Adolf Hitler
and is then forced to lure children to their deaths as punishment.
The footage that Lewis possessed of the Day The Clown Cried was donated to the Library of Congress in 2015. AFP
Lewis, who directed and starred in the film as clown Helmut Doork, donated five hours of footage to the US Library of Congress in 2015, adding a stipulation that it not be made available until June 2024.
The footage, which has been made available to scholars, was screened last August for
The New Republic
journalist Benjamin Charles Germain Lee, who reported that the footage was fragmentary and does not constitute a complete film, leading the industry to conclude that the full film did not exist.
Why the film was never released
While there were myriad alleged issues during the shoot itself, problems reportedly arose between Lewis and producer Nat Wachsberger once filming stopped, which is considered the main catalyst for the film's shelving.
Lewis was reportedly unsatisfied with the film’s financing and announced that Wachsberger did not fulfil his financial obligations. Hearing this, Wachsberger threatened to sue Lewis for breach of contract, which resulted in a fallout between the two that caused Lewis to leave with a rough cut of the film, according to a 2018 feature in
The New York Times.
Lewis had mixed feelings about the film, showing fragments of his footage to close friends. However, in his 1982 autobiography, Lewis said “the picture must be seen”.
No complete copy of The Day The Clown Cried has ever been confirmed to exist until now. AFP
After watching it,
The Simpsons
voice actor Harry Shearer said it was “a perfect object”, adding: “This movie is so drastically wrong, its pathos and its comedy are so wildly misplaced, that you could not, in your fantasy of what it might be like, improve on what it really is.”
In an interview with
The New York Times
in 2018, Chris Lewis, the comedian's son, said: “It was something that was very close to his heart.”
At other times, however, Lewis denounced the film. In 2013, footage of him surfaced on YouTube in which he stated: “It was bad, and it was bad because I lost the magic. No one will ever see it, because I'm embarrassed at the poor work.”
The history of lost films
The Day the Crown Cried
is an example of one of many films that were once thought lost or not fit for public screening.
Similar films include 1976’s
Chess of the Wind
by Iranian director
Mohammad Reza Aslani.
Until it was rediscovered in 2020, the film could only be watched on low-quality VHS tapes. Since then, it has been restored and screened around the world.
One of the best-known lost films is
The Passion of Joan of Arc
from 1928. After being lost for years, a copy was found in a Norwegian hospital in the 1980s. The film is now considered one of the most important historical film artefacts.
The Day The Clown Cried depicts a clown entertaining children during the holocaust. AFP
London After Midnight
, a 1927 horror film directed by Tod Browning starring Lon Chaney, is still a veritable white whale for fans after the last-known copy was destroyed in

data.author: storycraft
data.article_summary: Asdf Overlay 是一个高性能、易于使用的 Windows 游戏叠加库，支持多种渲染 API（如 OpenGL、DirectX 和 Vulkan），通过 GPU 共享纹理实现加速，避免了 CPU 上的帧缓冲复制，从而在任意大小下保持高效渲染。它支持多后端、输入捕获控制，并提供示例项目如游戏内浏览器和噪声矩形。该项目使用 Rust 开发，需要 node 和 pnpm 进行构建，并提供了详细的构建和运行说明。Asdf Overlay 采用双重许可：MIT 或 Apache-2.0。

Blazingly fast™ & Easy to use Windows Overlay library
Asdf Overlay provides an easy to use interface to draw on top of window framebuffer by hooking rendering backends
GPU shared texture was used to avoid framebuffer copy via CPU.

data.title: Show HN: Icepi Zero – The FPGA Raspberry Pi Zero Equivalent
data.author: Cyao
data.article_summary: Icepi Zero 是一款经济、便携的FPGA开发板，采用Raspberry Pi Zero外形设计，搭载Lattice ECP5 25F FPGA，具备强大的设计能力。它配有HDMI接口和三个USB-C端口，支持数字视频输出和多设备连接。该开发板适用于学生学习处理器内部结构、玩家模拟旧硬件以及程序员测试多架构代码。Icepi Zero 还具有板载USB至JTAG转换器，无需外部编程器，并且完全开源，用户可自行制造。主要特性包括24k LUT、112 KiB RAM、256Mbit SDRAM、MicroSD卡槽等，适用于实时视频处理、硬件AI加速和ASIC原型设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FPGA项目及其相关工具、应用和市场现状

不同观点：
• utopcell认为该FPGA在爱好者社区中很流行，且有其他便宜的ECP5开发板可以替代，同时指出市场上已有类似低成本FPGA产品（如Sipeed's Tang Nano）。
• jwrallie强调ECP5 FPGA支持开源工具链，建议如果进行商业化应确认兼容性以增加吸引力。
• MegaDeKay分享了cyao12在Reddit上的经历，提到其在13岁时设计CPU的成就，并引发其他用户的惊叹和讨论。
• NoOn3提到了类似项目fleaFPGA_Ohm，指出了市场上存在其他类似FPGA解决方案。
• nebula8804询问该FPGA的能力，特别是是否可以移植MISter核心。
• ost-ing表示FPGA是其嵌入式开发的最后一步，但目前微控制器和固定架构CPU已经足够使用。
• deivid询问是否可以购买已组装好的FPGA板，抱怨Tang Nano的工具和文档不够完善。
• mysterydip表示对FPGA编程感兴趣，认为这个项目可能是一个入门点。
• aappleby表示愿意购买该产品。
• sockbot询问如何实现通过USB-C端口输出eDP，关注设计和硬件要求。
• kaoD询问材料的 approximate 成本。
• jedbrooke询问HDMI是否可以配置为输入，并表示该项目激发了他重新使用NeTV2板的兴趣。
• ComplexSystems将该项目与Arduino MKR Vidor进行比较。
• peterburkimsher询问是否存在支持HDMI输入和输出的FPGA板，并提出特定应用场景。

补充讨论：
• 开源工具链的可用性及其对FPGA项目的重要性。
• 市场上已有的类似FPGA产品，如Sipeed's Tang Nano和fleaFPGA_Ohm。
• FPGA在不同应用场景中的能力，如HDMI输入输出和核心移植。
• 用户对项目商业化和购买意愿的关注。
• 用户对FPGA板的组装和文档支持的需求。

争议焦点：
• utopcell和cyao12之间关于市场上是否存在低成本FPGA的看法不同。utopcell认为市场上已有类似产品，而cyao12则表示没有满足其需求的产品。

Icepi Zero - The portable FPGA development board.
What is the Icepi Zero?
Icepi Zero is an economical FPGA development board with a Raspberry Pi Zero form factor. It carries a Lattice ECP5 25F, enabling powerful designs while keeping a small portable size. It also has a HDM- port allowing easy digital video output.
View PCB online
Why Icepi Zero?
Currently most powerful FPGA boards on the market are expensive and bulky.
I've always wanted a low-cost portable FPGA with video output to make my own CPU, but there isn't any on the market.
The Icepi Zero aims to fix this. Carrying a powerful ECP5 FPGA on a small Raspberry Pi Zero form factor, it is the ultimate portable solution for FPGA development. Additionally packing a HDM- mini port and 3 USB-C ports, it allows interfacing with multiple external I/O devices.
Icepi Zero is for everyone: Students can use it to learn about the internals of modern processors. Gamers can use it to emulate old hardware. Programmers can use it to test their code on multiple architecture.
Icepi Zero also has an on-board USB to JTAG converter, so no external programmers are needed. Moreover Icepi Zero is fully open-source, no strings attached. Fabricate your own boards if you want one!
Features
Raspberry Pi Zero form factor
Lattice ECP5U FPGA:
24k LUT
112 KiB of RAM
One MiniGPDI connector (it's HDM- but I don't have the money to buy a license...)
Three USB-C Ports
256Mbit 166MHz SDRAM
MicroSD card slot
On-board USB to JTAG and UART converter
40MHz external oscillator
128 Mbit of flash
4 user LEDs
1 user button
This powerful configuration allows the PCB to be used in numerous ways, including real time video processing, hardware AI acceleration and prototyping of ASICs.
Usage
Check out the
firmware
folder for example code and compilation instructions!
If you want to order this board, it uses a 1.2mm PCB with JLC04121H-7628 Stackup. Gerbers are in the
production
folder in the
hardware
directory.

If there is any questions DM
@Cyao
on Hackclub Slack or
cyao.
on Discord. Mail is also accepted at
cyao _at_ duck.com
.

highway & undercity, a hackathon at Github HQ

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Wasp和PgBoss实现轻量级任务调度。PgBoss是一个基于PostgreSQL的作业队列系统，利用数据库的可靠性和扩展性来高效管理后台任务，无需额外基础设施。Wasp是一个全栈框架，简化了与PgBoss的集成，提供声明式任务定义、自动配置以及类型安全等优点。对于大多数小型项目和早期创业公司，这种组合足够处理每日低于1000个任务的场景，尤其是简单的任务如发送提醒邮件。但如果任务耗时长、数量多或涉及复杂计算，则应考虑使用独立的任务处理系统。文章还通过一个网球比分跟踪应用示例演示了如何创建一次性调度任务和周期性CRON任务。基本要求包括Node.js、PostgreSQL、Google OAuth认证和Mailgun配置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用不同工具（特别是cron、systemd timers、pg_cron及其他PostgreSQL相关工具）进行任务调度的优缺点讨论。

不同观点：
• NeutralForest认为systemd timers比cron更好用，尤其是在管理定时任务方面，界面更友好，操作更统一，能够像管理服务一样管理定时器。
• OJFord提到pg_cron，指出文章可能只是为了提升Wasp的SEO，因为pg_cron在RDS中已经存在，并且更知名。
• zie列举了多种可用于PostgreSQL的队列和调度工具，如pg_boss、pg_timetable、pgmq、Oban等，认为选择很多，不必局限于某一个工具。
• SoftTalker纠正了关于"cron"的写法，指出它不是缩写，不应全大写，并提供了名称的来源。
• jackb4040分享了在node-cron和真实Linux cron之间的选择，选择了后者，因为node-cron效率低，并询问了有关库的具体工作方式，特别是服务器宕机时任务是否执行的问题。
• verdverm推荐使用PG-Boss，认为它易用且足够，没有必要为了Wasp学习其自定义DSL，同时指出Wasp的一些优点并不显著。
• jbverschoor认为对于应用或平台级别的任务，应该使用任务队列，而不是机器级别的cron等，这样可以实现更好的监控和追踪。
• mitjam提到Kubernetes CronJobs也是一个不错的选择，特别是在已经使用Kubernetes的情况下，不需要额外基础设施。
• xnx和lukasb对没有提到pg_cron和Next.js/neon表示关注。
• wewewedxfgdf认为每个人有自己的偏好和方式来完成任务调度，自己专注于systemd timers。
• mati365质疑文章是否完全由AI生成。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Wasp的推广文章是否只是为了SEO，以及其相对于pg_cron等工具的实际价值。
• 不同工具（如systemd timers、pg_cron、PG-Boss等）在易用性、效率和功能上的对比是另一个讨论重点。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是任务在服务器宕机时的执行保障问题，特别是对于node-cron和真实Linux cron的不同表现。
• 社区中有多种调度工具可供选择，用户根据自己的需求和偏好选择合适的工具。

44114436.article_content:
I had the pleasure to spend nearly 3 years working on live video infrastructure at TV2 Norway. As you know, when it comes to infrastructure, time
IS
money. Everything needs to be just-in-time, especially when it comes to provisioning costly components like encoders. For example, if there's a major live sports match scheduled, you want to ensure the streaming infrastructure is set up just minutes before kickoff, and torn down shortly after the final whistle blows.
The fact is, scheduling is synonymous with infrastructure complexity. But sometimes you're just working on your trusty little Node app, and all you really need is something simple — like sending a daily reminder to users about today's coding challenge. That's exactly the kind of lightweight scheduling we'll dive into in this article.
Scheduling Jobs with Wasp and PgBoss
​
What is PgBoss?
​
PgBoss
is a job queue built on
PostgreSQL
. It leverages the database's reliability, transactional safety, and scalability to manage background jobs efficiently. Unlike Redis-based queues, PgBoss doesn't require additional infrastructure — just Postgres, which is a great fit if you're already using it as your database.
Key features:
Transactional safety
– jobs are stored in Postgres, ensuring they survive crashes.
Retries & timeouts
– failed jobs can be automatically retried.
Scheduling
– supports both delayed and recurring (CRON) jobs.
No extra infrastructure
- only Postgres needed.
Why Wasp Makes It Even Better
​
Wasp
is a full-stack framework for React & Node.js that simplifies web app development by handling boilerplate for you. When combined with PgBoss, Wasp provides:
Declarative job definitions
– define jobs directly in your Wasp config.
Everything just works
– no need to manually set up workers or queues.
Type safety
– jobs are type-checked, reducing runtime errors.
NOTE: Since PgBoss runs in the same process as your Wasp app, CPU-heavy jobs can impact API responsiveness. For high-load scenarios, consider offloading to a dedicated worker process.
When Should You Consider a Different Solution?
For most side projects and early-stage startups, this setup will work perfectly fine. As a rule of thumb, if you're processing less than 1000 jobs per day or your jobs are mostly lightweight operations (like sending emails or updating records), you can stick with this solution.
However, you might want to consider a dedicated job processing system when:
Your jobs take more than a few seconds to complete.
You're processing thousands of jobs per day.
Your jobs involve heavy computational tasks (like image processing or data analysis).
You need to scale job processing independently from your main application
A dedicated system means running your jobs on a separate server or process, isolated from your main application. This prevents long-running jobs from affecting your app's performance.
But remember: premature optimization is the root of all evil. Start with this simple solution, and only upgrade when you have concrete evidence that you need something more robust.
We'll look at two use cases:
One-time scheduled jobs (e.g., send a reminder email at a specific time).
Recurring  (CRON) jobs (e.g., daily digest emails).
We are going to use the
Wasp Tennis Score
example app to demonstrate the functionality.
The main interface of our tennis score tracking app
This is a neat little tennis score tracking app we've built. Think of it like this: you're running a tennis tournament and need to keep track of who's winning. The judges can punch in scores as the matches happen, and everyone watching can see the results.
To run the app, you'll need to clone the repo, create a new
.env.server
file (copy
example.env.server
as a starting point), populate it with the required values and execute the sequence of commands listed in the
README file here.
Requirements:
Node.js
≥20 installed — I recommend using
nvm
.
A
Postgres
database connection URL — but in our case for development you can just use
wasp db start
.
Google OAuth
credentials (Client ID and Client Secret)
Mailgun
config (API Key, Domain, API Url)
How to Create Scheduled Jobs with Wasp
​
After cloning the repository, you can check out the working example implementation of the scheduled job feature by running the following command:
git
checkout scheduled_job_added
Start the app with
wasp start
and authenticate with Google.
You'll be met with a UI that displays a list of tennis matches. Ongoing (i.e. Live) matches on the top and Completed Matches below.
In the header you will find a "Schedule Summary Email" button. That button is configured to send you a summary of the previous day's matches to your email.
The logged-in interface of our tennis scoring app
Click the button and check the email address linked to your Google account. You should see something similar to the screenshot below.
Email summary screenshot
Since this is a new account without any record of previous day's matches, the summary will be empty.

data.title: Ray Tracing in J
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者使用J语言编写的一个简易光线追踪器。J语言以其简洁和独特的ASCII语法而闻名，虽然初学者可能觉得其语法晦涩，但理解其数组编程范式后会发现语法并非主要障碍。文章重点解释了J语言中的隐式函数（tacit verbs），特别是三动词组合的fork结构，如计算平均数的例子。此外，还讨论了J语言中从右到左的计算顺序。

作者定义了一些实用函数，如计算向量长度的`magnitude`，以及向量归一化的`normalize`和点积的`dotproduct`。为了处理颜色，作者定义了将值限制在0到255之间的`toRGB`。文章还介绍了函数组合和部分应用的技巧，如使用`&`进行参数部分应用。最后，定义了反射函数`reflect`和选择最小正交交点的`hit`函数，用于确定光线与球体的首次接触点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：J语言在几何计算中的应用及其与其他编程范式的对比

不同观点：
• Vox_Leone认为J语言在数组处理和几何计算方面非常强大，但提出可以结合更高层次的语义框架（如其Python项目SpinStep）来进行基于方向的树结构遍历，以补充J语言的低层次计算能力。Vox_Leone强调了结合不同编程范式以实现更复杂的定向推理的可能性。
• gcanyon对文章中未提及的J语言的其他重要特性进行了补充，如 tacit syntax、Hook和"under" conjunction。他指出J语言可以通过复杂的verb组合实现强大的功能，并提供了更简洁的向量长度计算方法。gcanyon的评论更侧重于J语言的内部机制和语法特性。
• magicalhippo对文章没有重新实现SmallPT表示失望，认为如果能够处理多种不同对象、不同材质以及递归等特性会更有趣。这表明他期望看到更复杂和多功能的实现。

补充讨论：
• bobsmooth的评论并未直接参与关于J语言或SmallPT的讨论，而是提出一个技术社区中常见问题的幽默建议，即统计某类问题在Hacker News上被发布的次数。这属于对社区讨论内容的元讨论，而非直接的技术分析。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于对文章内容深度的期望不同。Vox_Leone和magicalhippo对文章内容的期望超出了文章实际讨论的范围，前者关注更高层次的框架结合，后者则希望看到更复杂的实现。而gcanyon则专注于补充文章中未详述的J语言特性。

44118646.article_content:
Ray Tracing in J
2020-04-18
I've been reading up on J and decided another small project was in
order, this time I've written a minimal ray tracer.
Brevity
J is, perhaps infamously, a terse language. I think it may sometimes
get unfairly discounted for this brevity because of the flavor of the
syntax (namely, ASCII). It can be a little hard to describe, but the
syntax isn't the hard part of learning J, the jarring parts are a
result of the paradigm differences in array programming. By the time
I've started to wrap my head around the very functional, array
oriented style of programming the syntax has started to fall away. At
least in the case of my own code I don't find the syntax being an
obstacle, I'm curious how this would hold up in the face of someone
else's code.
Tacit Verbs
One piece of syntax that bears explaining is J's means of tacit
programming (that is, functions which make no reference to their
arguments). While there is a bit more depth to it than I bother using,
I've limited myself to using mostly trains of three verbs, so-called
forks
. A fork is a function comprised of three verbs, F G and H and
might look like this:
myNewVerb=. F G H    NB. results in application (F(y)) G (H(y))
The parsing rules for J identify this pattern and apply the function
in a specific way; the canonical example is to define "average":
sum=. +/
divide=. %
count=. #
average=. sum divide count
If you applied it to an array
1 2 3 4 5
:
average 1 2 3 4 5
NB. (sum 1 2 3 4 5) divide (count 1 2 3 4 5)
One last thing that may confuse the untrained eye is the order of
evaluation. Sentences respect the traditional means of evaluating
parenthesized phrases first, but otherwise proceed from right to
left. An example:
- +/ 1 2 3
_6
The result will be the sum of
1 2 3
(6), which is then negated, so
the result is -6 (which is written as
_6
to avoid confusion with the
minus/negate symbol).
Utility Verbs
I've written several verbs in the tacit style that are generally
useful or improve the reading of the program, even when they're only
used once. The first is
magnitude
, which returns the magnitude of a
vector:
magnitude=: [: %: [: +/ *:      NB. sqrt of sum of squares
The comment should suffice for those who don't yet know the syntax of
J but it may be worth pointing out two interesting details. The first
is the fact that this "train" looks like it is 5 verbs, which doesn't
sound like a
fork
at first. The thing to keep in mind is that forks
can compose on top of other forks, so this may be viewed like:
[: %: [: +/ *:
a train of 5 verbs
[: %: ([: +/ *:)
the first fork is parenthesized
the second fork is now F G H, where H is the parenthesized fork
the resulting application is like
([: y) %: (([: +/ *:) y)
The use of
[:
is a little weird to understand, but it is basically a
no-operation left argument to ensure that the verb is evaluated as a
function of one argument instead of two. This is a consequence of J's
overloading of verbs for the two cases, e.g.
3 % 4
is "3 divided by
4", but
% 4
is "reciprocal of 4". By using
[:
in a train we ensure
that whatever is left of
%
isn't taken as a left argument and
instead we use the monadic form of the verb.
Although it isn't used much here, one thing that is really attractive
about array programming is the way verbs can operate independent of
dimensionality. Here I take the magnitude of a two-dimensional vector
and then a three-dimensional vector (which is what I use throughout
the ray tracer):
magnitude 6 8
10
magnitude 3 4 12
13
normalize=: ] * [: % magnitude  NB. scale by reciprocal of magnitude
dotproduct=: +/ . *
Both normalize and dot product aren't particularly interesting,
normalize is notable for composing a new verb train from the
previously defined
magnitude
without any special syntax or handling.
toRGB=: ([: <.&255 >.&0) & ([: <. 255&*) NB. 0->1 becomes 0->255 (clamped)
Throughout the ray tracer I deal with color as vectors of 3 floating
point numbers, intended to be between 0 and 1.0. In order to map the
range into the RGB space I'm doing
max(0, min(floor(x * 255),
255))
.
&
("bond") is used to partially apply arguments to a verb, a
simple example would be to define "addOne" as
+&1
. Interestingly,
&
can bond nouns to verbs to apply arguments but it may also be used
to compose functions as in math, e.g.
(f â g)(x) = f(g(x))
is
analogous to
f&g y
(eliding
a few
details
here).
Reflection is defined as a verb taking two argument, a vector and a
normal. It works by subtracting the vector and the normal scaled by
twice the dot product of the vector and the normal.
reflect=: [ - ] * +:@dotproduct          NB. (vector normal)
Given an array of intersections (defined later) a "hit" is defined as
the smallest positive intersection. This identifies which of the
points the ray "touches" are to be drawn, since the vector "moves" in
the time dimension it means we pick the first contact of the ray with
the sphere:
hit=: ([: {. /:~) & (0&< # ])   NB. smallest positive intersection

data.title: Use AI code tools as collaborators, not crutches
data.author: adityaoberai1
data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了当前过度依赖“氛围编码”（vibe coding）的趋势，即开发者在不理解技术细节的情况下，依赖AI工具生成代码，导致安全和质量问题。作者强调，尽管AI工具可以帮助加速开发，但开发者仍需掌握基础知识，如系统架构、数据处理和安全实践。文章提出三点建议：首先，开发者应学习并理解自己正在构建的内容，避免盲目生成代码；其次，在编码前应暂停思考，评估最佳方案；最后，应在编码前做好规划，确保代码逻辑清晰。作者警告，忽视这些基础而依赖“氛围编码”可能导致严重后果，开发者必须对自己的代码负责。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程和自我思考能力中的作用及其潜在影响

Do You Control The Tools Or Do The Tools Control You?
Aditya Oberai

4

Stop Vibe Coding Every Damn Time!

Share
These days, the hype around vibe coding feels limitless. Tools that promise to turn your ideas into apps with nothing more than a chat prompt are everywhere. But back in March this year, I came across a tweet from a developer who discovered that one of those tools, Lovable, was exposing a user's Supabase API key. While it was a publishable API key, it had no permissions or restrictions, and the developer was able to access all the app's data without authentication, just by looking at the public build.
This is not innovation. This is a security breach waiting to happen.
This is what happens when people lean too hard on the vibe. They build software by instinct, skip fundamentals, and trust that the tool knows best. But when you are shipping products that handle real data, real users, and real consequences, vibes alone will not cut it.
Welcome to 2025, where AI code-generation tools can get you 80 percent of the way there. And yet,
so many early-career developers are building software like they are writing poetry at an open mic
. No structure, no planning, no understanding. Just vibes. It’s high time we start fixing that!
Are Vibe Coding And AI-Assisted Coding The Same Thing?
First, let’s clear the air. Vibe coding is not the same as using an AI assistant.
Vibe coding
is what happens when you build software without understanding how anything works
, relying entirely on tools to fill in the gaps. You feed ChatGPT a vague prompt, drag in some randomly generated code blocks, wire up a few buttons, and hope it works. You ship without testing. You copy code you don’t understand. You build with vibes, not logic.
AI-assisted coding
, on the other hand,
is intentional.
You still plan your features. You still understand how your system fits together. You just move faster because you’ve got an AI pair programmer who helps with boilerplate, explains confusing concepts, and suggests things you were going to write anyway.
The difference is in the mindset.
AI-assisted developers are still the architects, while vibe coders hope the house stands because someone else drew the blueprint.
The Basics Still Matter
Even with AI, you still need to be a developer. If you’re not doing these things, please start today!
#1: Learn What You’re Building
Wanting to skip the learning process before building is the number one reason for the sloppily generated code currently available. It is precisely how developers lose all control over what they are building.
If you’re building an authentication system, you can’t not learn what tokens are, how sessions work, and why storing passwords in plaintext is a terrible idea. If you’re calling APIs, you must understand how requests are structured, what status codes mean, and how to handle errors gracefully. If you’re storing data, you should know how relational and NoSQL databases differ, when to use indexes, and what trade-offs come with each schema decision.
AI can help you write the code, but it can’t teach you to care.
That part is on you.  And in this case, to care is also to control. Every decision you delegate without understanding becomes a potential landmine waiting to explode (maybe not today, but definitely someday!)
#2: Pause and Assess
Before you open Cursor, start wiring up a UI, or churning out an API, just pause and ask yourself:
What am I actually trying to build?
Can I describe the core flow of this feature out loud or on paper?
Is there a simpler solution hiding behind the flashy one?
Every minute spent thinking before you build will save you ten debugging later. That pause could be the difference between launching a feature that works and shipping one that silently breaks user data in production.
Sometimes, the best code is no code
(or just a well-placed conditional). But you won’t realize that if you rush to prompt before you plan.
#3: Plan Before You Code
Design still matters, now more than ever. Start outlining your features, sketching out your user journeys, and writing pseudocode if that helps you structure your logic.
Even a basic plan, a few bullets on what the function needs to do, can guide your AI assistant to better output. If you just prompt
“build me an upload feature”,
the results will vary wildly. But if you’ve already planned:
“I need to let users upload PDF files up to 10MB, store them in an S3 storage bucket, and tag them by user ID”
, now you’ve got a little more clarity than before (and you still need more but hey, it’s a start).
Think about how data flows through your app, how users interact with it, and where things might break. These are the habits that turn junior developers into senior on

data.title: What motivates you to contribute to open source projects?
data.author: rizs12
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件贡献的动机和方式

不同观点：
• [em3rgent0rdr] 认为，开源软件提供的免费使用本身就是一种回报，贡献代码可以视为对这种回报的回馈。修复bug或添加功能不仅帮助了软件发展，也让自己受益。
• [acheong08] 指出，他们编写的许多代码经济价值不高，公开分享无妨，有时这些代码对其他人也有帮助。他们完全将项目维护交给社区，并从开源软件中个人获益。
• [ryao] 的贡献主要集中在修复bug上，动机是解决自己的需求或享受解决问题的智力挑战。他们过去曾将此作为全职工作，但现在每周只花几个小时。
• [dyingkneepad] 表示，尽管信仰开源模式，但每两周的薪水和健康保险等实际利益是主要动机，因为他们每天花费大量时间在开源项目上。
• [brynet] 开玩笑说，他们的动机是食物，特别是披萨。
• [deciduously] 提到，贡献是因为特定项目未能满足他们的特定需求，且他们知道如何修复。
• [horsellama] 列举了几个动机：修复困扰自己的bug、建立人脉和学习。
• [UncleEntity] 分享了他们在Blender项目的经验，最初是因为兴趣，后来通过解决bug和添加功能获得贡献者身份，过程中学到了很多技术。
• [m3047] 强调，贡献可以有多种形式，不限于提交PR。他们通过反馈、编写辅助工具和开发相关项目来贡献开源社区，但尚未找到志同道合的群体。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[dyingkneepad] 提到的经济动机与其他参与者更理想化的动机形成对比，显示出开源贡献者社区中不同人的实际需求和理想目标之间的张力。
• 贡献方式多样性：从提交代码、修复bug到撰写文档和提供反馈，不同参与者展示了多种贡献开源项目的方式。
• 社区协作：[acheong08] 和 [m3047] 都提到了将项目交给社区维护的经验，显示了开源项目中协作和所有权转移的重要性。
• 个人受益：许多参与者提到，贡献开源项目不仅帮助了社区，也给他们自己带来了技术和个人方面的成长。

data.title: Simple programming language with offline usable browser IDE
data.author: chrisjj
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：简化编程语言的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• [_rousbound] 认为简化编程语言（如仅包含变量、字符串、数字、布尔值、条件语句和循环等基本功能）足以用于编程入门教学，但担心过度简化可能反而增加学习难度，倾向于使用真实编程语言的子集进行教学。
• [abjr] 提到 Easylang（与讨论中的语言类似），并指出其作者每年参与编程挑战（AoC），表明这种简化语言具有实际应用价值。
• [layer8] 联想到 Comal 80，这是一种介于Basic和Pascal之间的语言，具有老式的REPL和类似Logo的海龟绘图功能，认为这种历史语言与讨论中的简化语言有相似之处。
• [7thaccount] 梦想有一种简化的命令驱动语言，能够快速执行任务，并提到对PowerShell性能和功能的不满，暗示希望有一种更简单且功能强大的语言。
• [chrisbrandow] 非常赞同这种简化语言，认为它比Scratch更有用，尤其在结合简单的画布和文本/控制台输出方面，认为这种设计非常棒。
• [xunil2ycom] 简单地将这种语言比作Logo语言，暗示其核心概念并不新颖。
• [mdaniel] 关注语言的许可协议问题，指出GPLv3和"All rights reserved"之间的潜在冲突，并对该语言尚未自举表示遗憾。
• [jcmontx] 认为这种语言类似于图形领域的DSL（领域特定语言），认为其在图形编程方面非常酷。
• [bn-l] 质疑这种语言的目标受众，尤其是对于孩子的适用性，认为其偏离了预期目标。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是简化语言是否真正有助于编程入门，部分评论者如[_rousbound]和[bn-l]对其适用性提出质疑，而[chrisbrandow]和[abjr]则表示支持。
• 另一个讨论点是简化语言的实际应用价值和性能问题，如[7thaccount]对PowerShell的不满以及对更快更强大语言的期望。
• 技术实现和许可问题也被提及，[mdaniel]关注GPLv3许可的兼容性和自举问题。
• 历史相似性和对比，如[layer8]提到的Comal 80和[xunil2ycom]提到的Logo语言，提供了对这种简化语言的历史背景和对比视角。

  - [kumarvvr] 认为ChatGPT的快速用户增长主要是因为炒作和口碑传播，而不是与互联网早期相比的真正可比性。他质疑将ChatGPT的用户增长与互联网的使用增长直接对比是否合理。
  - [kumarvvr] 进一步指出，企业对AI的谈论（如S&P 500公司）往往只是为了迎合投资者的期望，并没有实际数据支持用户是否更满意或有其他选择。

• **对报告和幻灯片风格的批评**：
  - [zipmapfoldright] 认为这些幻灯片的风格（如使用`=`和`+`符号）难以理解，容易引起误解。他希望有相关的讲解或录音来帮助理解内容。
  - [fernly] 批评幻灯片标题和内容像AI生成，缺乏人类智慧的体现，并指出标题和术语（如"Leading USA-Based LLM User"和"MM"单位）含义不明，且不同概念（如"Usage"和"Loss Growth"）无法直接相加。

• **AI应用的实际价值和用例**：
  - [pdevr] 认为AI将对娱乐行业产生深远影响，并预测生物研究等领域可能会有重大突破。但他同时指出，城乡差距和不同国家间的民主程度会影响AI的快速执行和应用。
  - [CompoundEyes] 强调AI在“足够好”的应用场景中提供了很大价值，不必追求100%准确。他以Taco Bell的AI驱动通过订单为例，认为只要输出经过人类审核，AI的错误率不会比人类员工或不准确的信息源造成更多问题。

• **AI的盈利能力和市场接受度**：
  - [amazingamazing] 质疑普通用户是否愿意为AI付费，特别是当人们不愿意支付少量费用去除广告时，是否会愿意支付高额的AI订阅费用。
  - [nwlotz] 提到即使是像OpenAI这样的超大规模公司也未实现盈利，质疑企业何时能通过采用AI开始盈利，并担心投资者预期的回报可能导致价格上涨，从而减缓AI的采用。

• **AI发展的方向和技术垄断问题**：
  - [w10-1] 认为报告汇集了大量数据，但缺乏对机器人技术和工厂自动化的深入探讨。他担心AI的发展方向过于集中在少数公司手中，而这些公司更偏向于SaaS而不是制造业，可能导致错失未来基础设施建设的机遇。
  - [codr7] 简单地将当前的AI热潮视为风险资本追逐利益的一部分，暗示对实际价值的怀疑。

补充讨论：
• **对具体AI应用案例的质疑**：
  - [kumarvvr] 对Yum! Brands的AI应用案例提出质疑，认为其所谓的AI增强运营具体如何实现并不明确，且有可能只是常规软件更新的一部分，而非真正的AI应用。

• **对自动驾驶技术进展的惊讶**：
  - [redwood] 对Waymo在旧金山的自动驾驶车超过网约车 rideshare的每周乘坐次数表示惊讶，显示出对自动驾驶技术进展的关注。

• **对报告发布方式的疑问**：
  - [thomassmith65] 质疑Meeker报告是否总是立即发布，还是曾经有过延迟发布的情况。

争议焦点：
• **AI技术实际应用的价值和真实性**：部分评论者（如[kumarvvr]和[fernly]）对AI应用的具体案例和报告内容持怀疑态度，认为存在炒作和夸大现象。而另一部分评论者（如[pdevr]和[CompoundEyes]）则认为AI在某些领域已经展现了实际价值和潜力。
• **AI的盈利模式和市场接受度**：评论者对普通消费者是否愿意为AI服务付费存在分歧，特别是考虑到当前一些超大规模AI公司尚未实现盈利。

data.title: Java Virtual Threads Ate My Memory: A Web Crawler's Tale of Speed vs. Memory
data.author: dariobalinzo
data.article_summary:
文章讲述了作者在构建一个网页爬虫时，从使用平台线程（Platform Threads）切换到虚拟线程（Virtual Threads）以提升性能的经历。最初，作者使用传统的平台线程和固定线程池来处理URL，尽管速度尚可，但他好奇虚拟线程能否进一步提高性能。切换到虚拟线程后，URL处理速度显著提升，但很快程序因`OutOfMemoryError`崩溃。

虚拟线程本应用于解决I/O阻塞问题，因其轻量级特性可以支持更多并发操作。然而，由于虚拟线程创建不受限，导致内存被过度消耗，最终引发内存溢出错误。作者通过分析问题，指出在使用虚拟线程时需要更精细的控制，以避免性能提升同时造成内存压力。

文章最后总结，软件开发中每个工具都有权衡，解决问题的同时也可能引入新问题，开发者需平衡性能、安全性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：虚拟线程和流式处理的内存管理与并发控制

不同观点：
• [jsd1982] 认为应通过流式处理和缓冲IO来解决内存问题，CPU处理可以自然形成背压机制，防止过多的内容下载和无限制的内存分配。每个CPU worker只需分配一个小的缓冲区，从而使内存使用完全可预测。
• [koito17] 指出如果没有背压机制，程序会不断占用内存，并认为在具有真实线程的环境中，从OS线程转向绿色线程和异步处理会放弃经过验证的OS调度器机制，开发者需自行管理背压问题。
• [hocuspocus] 提到Jox提供了具有 bounded capacity 的缓冲通道，可以用于虚拟线程的高级API。
• [Copenjin] 认为异步和绿色线程等工具并不能消除对并发和程序流的思考需求，开发者仍需学会如何处理并发问题。
• [fjasdfwa] 认为虚拟线程和回调或async-await等机制之间存在权衡，开发者需在简化代码和内存管理之间做出选择。
• [ivolimmen] 指出如果进行大量内存密集型处理，虚拟线程的优势不明显，建议关注内存使用和线程数量的平衡。
• [kburman] 认为这是设计问题而非虚拟线程问题。
• [marginalia_nu] 强调虚拟线程并非万能，在某些场景如网络爬虫中，使用有界线程池可能更合适，因为其 boundedness 是一个特性。
• [unscaled] 补充即使内存不是问题，CPU也是一个有限资源，需要引入背压机制，否则会导致线程堆积和OOM问题。
• [geodel] 分享了通过阻塞队列限制并发任务数量的成功经验，发现保持虚拟线程在100倍于并发调用外部资源时性能最佳。
• [swsieber] 引用了Java虚拟线程的官方文档，强调限制并发操作的重要性，并指出虚拟线程和传统线程池任务在排队和阻塞机制上的等效性。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于虚拟线程是否能自动解决并发和内存管理问题，反对者认为开发者仍需手动控制背压和并发限制。
- 支持者认为通过适当的机制如Semaphore可以有效管理并发，但也有开发者指出在CPU密集型任务中，传统线程池可能更有效。
- 不同工具和语言（如Clojure的core.async和Zig语言）在处理并发和背压问题上的比较也被提及。

总体而言，讨论围绕虚拟线程的内存和并发管理展开，强调了即使使用虚拟线程，开发者仍需仔细设计系统以避免资源耗尽和性能瓶颈。

data.title: Valkey Turns One: Community fork of Redis
data.author: cebert
data.article_summary: 文章总结了开源项目Valkey在Redis闭源后，由社区推动成功分叉并超越Redis 8.0的历程。一年前，Redis Inc.关闭Redis源代码，引发社区不满。作为回应，社区创建了Valkey分叉项目，旨在保持Redis的开源精神。经过一年的发展，Valkey在性能测试中表现优异，在多线程I/O模型下，其吞吐量和延迟均优于Redis 8.0。具体来说，Valkey在8核实例上达到了999.8K RPS，而Redis 8.0为729.4K RPS。此外，Valkey在多线程环境下展示了更高的性能扩展，特别是在连接数增加时表现更为突出。最终，Valkey不仅存活下来，而且蓬勃发展，成为社区力量推动开源项目的成功案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Redis与ValKey的关系、技术改进、开源与商业化争议以及社区反应

不同观点：
• antirez（Redis创建者）认为，ValKey在I/O线程方面的工作是对Redis的有效补充，且I/O线程的改进早在2020年就由他亲自实现，并非完全新颖。他强调，Redis的"无共享"架构与I/O线程并不冲突，且这些改进对于一般用户而言并非必需，主要对高负载情境有显著效果。同时，他批评了有关Redis的技术文章，认为其中一些内容误导读者。
• geerlingguy提出Redis重新转向真正的开源是否为时已晚的问题，并以Node.js和Io.js的历史为例，暗示社区有可能修复和继续发展Redis，但也表达了对当前社区状况的不确定性。
• bhouston指出，将valkey纳入默认的发行版包管理器中是必要的，以简化安装流程，尤其是对于像GitHub Action runner这样的环境。
• linotype对Redis的未来持悲观态度，甚至希望Redis“安息”，暗示ValKey或将取代Redis。
• pipes讨论了.NET项目商业化对开源社区的潜在影响，认为这可能损害其他开源库的采用率。
• detail_orient对ValKey的发展表示支持，但对技术细节未做过多讨论。
• secondcoming关注ValKey是否提供自己的客户端库，并提到在使用Redis集群和TLS时遇到的困难，考虑转向Scylla。
• y2244建议ValKey和Redis进行合作，合并努力以避免重复工作。
• kamikazechaser预期会有关于GPL（通用公共许可证）的恐慌言论（FUD），并提供了一篇解释文章来缓解这种担忧。
• bofaGuy分享了在AWS上使用ValKey的负面体验，包括服务意外中断和AWS技术支持无法解决问题，最终换回Redis。
• nwlotz对ValKey没有像OpenTofu那样获得企业赞助表示好奇，并将其与HashiCorp更改Terraform许可引发的社区反应进行对比。

补充讨论：
• Redis和ValKey的技术改进，尤其是I/O线程的实现，对一般用户和高负载用户的影响不同。
• Redis开源状态的变化及其对社区的影响。
• ValKey在实际使用中的稳定性和技术支持问题。
• 开源项目商业化及其对社区和开发者的影响。
• 社区对Redis和ValKey未来发展的期望与建议。

44140379.article_content:
Valkey Turns One: How the Community Fork Left Redis in the Dust
Valkey is not only thriving, but now outperforming Redis 8.0 in real world benchmarks.
Khawaja Shams
Author
Perspectives
Share
A year ago, Redis Inc (formerly Garantia Data) made a controversial move that disrupted the open source ecosystem: it closed the source of Redis.
As I wrote at the time
, it was a trust-breaking decision that could have shattered the community.
But instead of splintering, the community responded with purpose. Out of that disruption came
Valkey
, a fork that took a shot at keeping the community alive.
A Return, A Reversal
As part of efforts to rebuild trust with the community, Redis Inc
brought back
Salvatore Sanfilippo (aka Antirez), the original creator of Redis. I am genuinely excited about his return because it is already impactful. He’s following through on his promise of contributing new features and performance optimizations to Redis. More profoundly,
Redis 8.0 has been open-sourced again
.
Redis acknowledged that adopting
SSPL
strained their bond with the community, questioning contributions from others in the same breath.
How do you keep innovating and investing in OSS projects when cloud providers reap the profits and control the infrastructure without proportional contributions back to the projects that they exploit?
The disheartening move from Redis Inc catalyzed an unprecedented wave of collaboration and contributions. Valkey became the test of the community resolve to keep itself together. One year later, Valkey hasn’t just survived –
it’s thriving
! The Async I/O Threading model
contribution
from AWS unlocked 3x+ throughput by fundamentally changing how I/O threads work inside Redis.
But how do these and other contributions compare to Redis 8? Can we hit 1M RPS out of an 8 VCPU instance (c8g.2xl) on either Valkey 8.1 or Redis 8.0 (with 1KB items, 3M items in the key space, and ~500 connections)? It’s time for a bake off!
Valkey 8.1 vs Redis 8.0: Can the Fork Outrun the Source?
The punchline: we could not sustain 1M RPS on an 8 VCPU instance with either Valkey or Redis 8.0, but we got really close!!
On a full-tuned c8g.2xl (8 VCPU), Valkey 8.1.1 pushed to 999.8K RPS on SETs with .8ms p99 latency. Redis 8.0 got as high as 729.4 RPS on SETs with .99ms p99 latencies. On each iteration, we tested 50M SETs followed by 50M GETs. We varied connection counts to optimize the maximum throughput for each system.
Valkey achieved higher throughput and lower latency across both reads and writes (37% higher on SET and 16% higher on GET), alongside 30% faster p99 latencies for SET and 60%+ faster on GET.
Threading the multi-threading needle
If I had a penny for every time heard, “but Redis /Valkey is single threaded….”
Antirez’s emphasis on a shared nothing architecture has been foundational for Redis. Nevertheless, as early as 2020, Redis added support for I/O threads. Unfortunately, they did not offer drastic improvement until recently. If you have previously tried and discarded I/O threads, it is time to evaluate again!
On Valkey, we see SET throughput going from 239K RPS without I/O threads to 678K with 6 threads. Meanwhile, p99 latencies dropped from 1.68ms to 0.93ms
despite doing nearly 3x the throughput
! Similarly, Redis went from 235K RPS without I/O threads to 563K RPS with 6 I/O threads. P99s for Redis also dropped around 40% from 1.35ms to 0.84ms.
Two key takeaways emerged:
With two threads, gains were modest (~20%). The impact only really surfaced at three threads and beyond.
Redis and Valkey were neck-and-neck until the fourth thread. After that, Valkey pulled away sharply.
SET Performance on Valkey with IO/Threads & 256 Connections:
SET Performance on Redis with IO/Threads & 256 Connections:
Pushing Valkey Throughput Further
In the previous section, we saw that Valkey could hit 678K RPS on SETs with 6 threads and 256 connections. If we up the connections to 400, the throughput goes up to 832K RPS. How did we get the additional 167K RPS?
We used
Rezolus
, our favorite Linux performance telemetry agent, to get deep insights into the system under stress. You can see in the charts below that overall CPU utilization is around 80% and unevenly distributed across the 8 cores.
Diving deeper, this is driven by hardware interrupts from network queues across all 8 cores. Interrupts are bad because they disrupt a hard working Valkey thread to yield to handle network packets.
What if we could avoid the context switching on our
c8g.2xl
with 8 cores? Running close to a million RPS requires considerable packet processing horsepower. Luckily, since a lot of work happens at the Nitro level on EC2 instances, two allocated cores to IRQs is all you need (if you let them focus). Pinning the IRQs to two cores is pretty straightforward.
sudo ethtool -L ens34 combined 2 # reduce to 2 IRQs
grep ens34 /proc/interrupts # ours were on 99 and 100
echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/irq/99/smp_affinity # pin 99 to core 1
echo 2 | sudo tee /proc/irq/1
44140379.article_summary: 文章总结了开源项目Valkey在Redis闭源后，由社区推动成功分叉并超越Redis 8.0的历程。一年前，Redis Inc.关闭Redis源代码，引发社区不满。作为回应，社区创建了Valkey分叉项目，旨在保持Redis的开源精神。经过一年的发展，Valkey在性能测试中表现优异，在多线程I/O模型下，其吞吐量和延迟均优于Redis 8.0。具体来说，Valkey在8核实例上达到了999.8K RPS，而Redis 8.0为729.4K RPS。此外，Valkey在多线程环境下展示了更高的性能扩展，特别是在连接数增加时表现更为突出。最终，Valkey不仅存活下来，而且蓬勃发展，成为社区力量推动开源项目的成功案例。

data.title: Revenge of the Chickenized Reverse-Centaurs
data.author: GreenWatermelon
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了人工智能和劳动领域中的两种现象：“半人马”和“鸡肉化”。在人工智能领域，“半人马”指的是人类与机器协作以发挥各自优势的模式，例如国际象棋大师与计算机程序合作。而在劳动领域，“鸡肉化”指的是一种剥削性的工作安排，类似于美国养鸡农民的困境。大公司通过控制农民或司机的每一个环节，如工具、服务和操作方式，使他们仅能维持生计而无法改变职业。

文章进一步指出，新一代的劳动剥削结合了“鸡肉化”和“反向半人马”模式，即人工智能主导人类劳动。尽管表面上人类与机器协作，但实际上人类被机器控制。文章强调，解决这一问题需要工会和新的高科技组织工具，以对抗企业的高科技策略，恢复工人权力。尽管面临政治上的阻碍，工会正努力复兴并创造新的策略来保护工人权益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI和技术进步对劳动力市场、社会结构及经济的影响

不同观点：
• **theptip**：对AI可能导致的负面结果表示担忧，尤其是技术封建主义（techno-feudalism）和失业问题。虽然低技能工作可能被自动化取代，但高需求的技术工种（如木工和机械师）仍然有较好的就业前景。社会如何应对失业的低技能工人将是关键问题。长期来看，许多工作都会被自动化，因此需要新的社会契约（如UBI），但资本会强烈反对这种变革。

• **kragen**：提到Marshall Brain在2003年写的书《Manna》预见了当前的自动化问题，但对乐观的结局持怀疑态度。这本书讨论了自动化对就业的取代以及社会可能的反应。

• **Animats**：通过具体案例（如家禽加工业和乳制品行业）说明了劳动者面临的剥削问题，尤其是家禽农户被垄断企业控制的困境，反映了当前劳动市场的结构性问题。

• **GreenWatermelon**：强烈反对家禽农户被“鸡肉化”（chickenization）剥削的现状，描述了农户在垄断企业控制下的困境，并对此表示愤怒。

• **scotty79**：提出AI取代的不仅是低技能工作，还可能包括管理职位。AI可以通过代码或算法替代管理者的职能。

• **euroderf**：关注美国家禽行业的困境，并询问欧盟是否对农民和动物有更好的保护措施，暗示可能存在跨国差异。

• **cosmicgadget**：认为商业利益通常会在劳动组织方法流行之前就加以限制，例如通过服务条款的限制。在某些情况下，法规可能是防止这种情况的唯一途径。

• **droopyEyelids**：指出在美国，工会化面临法律限制，包括禁止行业工会化、同情罢工、二次抵制等，这使得工会化难以复兴。

• **ses1984**：建议创建一个具有合作所有权模式的零工平台，以解决当前零工经济中的剥削问题。

• **motoboi**：反驳关于人类与AI协作能提高竞争力的观点，认为顶级AI（如Alpha Zero）的棋艺远超任何人类，不需要人类协作。

• **MichaelZuo**：认为如果工会化能带来更高的客户价值，那么市场自然会选择这种模式，不需要过多的理论辩论。客户会用钱包投票，支持那些提供更高价值的服务。

补充讨论：
- **自动化对不同技能层次工作的影响**：一部分观点认为低技能工作将被取代，但高技能技术工种仍有需求；另一部分讨论则涉及管理职位也可能被AI取代。
- **工会化和法律限制**：讨论了美国法律对工会化的限制以及其对劳动者权益的影响，并提出了可能的解决方案，如合作所有权模式。
- **跨国比较**：有人提出美国与其他地区（如欧盟）在劳动者保护和市场结构上的差异，反映了全球范围内对劳动者待遇的关注。

争议焦点：
- **自动化与就业取代的不可避免性**：部分人认为自动化将不可避免地取代大量工作，而社会需要为此做出结构性调整（如实施UBI），另一部分人则关注特定高需求工种的就业前景。
- **工会化的可行性**：在美国法律限制下，工会化是否能复兴以及如何应对当前的劳动剥削问题存在争议。

44118055.article_content:
Algorithms and worker power
Cryteria
,
CC BY
, modified
In AI circles, a “centaur” describes a certain kind of machine/human collaboration, in which “decision-support” systems (which the field loves to call “AI”s) are paired with human beings for results that draw upon the strengths of each, such as when a human chess master and a chess-playing computer program collaborate to smash their competition.
In labor circles, “chickenization” refers to exploitative working arrangements that resemble the plight of the American poultry farmer. The U.S. poultry industry has been taken over by three monopolistic packers, who have divided the nation up into exclusive territories, so that each chicken farmer has only one buyer for their birds.
Farmers are “independent small businesspeople” who nominally run their own operations, but because all their products must be sold through a single poultry processor, that processor is able to exercise enormous control over the operation. The processor tells the farmer which birds to raise, as well as what the birds are to be fed, how much, and on what schedule. The processor tells the farmer how to build their coops and when the lights are to go on and off. The processor tells the farmer which vets to use, and tells the vets which medicines to prescribe.
The processor tells the farmer everything…except how much they’ll be able to sell their birds for. That is determined unilaterally when the farmer brings their birds to market, and the payout is titrated to the cent, to represent exactly enough money for the farmer to buy birds and feed and vet services through the processor’s preferred suppliers, and to service the debts on the coops and light and land, but not one penny more.
Chickenization has spread beyond chicken farming.
Uber drivers are paid on a variable reinforcement drip-feed that gives them just enough to keep up the lease and gas and insurance payments on their vehicles
, but not enough to give them breathing space to think about changing careers.
Likewise for Amazon drivers. Amazon styles the drivers as subcontractors working for a “Delivery Service Partner” (DSP), and the DSP is fully chickenized: They have to buy Amazon vans and subject them to Amazon maintenance, but
Amazon reserves the right to fire a DSP without notice, stranding them with vehicle and lot leases and payroll liabilities.
The DSP owners are chickenized, but the drivers themselves? They’re more like the chickens. Or rather, they’re centaurs: From the instant you get behind the wheel of an Amazon van,
you are being surveilled by an array of cameras hooked up to high-handed, judgemental AIs that monitor your facial expressions, your eye movements, and your ability to meet an impossible quota
.
But even though an Amazon driver represents the tight coupling of a human and a machine to do more than either could do on their own, that’s not the kind of centaur that we talk about when it’s a chess master paired with a chess program. That chess master is being
augmented
by the machine, and the machine is the junior partner in the relationship. The human is the head, and the AI is the body.
By contrast, an Amazon driver is a
reverse-centaur
. The AI is in charge, and the human is the junior partner. The AI is the head, telling the body what to do. The driver is the body — the slow-witted, ambulatory meat that is puppeteered by the AI master.
The next generation of labor exploitation merges chickenization
with
reverse-centaurs. DoorDash and other gig companies use apps to script the movements and conduct of “independent contractors” to the finest degree, while
hiding their true wages
from them until they’ve finished their jobs.
The simplistic answer to this is, “Well, if you don’t like it, don’t work for a gig company.”
But that’s not how labor rights work. Behind every labor struggle is a recognition that business owners have negotiating power over workers that will, over time, shift more and more value from workers to bosses. Labor market outcomes are not a matter of individuals bargaining with one another: In a labor market, atomized workers bargain with consolidated firms.
It’s hard for workers to play companies off against each other to get higher wages (
and companies get furious when they pull it off
), but it’s easy for businesses to play workers off against each other to pay lower wages.
Historically, worker power has come from unions, which were able to bargain for workers at a specific job-site, or across a sector, and, just as importantly, to win labor regulations that protect
all
workers. Forty years of all-out assaults on labor organizing have weakened that source of worker power, and
both Republicans and Democrats
are deeply committed to keeping unions weak.
Despite this lack of institutional support,
unions are coming back with a vengeance
, and they’re pulling it off by creating new, high-tech organizing tools and strategies that answer high-tech employer tactics with high-tech worker tactics.

data.title: Silicon Valley finally has a big electronics retailer again: Micro Center opens
data.author: modeless
data.article_summary: Micro Center Silicon Valley正式开业，位于圣克拉拉市史蒂文斯溪大道5201号。开业当天吸引了数百名科技爱好者和DIY PC建造者排队等候。新店提供丰富的电脑组件、显卡和3D打印机等，并有专业知识丰富的员工提供咨询服务。开业促销包括Windows台式机和笔记本电脑享受八折优惠，显示器也打八折。店内还备有超过4000张显卡，包括独家型号。此外，一款由NVIDIA CEO签名、镀金的Asus Astral RTX 5090 Dhahab Edition GPU将在店内展出，随后用于慈善拍卖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Micro Center与其他电子产品零售商的比较以及电子产品零售行业的变迁。

不同观点：
• **Micro Center的改进与优势**：
  - **[neilv]**：认为Micro Center相较于以前有了很大改进，商品齐全，且未将开封退货重新作为新品出售。同时表达了对本地缺乏优质剩余电子产品和电子回收店的遗憾。
  - **[Braxton1980]**：强调Micro Center对爱好者的重视，比如设有专门的水冷配件通道，已经取代Newegg成为其首选购物地点。
  - **[mcbuckeye]**：对Micro Center能存活至今表示惊讶，并怀念过去在店里探索的乐趣。

data.title: Show HN: Smart Silence – Remind your iPhone to stay quiet in quiet places
data.author: ebagsnave
data.article_summary: 要加入Smart Silence的测试版，首先需要在iPhone、iPad或Mac上安装TestFlight应用。TestFlight用于帮助开发者测试beta版应用和App Clips。安装TestFlight后，通过链接即可参与Smart Silence的beta测试。Smart Silence利用信标技术，在指定地点（如会议室、图书馆）自动提示启用“勿扰模式”，帮助用户减少干扰，专注于重要事务。该应用提供基于 proximity 的通知、可定制体验、简化的设置和隐私保护等功能，适合需要管理分心的专业人士和学生使用。测试版应用有90天的测试期，过期后需从App Store下载正式版。测试期间的内购不会延续到正式版。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS的“勿扰模式”（DND）及其自动化功能的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• [matricaria] 认为iOS的DND功能已经可以基于位置自动激活，不需要额外功能。
• [russelldjimmy] 提出疑问，认为通过基于位置的快捷指令（Shortcut）已经可以实现类似功能，质疑新功能的必要性。
• [nytesky] 建议Apple和Google引入一种地理围栏协议，允许地点自动触发DND或限制网络访问，并举例说明在特定场合如教堂或学校自动进入DND模式的好处，特别是对特殊职业如医生和消防员提供可选的覆盖功能。
• [neepi] 提出区域性差异，指出在英国手机通常已经默认静音，因此这种功能在某些地区可能不那么必要。
• [nico] 关注闹钟问题，指出静音模式不会静音闹钟，导致自己经常忘记检查，希望有一种模式可以同时静音闹钟。
• [anArbitraryOne] 对Apple的操作系统持否定态度，表示更喜欢使用传统的纸笔，而不是Apple的系统。
• [kurtis_reed] 指出讨论假设用户拥有iPhone，而自己并没有iPhone，质疑讨论的前提。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于当前iOS系统是否已经具备用户所需的功能（如基于位置的DND和快捷指令），以及是否有必要引入更复杂的地理围栏协议。
• nytesky的建议引发了对特殊场合和职业需求的讨论，特别是自动DND模式的可覆盖性。
• 不同地区的手机使用习惯（如英国默认静音）也被视为影响功能需求的一个因素。
• 个别用户对Apple产品的整体态度（如anArbitraryOne和kurtis_reed）也反映了更广泛的技术选择偏好问题。

data.title: Personal Ambient Computing
data.author: delaugust
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了个人计算的未来，提出“个人环境计算”（PAC）概念，旨在让计算摆脱单一设备的束缚。作者受《星际迷航》启发，设想了一种模块化、圆盘形的计算单元，直径如银元，厚度更大，包含处理器、存储、连接、传感器和麦克风。该圆盘可通过磁性边缘系统嵌入各种设备，如手表、手持设备、桌面显示器等，形成个人网络。这种设计强调模块化、开放源代码以及设备间的协同工作，减少对单一智能手机的依赖，同时提升移动性和专注度。作者还设想通过开放硬件外壳设计，提升可修复性和可持续性，创造更多利基设备。这种新计算范式并非取代现有设备，而是增加设备间的互操作性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕设备设计和功能的讨论，包括对历史设计概念的评价和未来潜力的分析]

不同观点：
• **calmbonsai** 认为Don Norman的《The Invisible Computer》一书中的设计理念，尤其是环境界面和智能手机作为“中心”的概念，尽管书中关于网格网络和语音交互的想法已经过时，但仍具有潜力。他强调智能手机作为核心设备的构想。

• **brador** 则持更简化、实际的观点，认为这仅仅是一个具有动能供电或超三天电池寿命的开源智能手表，没有特别突出的新意或复杂设计。

• **ocdtrekkie** 提出“可替换计算模块”的设计早已有之，但往往在第二代产品推出之前就失败了。尽管如此，他仍然支持这种设计理念，尤其是将个人手机数据与更强大硬件对接的想法，尽管历史上类似的lapdock设计大多未能延续多代。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：calmbonsai和ocdtrekkie对历史设计理念的评价存在差异。calmbonsai认为某些过时的概念仍有潜力，而ocdtrekkie则指出这些概念在历史上多次失败，显示出对其实际可行性的怀疑。

• **技术实现**：brador更关注设备的实际功能，如电池寿命和开源性，而其他讨论者更重视设计理念和未来潜力。

• **历史教训**：ocdtrekkie特别提到过去的设计失败案例，如lapdock和计算模块，这为当前讨论提供了历史背景和实际限制。

• **未来潜力**：calmbonsai对智能手机作为中心设备的未来应用持乐观态度，而ocdtrekkie则在支持概念的同时，对其实际可行性和持续性持谨慎态度。

44139053.article_content:
Christopher Butler
Info
/Now
Archive
PAC
— Personal Ambient Computing
The next evolution of personal computing won’t replace your phone — it will free computing from any single device.
Like most technologists of a certain age, many of my expectations for the future of computing were set by Star Trek production designers. It’s quite easy to connect many of the devices we have today to props designed 30-50 years ago: The citizens of the Federation had communicators before we had cellphones, tricorders before we had smartphones, PADDs before we had tablets, wearables before the Humane
AI
pin, and voice interfaces before we had Siri. You could easily make a case that Silicon Valley owes everything to Star Trek.
But now, there seems to be a shared notion that the computing paradigm established over the last half-century has run its course. The devices all work well, of course, but they all come with costs to culture that are worth correcting. We want to be more mobile, less distracted, less encumbered by particular modes of use in certain contexts. And, it’s also worth pointing out that the creation of generative
AI
has made the corporate shareholders ravenous for new products and new revenue streams. So whether we want them or not, we’re going to get new devices. The question is, will they be as revolutionary
as they’re already hyped up to be
? I’m old enough to remember the gasping “city-changing”
hype of the Segway
before everyone realized it was just a scooter with a gyroscope. But in fairness, there was equal hype to the iPhone and it isn’t
overreaching to say that it remade culture even more extensively than a vehicle ever could have.
So time will tell.
I do think there is room for a new approach to computing, but I don’t expect it to be a new device that renders all others obsolete. The smartphone didn’t do that to desktop or laptop computers, nor did the tablet. We shouldn’t expect a screenless, sensor-ridden device to replace anyone’s phone entirely, either. But done well, such a thing could be a welcome addition to a person’s kit. The question is whether that means just making a new thing or rethinking how the various computers in our life work together.
As I’ve been pondering that idea, I keep thinking back to Star Trek, and how the device that probably inspired the least wonder in me as a child is the one that seems most relevant now: the Federation’s wearables. Every officer wore a communicator pin — a kind of Humane Pin light — but they also all wore smaller pins at their collars signifying rank. In hindsight, it seems like those collar pins, which were discs the size of a watch battery, could have formed some kind of wearable, personal mesh network. And that idea got me going…
The future isn’t a zero-sum game between old and new interaction modes. Rather than being defined by a single new computing paradigm, the future will be characterized by an increase in computing: more devices doing more things.
I’ve been thinking of this as a
PAC
—
P
ersonal
A
mbient
C
omputing.
Personal Ambient Computing
At its core is a modular component I’ve been envisioning as a small, disc-shaped computing unit roughly the diameter of a silver dollar but considerably thicker. This disc would contain processing power, storage, connectivity, sensors, and microphones.
The disc could be worn as jewelry, embedded in a wristwatch with its own display, housed in a handheld device like a phone or reader, integrated into a desktop or portable (laptop or tablet) display, or even embedded in household appliances. This approach would create a personal mesh network of
PAC
modules, each optimized for its context, rather than forcing every function in our lives through a smartphone.
The key innovation lies in the standardized form factor. I imagine a magnetic edge system that allows the disc to snap into various enclosures — wristwatches, handhelds, desktop displays, wearable bands, necklaces, clips, and chargers. By getting the physical interface right from the start, the
PAC
hardware wouldn’t need significant redesign over time, but an entirely new ecosystem of enclosures could evolve more gradually and be created by anyone.
A worthy paradigm shift in computing is one that makes the most use of modularity, open-source software and hardware, and context. Open-sourcing hardware enclosures, especially, would offer a massive leap forward for repairability and sustainability.
In my illustration above, I even went as far as sketching a smaller handheld — exactly the sort of device I’d prefer over the typical smartphone. Mine would be proudly boxy with a larger top bezel to enable greater repair access to core components, like the camera, sensors, microphone, speakers, and a smaller, low-power screen I’d depend upon heavily for info throughout the day. Hey, a man can dream.
The point is, a
PAC
approach would make niche devices much more likely.
Power

data.title: Illinois man has spent 40 years rebuilding a WWII-era B-17 bomber in his barn
data.author: frasermarlow
data.article_summary: 一名来自伊利诺伊州Marengo的男子Mike Kellner正在努力修复一架二战时期的B-17轰炸机，这一项目他已经在路边的一个谷仓中坚持了40年。Kellner自高中起就是航空爱好者，当年从缅因州的一个废车场购买了这架拆解的飞机残骸，并用卡车运回。他花费无数时间自行修复飞机，寻找稀有零件，并吸引了其他志愿者协助。他的目标不仅是修复外观，更希望让这架“飞行堡垒”重新飞上天空。Kellner在Facebook上记录了整个修复过程，吸引了广泛关注。B-17是二战期间美国军方使用的标志性四引擎重型轰炸机，以其强大的火力和高空轰炸能力闻名。
data.comments_summary:

• [spanktheuser] 表达了对该项目在附近进行的惊讶，显示出对该项目的地域性关注，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [toomuchtodo] 提供了有关该项目的更多信息，分享了一个Facebook页面链接，引导感兴趣的读者获取更多详情。

• [frasermarlow] 指出该修复项目不仅仅是为了展示，还包括实际飞行的意图，强调了项目参与者的实际目标。

- 讨论中出现了对轰炸机技术能力和历史表现的不同评价，特别是[cafard]对其实际作战表现的批评与其他评论者对项目的赞赏形成对比。

A man in Marengo, Illinois, is on a mission to fully restore a World War II-era B-17 bomber—a project he’s been diligently working on in a roadside barn for the past 40 years.
A lifelong
aviation
enthusiast, Mike Kellner began his journey in high school after hearing that a junkyard in Maine was looking to offload the abandoned remains of the historic bomber. The asking price was “$7,000 or best offer” for a collection of disassembled parts. Kellner loaded the 75-foot aluminum behemoth onto a house trailer (he had to extend it by about 10 feet) and hauled it halfway across the country with a pickup truck. It’s lived in his barn ever since. Kellner shared the decades-long story of his restoration project
with local outlet WGN
earlier this week.
And unlike many World War II-era roadside relics, this one isn’t just collecting dust. Kellner has spent countless hours working to restore the plane to its former glory, performing his own repairs, adding finishing touches, and tracking down an array of rare and hard-to-find parts. Word of his efforts spread, attracting other aviation enthusiasts who have volunteered their time over the years to assist with the restoration. Kellner documents the entire process on a
Facebook page
, which features thousands of update posts dating back to 2010. He doesn’t just want the project to be something pretty to look at—he wants it to fly.
“It is a piece of history, and I would like the opportunity to fly it,” Kellner told WGN.
Popular Science
reached out to Kellner for more details but has not heard back.
Rebuilding a ‘Flying fortress’
The B-17 was the
most iconic bomber used by the US military
during the second World War. Its origin actually traces back a decade earlier to 1934, when the Army Air Corps approached Boeing with an ask to design and develop a massive plane capable of carrying bombs at 10,000 feet and for more than 10 hours. The military wanted a new breed of bomber that would be able to travel beyond enemy lines at great distances and drop bombs with precision. It needed to be able to reach altitudes high enough to fly outside of the range of enemy antiaircraft artillery. The eventual B-17 featured a state-of-the-art
Norden bombsight
to maintain accuracy even at extreme altitudes.
Early versions of the B-17 entered production in 1937, but manufacturing ramped up significantly after the U.S. officially entered World War II in 1941. The bomber that eventually flew missions behind enemy lines featured four engines—a major upgrade from the then-standard two—and was equipped with a smattering of gun turrets, including ones in the nose, upper fuselage, and tail. This cornucopia of munitions, combined with the aircraft’s mammoth size, earned it the nickname “Flying Fortress.”
The B-17 currently being resurrected in Kellner’s barn reportedly carries two names. One, “Desert Rat,” is painted in bold yellow lettering on the aircraft’s exterior. The other, “Tangerine,” was discovered later, scrawled somewhere inside the fuselage.It’s unclear how much longer Kellner will need to make his dream of flying the Desert Rat a reality. The task seems like a daunting one for someone working part-time on a shoestring budget but then again, few would have likely predicted he would have made it this far to begin with. You can keep up with all of Kellner’s progress by
following his official Facebook page here
.

Feature
The Maid Who Restored Charles II
In 1659 the restoration of the exiled Charles II seemed impossible. It might not have occurred at all but for the forgotten intervention of a blacksmith’s daughter.
Anna Keay
| Published in
History Today
Volume 72 Issue 4 April 2022
I
n the early months of 1660 the taciturn West Country soldier George Monck held the fate of the British Isles in his hands. Oliver Cromwell was dead and the British republic had descended into chaos. The army and its leaders had ousted his son, Richard, and – once again – marched Members of Parliament out of their chamber in Westminster before bolting the door. Monck had been watching at a distance as army chief of Scotland. In the ensuing game of military and strategic chess, played for the future of the nation, he intervened as few had done before or since. Declaring his support for the expelled parliament, he marched south.
Monck enabled the MPs to return but, having done so, those parliamentarians then instructed him to arrest prominent London citizens and emasculate the city. He faced a stark choice. Would he carry out these orders, with which he bitterly disagreed, at the command of the ‘Rump’ Parliament? Would he reinstate Richard Cromwell as Lord Protector or take control by slipping into those shoes himself? Or would Monck do the unthinkable and make contact with the exiled Stuart, Charles II?
The question of how and why George Monck made the choices he did – resulting in the return of the monarchy on terms almost unchanged from those it enjoyed before its abolition in 1649 – has been long debated. That had certainly not been his original intention. How and when was his mind changed? Was it Charles Stuart and his agents or the Parliamentary leader Arthur Haselrige? Was it his disgust with fellow army officers or the intervention of the retired hero of the New Model Army, Thomas Fairfax?
In fact, the person who won George over was his wife, Anne. This remarkable woman has not been the subject of a biography and, unlike 60,000 other figures, she does not even have an entry in the
Dictionary of National Biography
. Yet without her influence the course of British history would have been entirely different.
Love in a hopeless place
Anne Monck met her future husband in the least promising circumstances: the dank chambers of the Tower of London in the mid-1640s. George Monck was a prisoner, she the laundry maid or seamstress who washed and repaired the inmates’ clothing. Though George was a detainee, Anne was still many rungs below him on the social ladder. He was the 37-year-old son of a Devon knight. She was the daughter of a Soho blacksmith in her mid-20s. Their characters were also different. He was serious and uncommunicative, ‘the most reserved man alive’. She had a lively forthright manner that displeased many but captivated him.
As a soldier of the royal army George had been captured by the parliamentary forces at the Battle of Nantwich in 1644. He was thought worth retaining and so was sent to the Tower, where he whiled away long hours writing a manual of military discipline. What relief Anne’s visits gave him and exactly what transpired between them is lost to history. But from that time on he ‘never cast an amorous glance upon any other woman’.
General George Monck, duke of Albemarle, after Michael van der Gucht. Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection. Public Domain.
George Monck was released from the Tower on the condition that he join his former opponents. He did so without hesitation, having fought for the king as a career soldier rather than from any ideological fervour. When he left London, Anne went with him. In the remaining years of the Civil War George’s abilities saw him promoted, rising up the ranks as the New Model Army fought on to victory. When moderate MPs were purged from Parliament and Charles I was tried and executed by an army-backed minority, the Moncks voiced no protest.
In 1653 Anne gave birth to a son named Christopher. A furtive wedding took place in the early months of the pregnancy in St George’s Church, Southwark, at which only the couple’s Christian names were entered in the parish register. There was a good reason for such secrecy: Anne Clarges was already married, betrothed in her teens to haberdasher Thomas Radford. He was from Derbyshire but had been apprenticed in London and kept a shop at the New Exchange. From here, Anne had plied her trade as a seamstress, which had taken her to the Tower of London. As the Moncks’ relationship was sealed, the Radfords’ disintegrated. It was later claimed that Thomas had died, though when evidence was sought in the burial registers none could be found. Instead, Radford had, it seems, been induced to leave London.
Bigamy was a serious crime, punishable by death, so the risk George and Anne ran was colossal. Monck would later remark of his intervention in national politics that it was better to chance death in the jaws of a lion than to be slowly

data.title: Ensloppification
data.author: treadump
data.article_summary: 本文作者自称为AI路德派（AI Luddite），反对当前对AI技术的盲目崇拜和快速推广。作者批评了反AI人士的无知和AI拥护者的盲目乐观，认为两者皆为反智表现。作者引用了Declan Chidlow的《建议合理的AI批评》一文，认同其理性讨论的观点，但表示自己不会遵循这种“合理批评”，因为自己有明确的反对AI的立场。作者担心AI技术的推广会导致职业技能的贬值（deskilling），并对大科技公司（Big Tech）急功近利的做法表示不满，认为AI的快速应用忽视了技术成熟和人类创造力的重要性。最终，作者表示不愿参与这种被大公司主导的AI未来，宁愿放弃现有特权寻找其他出路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI技术（特别是生成式AI）在创意产业（如网页开发和艺术设计）中影响的看法和争议。

不同观点：
• **[suprjami的观点]**：认为AI生成内容（如网页设计）会导致市场缩小，并影响创意产业的未来发展。他指出，虽然高端手工创意网站仍有市场，但整体市场需求已经减少。他还担心如果AI生成内容成为主流，网络开发可能会停滞不前，创意多样性会减少，未来网络创新的潜力也会受到限制。此外，他批评了一些AI支持者对批评的简单回应，如“刀子也有害处”这种类比，认为不具说服力。

• **[bitpush的观点]**：表达了对AI介入创意工作的强烈反感，认为AI工具缺乏人手的温度和情感，使用这些工具会让他失去创作的快乐和成就感。他强调了自己对传统手工艺的热爱，并表示宁愿放弃现有职业，也不愿意成为一个“提示艺术家”或“图形操作员”。他对AI生成内容的体验是负面的，尤其是图像生成让他感到抑郁，暗示AI工具可能对艺术家的精神健康有负面影响。

• **[absurdo的观点]**：对反AI的言论持批评态度，认为那些反对AI新工具的人只是因为不喜欢新事物而在没有充分理由的情况下反对。他认为没必要为不喜欢AI找各种理由，直接承认不喜欢就可以了，而不必借用像Doctorow等人的观点来强化自己的立场。他主张接受技术进步，并指出有些人确实喜欢和欣赏AI生成内容。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：AI生成内容对创意产业的影响，尤其是它是否会导致创意枯竭和市场缩小。suprjami和bitpush都表达了对AI的担忧，而absurdo则批评反AI言论缺乏原创性和理性基础。

• **重要论据和例子**：
  - suprjami提到AI生成网站可能导致网络开发停滞，特别是创新性网络版本（如“web 4.0”）的出现受阻。
  - bitpush强调传统手工艺术的情感价值和AI工具的冷漠感，并提到AI图像生成对他的负面心理影响。
  - absurdo认为不喜欢AI不需要复杂理由，直接承认即可，并批评反AI言论的追随者只是为了迎合特定群体。

通过这些观点，可以看出人们对AI在创意产业中的角色持有不同的态度，有人担忧其负面影响，有人则认为应接受技术进步。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：AI生成内容对创意产业的影响，尤其是它是否会导致创意枯竭和市场缩小。suprjami和bitpush都表达了对AI的担忧，而absurdo则批评反AI言论缺乏原创性和理性基础。

• **重要论据和例子**：
  - suprjami提到AI生成网站可能导致网络开发停滞，特别是创新性网络版本（如“web 4.0”）的出现受阻。
  - bitpush强调传统手工艺术的情感价值和AI工具的冷漠感，并提到AI图像生成对他的负面心理影响。

通过这些观点，可以看出人们对AI在创意产业中的角色持有不同的态度，有人担忧其负面影响，有人则认为应接受技术进步。

data.author: flashblaze
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了对Linear应用的同步引擎（LSE）进行逆向工程以供学习的过程，并得到了Linear CTO的认可。LSE是一种用于协作软件的同步引擎，支持实时编辑、离线可用、文件历史记录等功能。文章对比了操作转换（OT）和无冲突复制数据类型（CRDTs）两种技术，指出了它们的优缺点，并阐述了LSE如何在复杂性、功能性和开发者体验之间取得平衡。LSE支持任意数据模型、部分同步、权限控制、撤销/重做等功能，并通过直观的API简化开发。文章详细解析了LSE如何定义模型、使用MobX实现模型观察、引导启动、构建本地数据库、同步客户端与服务器，以及处理撤销和重做等机制。此外，文章还提及了一些现成的同步解决方案如ElectricSQL和ZeroSync，供读者参考。

My friends found this too long, so I wrote a summary highlighting the key points—making it a 10-minute read. If you're only interested in the main ideas or want to skip the implementation details, just read the summary.
Reverse Engineering Linear's Sync Engine: A Detailed Study
Join in
discussion
.
I work on collaborative softwares, focusing on rich text editors and spreadsheets.
Collaboration engines
, also known as
data sync engines
, play a pivotal role in enhancing user experience in these softwares. They enable real-time, simultaneous edits on the same file while offering features like offline availability and file history. Typically, engineers use
Operational Transformation (OT)
or
Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)
to build sync engines. While these technologies are effective for editors and spreadsheets, they may not be ideal for other types of applications. Here's why.
OT is widely adopted but notorious for its complexity. This complexity stems from the need to account for diverse data models and operation sets across different applications, which requires significant effort to implement correct operations and transformation functions. While OT excels at synchronizing edits, preserving user intent, and handling conflicts, its complexity often makes it overkill for simpler use cases—such as managing user information or file metadata—where a straightforward
last-writer-wins
approach might suffice.
CRDTs, on the other hand, appear more user-friendly. They offer built-in support for fundamental data structures (e.g., texts, lists, maps, counters), reducing the workload for developers. However, CRDTs often introduce metadata overhead and become challenging to manage in scenarios involving partial syncing or permission controls—such as when users can only access a subset of files. These issues arise because CRDTs are primarily designed for decentralized systems, while most modern applications still depend on centralized servers. Although I am personally an advocate of CRDTs, they often fall short for some use cases.
What I look for in a sync engine includes:
Support for arbitrary data models
: Making it adaptable to a wide range of scenarios.
Rich features
: It should support partial syncing, enforce permission control, and include features like undo/redo, offline availability, and edit history.
Great developer experience
: Ideally, it should allow model definitions in an ORM-like manner. Developers should not need to be experts in sync engines to build collaborative applications.
Linear
's Linear Sync Engine (LSE) provides an elegant solution to all the aforementioned requirements. Moreover, it offers an intuitive API that abstracts away the underlying complexity, making feature development significantly simpler. For instance, updating the title of an issue can be as straightforward as:
issue
.
title
=
"New Title"
;
issue
.
save
(
)
;
I believe LSE is exactly what I've been looking for, so I decided to reverse-engineer its frontend code to understand how it works. Additionally, I'm documenting my findings to help others who are interested as I am.
Note
Good References
This
gist
introduces some off-the-shelf solutions, such as ElectricSQL and ZeroSync (which, BTW, I am also very curious about), for general-purpose synchronization. You might want to check them out as well.
In this post, we will explore how LSE:
Defines models, properties, and references.
Uses
MobX
to make models observable.
Performs
bootstrapping
.
Builds and populates a local database (IndexedDB).
Hydrates lazily-loaded data.
Syncs clients with the server.
Handles undo and redo.

data.title: Anthropic launches a voice mode for Claude
data.author: kordlessagain
data.article_summary: Anthropic 为其 Claude 聊天机器人应用推出了“语音模式”（目前为测试版），允许用户通过语音进行对话，并在屏幕上显示要点和对话总结。该功能默认由 Claude Sonnet 4 模型驱动，用户可在忙碌时通过语音与 Claude 互动，例如让其总结日程或搜索文档。语音模式支持五种不同语音选择，并可自由切换文本和语音。不过，语音对话计入使用限制，免费用户预计可进行 20-30 次对话，而付费用户可使用更多功能，如连接谷歌日历和 Gmail。Anthropic 还在与亚马逊和 ElevenLabs 等公司探讨未来语音功能的合作。

44116535.article_content:
Anthropic has begun to roll out a “voice mode” for its Claude chatbot apps.
The voice mode (in beta for now) allows Claude mobile app users to have “complete spoken conversations with Claude,” and will arrive in English over the next few weeks, according to Anthropic’s
official account on X
and
updated documentation
on the company’s website.
At least
one user on X
reports having gained access to voice mode late Tuesday. By default, it’s powered by Anthropic’s
Claude Sonnet 4
model.
“Voice mode … enables you to speak to Claude and hear responses through voice, making it easier to use Claude when your hands are busy but your mind isn’t,” reads a
support page
. “Voice mode transforms how you interact with Claude by … displaying key points on-screen as Claude speaks [and] allowing you to speak to Claude and hear Claude’s voice responses.”
We're rolling out voice mode in beta on mobile.
Try starting a voice conversation and asking Claude to summarize your calendar or search your docs.
pic.twitter.com/xVo5VHiCEb
— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI)
May 27, 2025
A number of AI companies, including OpenAI, offer voice chat experiences for their respective chatbots. Google, for example, has
Gemini Live
, while xAI has Voice Mode for Grok. Each lets users interact with bots by speaking instead of typing, making conversations feel more natural and intuitive.
With Anthropic’s flavor of voice mode, users can chat about things like documents and images, and choose from five distinct voice options. Users can also switch between text and voice on the fly, and see a transcript and summary following conversations.
The capability has certain limits. Voice conversations count toward regular usage caps — Anthropic says that 20-30 conversations is what most free users can expect. Moreover, only paid Claude subscribers can take advantage of a Google Workspace connector that allows voice mode to access Google Calendar appointments and Gmail emails (Google Docs integration is exclusive to Claude Enterprise plans).

data.title: Why Writing by Hand Is Better for Memory and Learning
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了手写对记忆和学习的积极影响。研究表明，与打字相比，手写笔记能够激活大脑中更多的区域，包括运动、视觉和感官处理等，从而增强记忆和学习效果。手写迫使学生在记录时进行信息处理和优先排序，而不仅仅是机械地打字。这有助于学生更好地理解和吸收新知识。此外，手写过程中，运动系统与感官系统的结合能够强化概念和图像的联系，进一步帮助记忆。研究还指出，手写对儿童学习字母和区分相似字母尤为重要。总体而言，手写通过多重感官参与提高了学习效果。
