Why Writing by Hand Is Better for Memory and Learning
Engaging the fine motor system to produce letters by hand has positive effects on learning and memory
By
Charlotte Hu
edited by
Lauren J. Young
Studies continue to show pluses to writing by hand.
Image Source/Getty Images
Handwriting notes in class might seem like an anachronism as smartphones and other digital technology subsume every aspect of learning across schools and universities. But a steady stream of research continues to suggest that taking notes the traditional way—with pen and paper or even stylus and tablet—is still the best way to learn, especially for young children. And now scientists are finally zeroing in on why.
A recent study in
Frontiers in Psychology
monitored brain activity in students taking notes and found that those writing by hand had higher levels of electrical activity across a wide range of interconnected brain regions responsible for movement, vision, sensory processing and memory. The findings add to a growing body of evidence that has many experts speaking up about the importance of teaching children to handwrite words and draw pictures.
Differences in Brain Activity
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
The new research, by Audrey van der Meer and Ruud van der Weel at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), builds on a foundational
2014 study
. That work suggested that people taking notes by computer were typing without thinking, says
van der Meer
, a professor of neuropsychology at NTNU. “It’s very tempting to type down everything that the lecturer is saying,” she says. “It kind of goes in through your ears and comes out through your fingertips, but you don’t process the incoming information.” But when taking notes by hand, it’s often impossible to write everything down; students have to actively pay attention to the incoming information and process it—prioritize it, consolidate it and try to relate it to things they’ve learned before. This conscious action of building onto existing knowledge can make it easier to
stay engaged and grasp new concepts
.
To understand specific brain activity differences during the two note-taking approaches, the NTNU researchers tweaked the 2014 study’s basic setup. They sewed electrodes into a hairnet with 256 sensors that recorded the brain activity of 36 students as they wrote or typed 15 words from the game Pictionary that were displayed on a screen.
When students wrote the words by hand, the sensors picked up widespread connectivity across many brain regions. Typing, however, led to minimal activity, if any, in the same areas. Handwriting activated connection patterns spanning visual regions, regions that receive and process sensory information and the motor cortex. The latter handles body movement and sensorimotor integration, which helps the brain use environmental inputs to inform a person’s next action.
“When you are typing, the same simple movement of your fingers is involved in producing every letter, whereas when you’re writing by hand, you immediately feel that the bodily feeling of producing A is entirely different from producing a B,” van der Meer says. She notes that children who have learned to read and write by tapping on a digital tablet “often have difficulty distinguishing letters that look a lot like each other or that are mirror images of each other, like the b and the d.”
Reinforcing Memory and Learning Pathways
Sophia Vinci-Booher
, an assistant professor of educational neuroscience at Vanderbilt University who was not involved in the new study, says its findings are exciting and consistent with past research. “You can see that in tasks that really lock the motor and sensory systems together, such as in handwriting, there’s this really clear tie between this motor action being accomplished and the visual and conceptual recognition being created,” she says. “As you’re drawing a letter or writing a word, you’re taking this perceptual understanding of something and using your motor system to create it.” That creation is then fed back into the visual system, where it’s processed again—strengthening the connection between an action and the images or words associated with it. It’s similar to imagining something and then creating it: when you materialize something from your imagination (by writing it, drawing it or building it), this reinforces the imagined concept and helps it stick in your memory.
The phenomenon of boosting memory by producing something tangible has been well studied. Previous

44141442.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了手写对记忆和学习的积极影响。研究表明，与打字相比，手写笔记能够激活大脑中更多的区域，包括运动、视觉和感官处理等，从而增强记忆和学习效果。手写迫使学生在记录时进行信息处理和优先排序，而不仅仅是机械地打字。这有助于学生更好地理解和吸收新知识。此外，手写过程中，运动系统与感官系统的结合能够强化概念和图像的联系，进一步帮助记忆。研究还指出，手写对儿童学习字母和区分相似字母尤为重要。总体而言，手写通过多重感官参与提高了学习效果。

主要讨论点：Waymo自动驾驶技术的现状与安全性

不同观点：
• 对Waymo的理论支持但实际担忧：[evilsaloon]对Waymo的理念表示赞赏，但实际观察到的问题（如在旧金山收到近600张罚单）让他对这项技术持保留态度。他认为目前的自动驾驶技术尚未达到令人放心的安全水平，宁愿选择虽然有缺陷但更加熟悉的人类司机。

• 对人类驾驶的信任：[evilsaloon]表示尽管人类司机也会犯错，但在驾驶安全性上，他更信任人类，直到自动驾驶技术达到航空级别的安全性。他认为车辆本质上是危险的，需要司机高度谨慎。

• 对自动驾驶礼让行人的肯定与担忧：[evilsaloon]赞赏Waymo车辆对行人的礼让行为，但也担心未来这些限制会被解除，可能导致更危险的情况。

补充讨论：
• 自动驾驶技术的发展阶段：评论中提到目前Waymo自动驾驶技术在现实应用中出现问题，显示出这项技术仍处于发展阶段，尚未达到完全成熟的水平。

• 安全标准的比较：[evilsaloon]以航空安全标准作为对比，强调了对自动驾驶技术安全性的期望和要求。他认为只有达到这种极高标准，才能真正放心使用自动驾驶技术。

• 对车辆本质危险的认知：评论中提到车辆作为高速行驶的金属物体，其固有危险性是自动驾驶技术需要特别关注和解决的问题。

争议焦点：
• 自动驾驶技术的安全性是否已经达到或接近人类驾驶的水平：[evilsaloon]认为目前尚未达到，并对实际应用中的问题表示担忧。

• 未来自动驾驶技术的发展方向：对当前礼让行人等限制的担忧，以及未来可能出现的解除限制带来的潜在危险。

data.title: High-quality OLED displays now enabling integrated thin and multichannel audio
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: POSTECH研究团队开发了全球首款基于像素的局部发声OLED技术，使每个OLED像素能够同时发出不同声音，实现多声道音频输出。该技术在一个13英寸OLED面板上成功展示，适用于笔记本电脑和平板电脑。通过在OLED显示框内嵌入超薄压电激励器，实现了无串扰的像素级音频控制，解决了传统方法中声音定位不准确和设备笨重的问题。该技术可应用于移动设备、电视、汽车、VR等领域，提供本地化音效体验，且无需外部扬声器，保持了OLED的轻薄优势。这项创新有望成为下一代设备的核心功能，提升用户沉浸感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OLED显示屏结合压电元件实现声音发射的技术及其潜在应用和限制

不同观点：
• [layer8] 和 [kragen] 指出，该技术实际上并不是让每个显示屏的像素发出声音，而是通过在OLED面板后安装压电元件阵列（例如3x3或5x4阵列）来实现的，与显示像素无关。此技术利用了声学振动隔离的结构设计。
• [lmpdev] 关注触觉体验，提出该振动是否可以通过触摸感知，并设想将其应用于触觉反馈技术中。
• [teekert] 认为显示屏像素的移动范围有限，无法产生深低音，因此该技术可能在低频声音的表现上存在局限。
• [walterbell] 提出该显示屏是否也可以作为麦克风使用，暗示该技术可能具有双向的声音传输潜力。
• [jtthe13] 对该技术能否产生完整的音频表示怀疑，尤其对于低频音效，认为仍需传统的低音扬声器辅助。
• [chris_engel] 质疑该技术在移动设备中的应用，因为移动设备的屏幕通常由耐用玻璃层保护，可能影响声音的传递。
• [tuukkah] 和 [amelius] 关注如何通过组合多个像素来重现低频音效，并质疑该技术如何实现声音的方向性和独立控制。

补充讨论：
• [steelbrain] 提供了该显示屏产生声音的录音链接，以便其他人验证音频效果。
• [ra120271] 担心振动可能增加显示屏组件的损坏风险，并关注不同屏幕区域如何生成不同的声音源，以实现个性化的声音体验。
• [atoav] 提到该技术可能实现波场合成（wavefield synthesis），通过精确控制多个独立扬声器来重建虚拟声源，提升空间音效的真实性。
• [dedicate] 联想到虚拟现实（VR）应用，认为该技术可以增强沉浸感。

争议焦点：
• 该技术是否真正实现了每个像素独立发声，还是仅通过整体阵列发声。
• 该技术在低频音效表现上的能力及其在实际应用中的有效性。
• 该技术在移动设备和触觉反馈等不同场景下的可行性和潜在问题。

44112149.article_content:
Science News
from research organizations
High-quality OLED displays now enabling integrated thin and multichannel audio
Date:
May 21, 2025
Source:
Pohang University of Science & Technology (POSTECH)
Summary:
A research team has developed the world's first Pixel-Based Local Sound OLED technology. This breakthrough enables each pixel of an OLED display to simultaneously emit different sounds, essentially allowing the display to function as a multichannel speaker array. The team successfully demonstrated the technology on a 13-inch OLED panel, equivalent to those used in laptops and tablets.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
A research team led by Professor Su Seok Choi of the Department of Electrical Engineering at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology) and PhD candidate Inpyo Hong of the Graduate Program in Semiconductor Materials and Devices has developed the world's first Pixel-Based Local Sound OLED technology. This breakthrough enables each pixel of an OLED display to simultaneously emit different sounds, essentially allowing the display to function as a multichannel speaker array. The team successfully demonstrated the technology on a 13-inch OLED panel, equivalent to those used in laptops and tablets. The research has been published online in the journal
Advanced Science.
Visuals Meet Audio: Toward a Multisensory Display Era
While display technologies have evolved with significant advances in resolution, high dynamic range, and color accuracy -- particularly with OLEDs and QD-enhanced displays -- the industry now faces the need for breakthroughs that enhance not only image quality but also the realism and immersion of user experience.
As visual technologies approach maturity, integrating multisensory inputs -- such as seeing, hearing, and touch -- into displays has become a new frontier. Therefore, now displays are no longer passive panels that simply show images; they are evolving into immersive interfaces that engage multiple human senses. Among these, sound plays a critical role: research indicates that audiovisual synchronization accounts for nearly 90% of perceived immersion.
However, most current displays still require external soundbars or multi-channel speakers, which add bulk and create design challenges -- especially in compact environments like vehicle interiors, where integrating multiple speakers is difficult.
OLEDs with Built-in Pixel-Based Sound: A Game Changer
To address this, researchers have focused on integrating advanced sound capabilities directly into OLED panels, known for their slim, flexible form factors. While companies have explored attaching exciters to the back of TVs or bending OLEDs around speakers -- as seen at MWC 2024 by Samsung and OLED panel speaker by LG -- these methods still rely on bulky hardware and face challenges in accurate sound localization.
The core issue is that traditional exciters -- devices that vibrate to produce sound -- are large and heavy, making it difficult to deploy multiple units without interference or compromising the OLED's thin design. Additionally, sound crosstalk between multiple speakers leads to a lack of precise control over localized audio.
Crosstalk-Free Pixel-Based Local Sound Control integrated with real working OLED
The POSTECH team overcame these challenges by embedding ultra-thin piezoelectric exciters within the OLED display frame. These piezo exciters, arranged similarly to pixels, convert electrical signals into sound vibrations without occupying external space. Crucially, they are fully compatible with the thin form factor of OLED panels.
As a result, each pixel can act as an independent sound source, enabling Pixel-Based Local Sound technology. The researchers also developed a method to completely eliminate sound crosstalk, ensuring that multiple sounds from different regions of the display do not interfere with each other -- something previously unattainable in multichannel setups.
Real Applications: Mobile, Tablet, Laptop, TV, Automotive, VR, and Beyond
This innovation allows for truly localized sound experiences. For instance, in a car, the driver could hear navigation instructions while the passenger listens to music -- all from the same screen. In virtual reality or smartphones, spatial sound can dynamically adapt to the user's head or hand movements, enhancing realism and immersion.
Most notably, the technology was successfully implemented on a 13-inch OLED panel, proving its practical scalability and commercial viability. The display delivers high-quality audio directly from the screen, without the need for external speakers, all while preserving the slim and lightweight benefits of OLED.
A Word from the Researcher

data.title: How to Automate Software Engineering
data.author: Tamaybes
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何完全自动化软件工程，指出尽管AI在特定编码任务上表现优异，但目前仍无法完全取代人类工程师。主要问题在于AI缺乏可靠性、长期情境处理能力以及广泛的自主能力。作者认为，当前AI学习算法的效率远不及人脑，但通过大规模数据训练和强化学习可以改善这一状况。自动化软件工程需要结合人类数据训练和定制环境的强化学习，以提升模型的通用能力。然而，当前的强化学习环境过于简单，缺乏真实世界的复杂性，限制了模型的进一步发展。要实现完全自动化，还需要更丰富、高质量的训练环境和数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否能够完全自动化软件工程，以及相关技术和经济影响

不同观点：
• [hnthrow90348765] 认为Mechanize的成立标志着AI发展的巅峰，目标是完全自动化经济活动。然而，即使是如此强大的技术人才，其薪酬和股权激励（1%-2%）仍然显得不足。
• [sublinear] 认为当前软件工程的自动化问题被过度夸大。软件工程不仅仅是解决技术问题，还涉及多个维度，如业务需求和人类沟通。那些可以合理自动化的部分已经被自动化，剩下的代码是独特的，难以复用。
• [dasil003] 对Mechanize的路线图表示怀疑，认为要捕捉人类在工作中的复杂思维和非语言沟通非常困难。软件工程中的直觉和常识是AI难以跨越的鸿沟。
• [ctoth] 提到软件工程师可能会转向管理等较难自动化的职位，但这些职位最终也可能被自动化。同时，对软件工程自动化的速度表示质疑。
• [nitwit005] 对Mechanize所宣称的巨大市场潜力表示怀疑，认为其市场规模估算过于夸张。
• [gerdesj] 直接否定AI在大多数软件工程任务上正在变得更好，认为当前的AI技术并不足以替代人类工程师。
• [rvz] 提到过去已有类似尝试自动化软件工程的创业公司（如builder.ai）失败的案例，认为Mechanize等公司也可能面临相同命运，且自动化软件工程的成本可能远超预期。
• [jes5199] 讽刺地建议记录C-suite高管的日常互动，看看是否能通过模拟来替代他们的工作，暗示高管工作同样难以自动化。
• [jongjong] 认为软件工程的复杂性和经验差异巨大，从初级工程师到高级工程师的技能水平和代码质量有显著差异，自动化难以涵盖所有层次。
• [aurizon] 认为AI可以在某些方面（如fuzzing测试）发挥作用，但最终的复杂问题仍需要人类能力来解决。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI是否能够真正实现软件工程的完全自动化，特别是涉及到人类直觉、沟通和复杂决策的部分。
- 有人质疑Mechanize所宣称的市场规模和自动化速度，认为过去失败的案例表明这一目标难以实现。

44139765.article_content:
How to fully automate software engineering
Ege Erdil, Matthew Barnett, Tamay Besiroglu
May 30, 2025
With every passing month, AI models get better at most tasks that a software engineer does in their job. Yet for all these gains, todayâs models only assist human engineers, falling far short of automating their job completely. What will it take to build AIs that can fully replace software engineers, and why arenât we there yet?
Current AIs present something of a paradox. Their performance on narrow coding tasks already exceeds that of most human software engineers. However, any engineer who has worked with them quickly notices the need to keep AI agents such as
Claude Code
on a very short leash. Despite good benchmark scores and impressive demos, there are clearly core capabilities that human engineers have that our current systems are missing.
Weâve
previously highlighted
some of these shortcomings: lack of reliability, poor long context performance, and overly narrow agentic capabilities, among others. But why are these capabilities missing in AI systems to begin with? We train them on more compute and data than humans have access to in their entire lives, and we can run tens of millions of parallel copies of them, and yet itâs still not enough.
On some level, the answer has to be that our learning algorithms have been and remain
much less efficient
than the human brain. Deep learning skeptics often point to this and say that itâs a sign the entire paradigm is doomed.
We draw a different conclusion.
The bitter lesson
of the past decades of AI research is that handcrafted algorithms perform poorly, and the best algorithms are the ones that are discovered by applying massive amounts of compute for search and learning. This is the principle that drove the pretraining revolution, where scaling up training on massive text datasets allowed models to spontaneously develop powerful meta-learning abilities.
For the past decade of scaling, weâve been spoiled by the enormous amount of internet data that was freely available for us to use. This was enough for cracking natural language processing, but not for getting models to become reliable, competent agents. Imagine trying to train GPT-4 on all the text data available in 1980âthe data would be nowhere near enough, even if we had the necessary compute. In 2025, our situation when it comes to automating software engineering is no different.
The key question now is: what data do we need, exactly?
How software engineering will be automated
There are two powerful tools that have driven AI capabilities in the deep learning era: training on large corpuses of human data and reinforcement learning from various reward signals. Often, combining these two methods produces results that neither method could achieve alone. Neither pure training on human data nor pure reinforcement learning from a random initialization would have been enough to build models as capable as OpenAIâs o3, Anthropicâs Claude 4 Opus, or DeepSeekâs R1.
We expect the automation of valuable occupations such as software engineering to look no different. The roadmap to success will most likely start with training or fine-tuning on data from human professionals performing the task, and proceed with reinforcement learning in custom environments designed to capture more of the complexity of what people do in their jobs. The initial human data will ensure that models are able to start getting useful reward signals during RL training instead of always failing to perform tasks, and the subsequent RL will allow us to turn compute spent on training directly into better performance on the job tasks we care about.
Today, reinforcement learning tends to produce models which are very competent at doing the narrow tasks they were trained to perform, but donât generalize well out of distribution. We think this is essentially a data problem, not an algorithms problem. Just like weâve seen in the past with pretraining, as our RL environments become richer, more detailed and more diverse, our RL optimizers will begin to find models that have more general agentic capabilities instead of narrowly overfitting to the few tasks weâre giving them.
If we do this well, AI models will become capable of the same kind of online learning that humans can do: instead of having to work inside bespoke RL environments with custom graders, we will be able to deploy them in the real world for them to learn from their successes and failures. The most plausible way for models to reach this level of meta-learning skill goes through RL, which will require environments of much greater volume and quality than the ones that are available today.
Unfortunately, todayâs RL environments are rudimentary and offer only a limited set of tasks and tools. To visualize how limited they are, imagine you had to learn how to be a software engineer without internet access, virtual machines or Docker containers, without critical features i

data.title: AI Responses May Include Mistakes
data.author: userbinator
data.article_summary: 这篇文章描述了作者在使用Google搜索IBM PS/2 280型服务器时遇到的困境。他最初的查询结果看似合理，但与实际不符，因为根本不存在PS/2 280型。作者多次尝试查询，发现人工智能（AI）生成的答案经常变化，且多数是错误的“幻觉”答案，如错误的处理器型号、内存容量等。虽然偶尔会得到正确答案，但错误答案往往看起来更可信，可能误导非专业用户。文章提醒读者，AI生成的搜索摘要可能会严重出错，不应轻信，需谨慎对待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和AI搜索结果的准确性、可靠性及用户信任问题

不同观点：
• **[_wire_], [9x39], [rcarmo]** 认为Google的Gemini及其他AI搜索结果存在随意编造信息（confabulation）的问题，尤其在缺乏上下文和准确性的情况下。他们指出AI生成的内容经常不符合逻辑，且可能会误导用户，尤其是在用户不熟悉结果的情况下。

• **[sspiff]** 表达了对身边人过度依赖LLM的担忧，特别是在不适合的任务（如数学计算和事实查询）上使用LLM，但其担忧常常被忽视。这表明在实际生活中，许多人并未充分认识到LLM的局限性。

• **[minimaxir], [hannob]** 强调当前LLM供应商提供的免责声明不足以提醒用户可能出现的错误，呼吁更积极的教育和警示，因为LLM的“幻觉”问题可能永远无法完全解决。

• **[jll29]** 从技术角度解释了LLM的工作原理，指出它们是基于概率的语言模型，而非知识模型，输出结果受伪随机数生成器和“温度”参数的影响。因此，模型并不真正“知道”事实，只是根据词频生成答案。

• **[neilv]** 认为当前的AI技术在一定程度上是“计算式的客厅游戏”，虽然能帮助完成一些任务（如家庭作业），但在质量和版权方面存在问题，尤其对非计算机科学背景的用户可能产生误导。

• **[simianwords]** 提出随着模型的迭代，LLM的准确性在提高，尽管未达到100%的准确度，但已具备一定的实用价值。他认为应在某个准确度阈值上承认LLM的实用性，而不是一味苛求完美。

• **[csomar]** 分享了一个真实案例，展示了Google搜索结果中的错误信息如何误导用户，甚至在与事实明显不符的情况下仍然被信任。

• **[afro88]** 认为Google可能为了节省成本而使用低质量模型生成搜索结果，导致用户信任度下降。

• **[Almondsetat]** 对网络上大量“LLM给出错误答案”的内容感到厌烦，认为这些故事除了重复“不要盲目信任LLM”的常识外，没有建设性意义。

• **[Biganon]** 讽刺AI会随意编造内容来迎合用户查询，即使查询内容是虚构的。

• **[Dwedit]** 指出Duckduckgo和Brave Search的AI生成答案相对更准确，但这是基于更新的搜索结果，表明AI生成内容的质量依赖于基础数据的更新速度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的可靠性和用户对AI的过度信任。许多用户在未充分理解LLM局限性的情况下，过度依赖AI进行事实查询和决策，导致潜在错误传播。
• 技术社区内部对如何警示普通用户LLM的错误和局限性存在讨论，有人呼吁更显著的教育和警示措施。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，AI生成内容的质量和可信度可能依赖于基础数据和模型的更新频率。不同搜索引擎在处理相同查询时可能会有不同的表现。

44142113.article_content:
The other day I wanted to look up a specific IBM PS/2 model, a circa 1992 PS/2 Server system. So I punched the model into Google, and got this:
That did not look quite right, since the machine I was looking for had 486 processors (yes, plural). And it most certainly
did
use Microchannel (MCA).
Alright, let’s try again:
Simply re-running the identical query produces a different summary. Although the AI still claims that PS/2 Model 280 is an ISA-based 286 system. Maybe the third time is the charm?
The AI is really quite certain that PS/2 Model 280 was a 286-based system released in 1987, and I was really looking for a newer machine. Interestingly, the first time the AI claimed Model 280 had 1MB RAM expandable to 6MB, and now it supposedly only has 640 KB RAM. But the AI seems sure that Model 280 had a 1.44 MB drive and VGA graphics.
What if we try again? After a couple of attempts, yet different answer pops up:
Oh look, now the PS/2 Model 280 is a 286 expandable to 128 MB RAM. Amazing! Never mind that the 286 was architecturally limited to 16 MB.
Even better, the AI now tells us that “PS/2 Model 280 was a significant step forward in IBM’s personal computer line, and it helped to establish the PS/2 as a popular and reliable platform.”
The only problem with all that?
There is no PS/2 Model 280, and never was.
I simply had the model number wrong. The Google AI just “helpfully” hallucinates something that at first glance seems quite plausible, but is in fact utter nonsense.
But wait, that’s not the end of the story. If you try repeating the query often enough, you might get this:
That answer is
actually correct
! “Model 280 was not a specific model in the PS/2 series”, and there was in fact an error in the query.
Here’s another example of a correct answer:
Unfortunately the correct answer comes up maybe 10% of the time when repeating the query, if at all. In the vast majority of attempts, the AI simply makes stuff up. I do not consider made up, hallucinated answers useful, in fact they are worse than useless.
This minor misadventure might provide a good window into AI-powered Internet search. To a non-expert, the made up answers will seem highly convincing, because there is a lot of detail and overall the answer does not look like junk.
An expert will immediately notice discrepancies in the hallucinated answers, and will follow for example the
List of IBM PS/2 Models
article on Wikipedia. Which will very quickly establish that there is no Model 280.
The (non-expert) users who would most benefit from an AI search summary will be the ones most likely misled by it.
How much would you value a research assistant who gives you a different answer every time you ask, and although sometimes the answer may be correct, the incorrect answers look, if anything, more “real” than the correct ones?
When Google says “AI responses may include mistakes”, do not take it lightly. The AI generated summary could be utter nonsense, and just because it sounds convincing doesn’t mean it has anything to do with reality. Caveat emptor!

data.title: Simpler Backoff
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何通过使用查找表（lookup table）简化带有指数退避和抖动（jitter）的重试机制代码。初始代码通过循环计算延迟时间并加入随机抖动，而改进后的代码使用预定义的查找表直接列出可能的延迟时间，减少了变量和计算复杂度。这种方法使代码更简洁、易读且易修改，避免了跨循环的逻辑推理和计算错误的风险。文章建议，对于生成少量固定值的场景，应优先使用查找表而不是动态计算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： backoff算法的实现方式及其优化

不同观点：
• **支持算法生成backoff**：
  - [efitz] 建议客户端记住上次的backoff值，通过乘以常数并设置上限来生成新的backoff值，同时建议加入随机值（jitter）以避免客户端同时重试导致服务器过载。还提到服务器端提示（server-side hinting）的有效性，通过返回随机化的重试值来分散重试请求。
  - [yawaramin] 提出使用斐波那契数列作为backoff，认为这种方法在某些场景下比标准的指数backoff更合适。
  - [grg0] 建议使用一个抽象的backoff函数，可以是高阶函数，以提高代码的复用性和灵活性。

• **支持静态查找表**：
  - [unsnap_biceps] 认为在大型项目中，不同服务可能需要不同的backoff策略，倾向于使用算法生成backoff，而不是维护多个查找表。
  - [blensor] 认为原始代码比静态查找表更直观、可读，且更容易调整最大重试次数，查找表在配置和修改上不够灵活。

• **简化backoff实现**：
  - [handsclean] 提供了一个更简化的实现版本，减少了参数化，强调了代码简洁性和可读性。
  - [jpillora] 简单backoff最为有效，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• **其他考虑**：
  - [axeljohnsson] 提到AWS的“自适应重试”（adaptive retries）策略，强调在系统压力下不应增加负载。
  - [jelder] 提出使用迭代器生成器的可能性，质疑Go语言是否支持这种特性。
  - [ChrisMarshallNY] 分享了在Watch应用中的类似实现，强调了随机延迟的必要性。
  - [charcircuit] 认为改变实现方式可能降低代码的可读性，特别是如果新方法并不为团队所熟悉。

争议焦点：
• 不同backoff实现方式的优劣：算法生成与静态查找表的对比，以及实现的复杂性和可读性之间的权衡。
• 对简单backoff和高阶函数抽象的不同偏好。

总的来说，讨论围绕backoff算法的实现方式展开，重点在于如何平衡实现的简洁性、灵活性和对服务器的保护机制。

主要讨论点： backoff算法的实现方式及其优化

不同观点：
• **支持算法生成backoff**：
  - [efitz] 建议客户端记住上次的backoff值，通过乘以常数并设置上限来生成新的backoff值，同时建议加入随机值（jitter）以避免客户端同时重试导致服务器过载。还提到服务器端提示（server-side hinting）的有效性，通过返回随机化的重试值来分散重试请求。
  - [yawaramin] 提出使用斐波那契数列作为backoff，认为这种方法在某些场景下比标准的指数backoff更合适。
  - [grg0] 建议使用一个抽象的backoff函数，可以是高阶函数，以提高代码的复用性和灵活性。

• **支持静态查找表**：
  - [unsnap_biceps] 认为在大型项目中，不同服务可能需要不同的backoff策略，倾向于使用算法生成backoff，而不是维护多个查找表。
  - [blensor] 认为原始代码比静态查找表更直观、可读，且更容易调整最大重试次数，查找表在配置和修改上不够灵活。

• **简化backoff实现**：
  - [handsclean] 提供了一个更简化的实现版本，减少了参数化，强调了代码简洁性和可读性。
  - [jpillora] 简单backoff最为有效，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• **其他考虑**：
  - [axeljohnsson] 提到AWS的“自适应重试”（adaptive retries）策略，强调在系统压力下不应增加负载。
  - [jelder] 提出使用迭代器生成器的可能性，质疑Go语言是否支持这种特性。
  - [ChrisMarshallNY] 分享了在Watch应用中的类似实现，强调了随机延迟的必要性。
  - [charcircuit] 认为改变实现方式可能降低代码的可读性，特别是如果新方法并不为团队所熟悉。

争议焦点：
• 不同backoff实现方式的优劣：算法生成与静态查找表的对比，以及实现的复杂性和可读性之间的权衡。
• 对简单backoff和高阶函数抽象的不同偏好。

总的来说，讨论围绕backoff算法的实现方式展开，重点在于如何平衡实现的简洁性、灵活性和对服务器的保护机制。

data.author: gsundeep
data.article_summary: MCP Defender是一款桌面应用程序，提供对AI应用的自动保护。它通过实时分析AI应用与MCP服务器之间的通信，自动扫描并防御潜在威胁。主要功能包括高级LLM驱动的恶意活动检测、扫描控制和支持用户选择AI提供商。它防范多种安全威胁，如提示注入、凭据盗窃、任意代码执行和远程命令注入。MCP Defender是开源软件，采用Apache 2.0许可证，目前支持Cursor、Claude、Visual Studio Code和Windsurf等应用，并计划增加更多支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将安全功能外包给大型语言模型（LLM）的可行性、安全性及其潜在市场影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• meander_water：对将安全功能外包给LLM持怀疑态度，认为应该通过明确的授权（AuthZ）策略（如Toolhive和Cedar）来管理安全，强调通过SSE代理来确保客户端与服务器之间的通信安全。
• protocolture：认为如果应用程序能被正常输入文件中的指令轻易改变，那么它就不适合生产工作负载，将这种问题比作给wordpress安装“防病毒”插件而不是更新php。
• adithyassekhar：对AI需要防病毒/防火墙的概念表示惊讶和怀疑，同时提到如果这个市场是真实的，自己也想参与其中。
• superb_dev：质疑通过LLM实现的防火墙如何防御提示注入攻击，认为这可能不会比被保护的AI更安全。
• kingwill101：认为这是一个很酷的实验，并提出是否可以使用eBPF在 kernel 层面获得更好的控制。
• userbinator：担心LLM扫描会引入新的攻击向量。
• mmaunder：询问如何拦截本地MCP服务可能发出的各种网络调用和协议，关心该方案是仅支持远程MCP还是可以在客户端和进程之间工作。
• jdorfman：询问是否支持其他未列出的MCP客户端。
• insin：向grok询问当前情况是否可疑。
• lofaszvanitt：认为提示注入只是荒谬的表演，质疑技术进展是否在倒退。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术方案和工具，如Toolhive、Cedar、eBPF等，显示出社区对多种安全实现方式的探讨。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM是否适合用于安全功能，特别是关于提示注入攻击的防御能力和潜在的新攻击向量。
• 市场前景方面，有人对AI安全市场表示怀疑，但也有人表示兴趣，认为可能成为新的商业机会。

data.title: How large should your sample size be?
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了在数据科学中如何确定合适的样本大小，特别是面对大数据集时。Hadley Wickham指出，许多大数据问题实际上可以通过正确的子集或样本解决。文章强调，没有统一的规则来确定样本大小，这取决于多个因素，如总体大小、误差范围和置信水平。

在商业案例中，例如预测“Goatly”公司客户流失率，数据科学家需要从10万个农场中抽样，以运行逻辑回归分析。关键因素包括：
1. **总体大小**：Goatly有10万个农场。
2. **误差范围/置信区间**：可接受的偏差范围，通常以百分比表示。
3. **置信水平**：希望的置信度，通常为95%或更高，视情况而定。

确定样本大小时，需要平衡这些因素以确保样本具有代表性。文章提供了标准公式帮助计算，并指出在商业环境中，95%的置信水平通常足够。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：样本量与总体规模的关系，尤其是在统计推断中的应用，例如性别比例调查和选举投票。

不同观点：
• [lordnacho] 认为样本量与总体规模关系不大，只要样本无偏，小样本也能反映真实的性别比例，比如50%的男女比例，无论总体是1亿还是80亿人。

• [firesteelrain] 支持使用中心极限定理（CLT）来计算所需样本量，认为通过Z分数和置信区间可以得出合理的样本量，并强调理解背后的科学原理有助于解读研究结果，例如为什么某些研究使用300人的样本。

• [potamic] 提出了关于全国性选举的疑问，指出即便在99%置信水平和0.1区间下，100万人的样本量是否意味着每个人是否投票并不重要，因为即使投票率很低，也能代表整体人口。

• [rudebwai] 强调在估计样本量时，选择合适的统计模型是关键，没有这个模型就无法进行样本量估计。

• [roschdal] 没有提供实质性观点，仅回复了数字"42"，可以视为无贡献或调侃。

• [whatever1] 质疑统计学家的样本量选择，认为如果预测错误，统计学家会归咎于样本量不足，以此推卸责任。

补充讨论：
• 样本量计算的科学依据，特别是中心极限定理的应用，是一个重要讨论点。
• 关于选举中的样本量和投票代表性的讨论，引发了对统计结果与实际民主过程之间关系的思考。
• 争议焦点在于样本量是否足以反映总体特征以及统计模型选择的重要性。

44113847.article_content:
How large should your sample size be?
Aug 4 2015
I read a recent interview with
Hadley Wickham
. Two things stood out to me.
The first is how down-to-earth he seems, even given how well-known he is in the data science community.
The second was this quote:
Big data problems [are] actually small data problems, once you have the right subset/sample/summary. Inventing numbers on the spot, I’d say 90% of big data problems fall into this category.
##The technical side of sampling
Even if you don’t have huge data sets (defined for me personally as anything over 10GB or 5 million rows, whichever comes first), you usually run into issues where even a fast computer will process too slowly in memory (especially if you’re using R). It will go even slower if you’re processing data remotely, as is usually the case with pulling down data from relational databases (I’m not considering Hadoop or other NoSQL solutions in this post, since they’re a different animal entirely.)
In the cases where pulling down data takes longer than running regressions on it, you’ll need to sample.
But how big a sample is big enough? As I’ve been working through a couple of rounds of sampling lately, I’ve found that there’s no standard rule of thumb, either in the data science community or in specific industries like healthcare and finance. The answer is, as always,
“It depends.”
.
Before the rise of computer-generated data collection, statisticians used to have to work up to a large-enough sample. The question was, “I have to collect a lot of data. The process of collecting data, usually through paper surveys, will take a long time and be extremely expensive. How much data is enough to be accurate?”
Today, the question is the opposite: “How much of this massive amount of data that we’ve collected can we throw out and still be accurate?”
That was the question I was trying to answer a couple weeks ago when I was working with a SQL table that had grown to 1+ billion rows.
The business side of sampling
To understand the relationship between an entire population and a subset, let’s take a step back to see why someone might ask.
Let’s say you’re the data scientist at a start-up - Goatly - that sells artisanal handcrafted medicine boxes monthly to owners of narcoleptic goats (
this is a real thing and I could watch this video over and over again
.
Goatly has ~ 100,000 farms already in your system (who knew America had a narcoleptic goat problem?) and the CEO wants to buy a share in a private jet, so she needs the company to keep growing very quickly. A startling number of goats get much better after taking your medicine and hence, the farm leaves your service. The CEO needs you to figure out what makes these goats better and see if you can predict how many farms will be the next to leave, and as a result, how much business she needs to replace them.
You think you might be able to use
logistic regression
to predict whether the farm will cancel Goatly (number of goats, size of goats, color of goats, how much of the pills they buy in a month, how many pills they use in a month, ratio of narcoleptic to regular goats, etc.) But when you try to run the regression on the entire data set, it fails because it’s simply too much.
So you need to sample. How many farms do you need to pick to make sure that they accurately represent the total population of farms? There are some smaller farms, some larger farms, some farms with more narcoleptic goats, some farms where the farmers are more aggressive in giving the goats the medicine, etc. If you pick the wrong sample, it won’t be the same as the population, and then all the tests you plan to do later will fail.
Determining sample size
Here’s the standard equation
used to calculate error. It’s often the precursor to testing the power of a test (that is, if this equation works in your favor, then you can use power of a test to figure out whether logistic regression or most other tests you use actually work on your sample). More on that at the bottom of the post.
You need to know:
Population size - The entire population you’re sampling (in our case, 100,000.)
Margin of error/confidence interval - How far away are you willing to be from the population statistic?
Confidence level - How confident do you want to be that your sample statistic (the mean, for example) matches your population?
The two things you have to pass judgment on are:
how large you want your
confidence level
to be: i.e. do you want to be 90% sure that you found all the farms that will cancel Goatly and leave your CEO traveling coach with the peons? 95% or 99%? In settings where you’re dealing with medical data, you want this to be 99%. Elsewhere, 95%, or even 90%, depending on what you’re doing is good enough. I asked around the
Data Science Slack
and the general consensus was most business settings can do with 95%, again, depending on context.

data.title: Identifying Unmarked Iron
data.author: lelandfe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了无标识铸铁炊具的识别和背景。文章指出，许多18至19世纪的小铸造厂生产的无标识炊具常通过底部浇口标记来识别。由于这些铸造厂通常只服务于小市场，因此未在产品上标注制造商信息。20世纪的一些无标识铸铁炊具多为商店品牌或由主要铸造厂生产并通过纸质标签销售，以保持主产品线的品牌价值。尽管这些无标识炊具大多不被视为收藏品，但它们通常质量优良，适合日常使用，且价格低于有标识的同类产品。文章还详细描述了伯明翰火炉及范围公司（Birmingham Stove & Range Co.）生产的一些典型无标识炊具及其特征。

Identifying Unmarked Iron
Preface
Before we start, it's important to note that what collectors call "unmarked" ware does not necessarily pertain to just any piece which simply has no markings. Many small foundries of the 18th and 19th centuries put no markings as to maker on their pieces. Perhaps they only served a small market, everyone they supplied knew the maker, and that was sufficient.
It is likely that much of what those small foundries made was the result of copying other makers' wares, and who made what and copied from whom was better left unspoken. The identification of older unmarked pieces, particularly those with bottom gate marks, remains one of the most-often-asked questions in vintage cast iron cookware collecting. Sadly, the answer is almost always, "We'll never know."
But there is a category of unmarked pieces that we can identify, so let's continue with those.
Unmarked 20th Century Cast Iron
Part of the allure of vintage cast iron cookware, besides the fineness of the castings, are the unique trademarks and detail work the foundries of the past cast into each piece they produced. Pattern makers were both skilled craftsmen and artists, in some cases even carving small, unique figures ("maker's marks") into their work to identify themselves. There are instances, however, where the parentage of some 20th century cast iron ware seems mysteriously unclear.
Much of what's known to collectors as "unmarked" cast iron has quite a bit to do with marketing. In addition to store brands, like those made for companies such as Sears Roebuck and Montgomery Ward, several major foundries produced unmarked versions of their goods for sale in hardware, department, and building supply stores. As such, these no-name pieces could be sold at a lower price without sacrificing the brand image and value of their main product lines.
Product differentiation in the various channels was achieved by the use of paper labels affixed to the unmarked iron. A couple of manufacturers actually made the decision at some point to cast all of their pieces without inscribed trademarks, instead relying totally on the adhesive labels.
What's interesting about unmarked pieces is they are typically on par with if not equal to the quality of their marked counterparts. While the majority are not considered collectible, per se, they can represent excellent value as "user" pans, and can usually be obtained at a fraction of the price of comparable fully-marked ones.
Here are some unmarked pieces you're likely to see, and information on how to identify who made them and when. Some of them actually enjoy collectible status. Bear in mind that, as with marked pieces, transitions between designs did not necessarily occur abruptly, so all dates given are generalizations. The characteristics described apply to skillets unless otherwise noted.
Descriptions using clock face terms for marking positions assume viewing of bottom of pan with handle pointing downward.

data.title: C++ to Rust Phrasebook
data.author: wcrichton
data.article_summary: 《C++ to Rust Phrasebook》是一本帮助C++程序员学习Rust的书，提供了常见C++模式到Rust习惯用法的转换，通过具体代码示例和工程权衡的高层次讨论进行讲解。本书支持随机访问，适合在编写Rust代码时遇到困惑的情况下查阅。由布朗大学认知工程实验室的专家编写，确保信息的准确性和适度细节，所有内容均为人工撰写，无AI生成。适合有一定Rust基础的读者，也可以作为嵌入式系统程序员的补充资料。读者可以提交反馈或参与问卷调查，帮助改进书籍内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++与Rust的语言比较及其实践差异

不同观点：
• jpc0 认为该指南没有充分展现C++的现代特性，例如在类/结构中使用匿名枚举，以及C++中同样支持模块等特性，而指南却忽略了这些。他还指出，Rust在某些方面的便利性（如模块和FFI）并没有宣传的那么好，尤其是在处理图形等特定领域时，C++尽管需要额外的编译器标志或重写代码，但在某些场景下仍然更具优势。
• EliRivers 提到了一种常见的误区，即用C语言的思维方式去写C++代码，比如使用init()函数而不是构造函数。他进一步探讨了C++程序员在写Rust代码时可能遇到的“陷阱”，即直接套用C++的思维方式可能并不适合Rust。
• Animats 强调了Rust中的traits与C++中的类有本质区别，Rust的traits不包含关联数据，且不能访问父traits的数据，这使得在Rust中进行面向对象编程变得困难。此外，他指出指南中没有提及Rust的所有权机制，并解释了Rust处理错误的常见方式。
• amelius 认为Rust代码在多数示例中显得更冗长。
• npalli 提出了一种逆向思维，即通过学习Rust的优点来改进C++代码。
• 90s_dev 表示会利用该指南同时学习Rust和C++，并比较两者的优劣。
• leoh 对该指南表示高度赞赏。

补充讨论：
• jpc0 和 EliRivers 的观点形成了一种对比：jpc0 更关注C++被低估的现代特性，而EliRivers 则关注如何避免在Rust中错误地应用C++的惯用语法。
• Animats 的评论补充了jpc0 和 EliRivers 的讨论，特别指出了Rust与C++在数据结构连接和所有权机制上的核心区别。
• amelius 的简短评论提供了一个对Rust代码风格的直接观察，即在某些情况下可能更冗长。
• npalli 提供了一种实用主义的视角，即从Rust中学习并改进C++，而不是单纯比较两者优劣。
• 90s_dev 的评论展示了初学者对两种语言的学习态度，而leoh 的评论则是一种总体上的正面评价。

争议焦点：
• C++与Rust在现代特性上的对比，特别是C++被忽视的优点（如模块和编译器标志）与Rust的便利性（如错误处理和FFI）之间的对比。
• 在Rust中直接套用C++的编程惯例是否合适，尤其是在面向对象编程和所有权机制上的不同处理方式。

44140349.article_content:
C++ to Rust Phrasebook
This book is designed to help C++ programmers learn Rust. It provides translations of common C++ patterns into idiomatic Rust. Each pattern is described through concrete code examples along with high-level discussion of engineering trade-offs.
The book can be read front-to-back, but it is designed to be used random-access.
When you are writing Rust code and think, "I know how to do this in C++ but not Rust," then
look for the corresponding chapter in this book.
This book was hand-written by expert C++ and Rust programmers at Brown University's
Cognitive Engineering Lab
. Our goal is provide accurate information with a tasteful degree of detail. No text in this book was written by AI.
If you would like updates on when we add new chapters to this book, you can
drop your email here
.
Other resources
If you have zero Rust experience, you might consider first reading
The Rust Programming
Language
or getting a quick overview at
Learn X in Y Minutes
.
If you are primarily an embedded systems programmer using C or C++, this book is
a complement to
The Embedded Rust Book
.
Compared to resources like the
Rustonomicon
and
Learn Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists
, this book is less about "Rust behind the scenes" and more about explicitly describing how Rust works in terms of C++.
Feedback on this book
At the bottom of every page there is a link
to a form where you can submit feedback: typos, factual errors, or any other issues you spot.
If you answer the quizzes at the end of each chapter, we will save your
responses anonymously for research purposes.
Click here to leave us feedback about this page.

data.title: Learn touch typing – it's worth it
data.author: absoluteunit1
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在计算机科学专业学习期间学习盲打（触摸打字）的个人经历。作者在未获得技术实习机会后，选择了一份体力劳动工作，并在工作之余通过每天短暂的练习提升打字速度。起初，作者的打字习惯不佳，速度和准确率都很低，但通过坚持练习和使用打字应用，逐步提升到40-50字每分钟，且准确率大幅提高。学会盲打后，编程和写作变得更轻松有趣，作者的生产力也显著提高，甚至在技术面试中表现更好。作者还开发了自己的打字应用（TypeQuicker），帮助初学者更有效地学习打字。总体而言，学会盲打对作者的学习和职业发展产生了积极影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：触摸打字的益处、学习方法、不同键盘布局的体验以及是否必要学习触摸打字。

不同观点：
• sdovan1：通过观察同学快速打字受到启发，开始使用10FastFingers和keybr学习触摸打字，最终坚持使用monkeytype和typeracer。虽然不确定是否提高了生产力，但感觉很好。
• danpalmer：两次切换到Dvorak布局，第二次是为了健康原因，最终成功掌握了Dvorak触摸打字。认为切换键盘布局可以摆脱不良习惯，重新正确学习。
• khaki54：曾在八年级时有机会学习触摸打字，但作弊没有学会，现在感到遗憾。
• goku12：认为触摸打字是一项被低估的技能，可以提高生产力，减少眼睛的疲劳。建议程序员、作家、记者和秘书学习。
• michaelsalim：使用分体键盘时被迫学习触摸打字，虽然速度提高不多，但舒适度显著提升。
• NAR8789：好奇不会触摸打字是否普遍，自己从小在电脑上聊天时自然学会了。
• shivbhatia：作为程序员十多年后决定学习触摸打字，使用monkeytype.com，最终打字速度提升到120 wpm，并结合Vim键绑定，使编程体验更愉快。
• tmtvl：使用KDE's Ktouch学习触摸打字，认为Dvorak布局更有趣且有效。现在对速记感兴趣，并推荐typelit工具。
• Ezhik：使用keybr重新训练打字，但对右侧小指负责太多标点符号和键位感到不便。
• john01dav：从小使用电脑，打字速度很快，但不使用传统触摸打字方法。认为经常使用键盘的人会自然学会更好的打字方法，不需要专门教学。
• johan914：Qwerty布局导致自然打字时偏离home row，建议使用其他布局更好地掌握home row打字。
• wenc：打字速度较快，但实际上没有掌握传统的触摸打字方法，感觉home row打字不自然，影响使用Ctrl/Alt和Shift组合键。
• rafadc：推荐免费工具monkeytype和typeracer，认为不需要使用付费网站学习触摸打字。
• kn81198：质疑触摸打字的实际价值，认为在现代编程环境中打字速度不是主要瓶颈，CoPilots和自动补全IDE减少了打字需求。
• BaudouinVH：通过自制Dvorak-fr键盘图片学习触摸打字，最终成功掌握Dvorak-fr布局，并希望学习Bépo布局。

补充讨论：
• 学习触摸打字的动机各不相同，包括观察他人快速打字、健康考虑、提高生产力等。
• 不同键盘布局（Qwerty、Dvorak、Bépo）对触摸打字学习的影响和优劣存在争议。
• 触摸打字的必要性和价值在程序员和现代打字环境中受到质疑，特别是考虑到自动补全工具的普及。
• 免费和付费打字学习工具的推荐和使用体验。

争议焦点：
• 触摸打字是否必要以及其在现代工作环境中的实际价值。
• 不同键盘布局对触摸打字学习的影响和优劣比较。

44141636.article_content:
← Blog
This is a short, personal story about my typing journey
I started learning touch typing near the end of my first year of computer science. This was my second degree as I had already done engineering before.
I wasn't able to get a tech internship the first summer after one year of computer science despite countless applications and thoughtful DMs to recruiters.
I started working for a tiling company as a labourer - it paid well and I'm glad I received this job - it was through a family friend and sometimes a job outside your career path can teach you a lot.
I was working pretty long hours most days and tile work is not easy; most physical trade jobs aren't.
Each morning I made plans to study some programming topic after work to keep my skills up but after coming home from a 10hr+ shift doing tough physical work, all I wanted to do was eat and sleep.
It was very rare that I had the energy to study programming - I didn't have the mental capacity for it.
However, typing practice doesn't require mental capacity. You just turn your brain off, stare at a screen, blast music and type words you see on the screen.
It's like meditation (in a way).
It just takes 10-15 minutes a day to see good results so if I could do it, with my exhausted and beat up hands after
a long day of physical work, then I'm pretty sure most people can find the time and energy to practice daily as well.
Again, it takes very little time to improve.
When I did start learning touch typing, it was brutal at first. I had to change my habits completely.
Without a proper finger placement, my typing was some horrid version of pick-and-peck, look down frequently, etc.
I made so many mistakes while typing as well - accuracy was consistently around 75% and my speed was around 30wpm. I was awful at typing.
I had to look down on the keyboard for any numbers or symbols or even uncommon letters like z or q. Getting in the habit of not looking down is critical by the way -  this is why I hired an illustrator to create visual hand guides for TypeQuicker. You can type out text and look at the indicator instead of looking down at your keyboard.
You can toggle this feature on/off as you progress but it's critical (in my opinion) if you're just starting out typing.
When I had just started learning how to type, I used apps like TypingClub a lot.
Improving my speed was slow progress though.
It took some time but I started to improve and finally reached 30-40wpm with proper finger placement. After some time on TypingClub, I started getting bored with the app -
I wasn't a fan of the forced random games, the ads, the limited stats, lack of custom text, etc. In general, I think their platform is great but it feels like it's tailored to children and not adults.
Regarding limited stats; I wanted to know which character sequences I was struggling with, which words, etc.
I also wanted custom lessons and some other features.
Summer was over and I was back in school - some days I didn't have classes so I dedicated time to building my own typing app.
My favourite youtuber at the time said that you should try to build the things you like to use (for the sake of learning) so I did that.
I decided to build a typing app and that's how this website was born.
So, I continued practicing on TypeQuicker and my speed was averaging about 40-50wpm with much higher accuracy. Accuracy is key - if you type fast but your accuracy is <95%, slow down. You shouldn't be making mistakes. It's killing your speed - mistakes are interrupting the mental flow state.
Now that I was getting better at typing, programming and writing became so much more fun.
My mind could completely focus on the topic; the keyboard became an extension of my brain - I never had to think about it anymore.
It felt liberating as fuck.
It's hard to describe, but once you really go from having struggles on the keyboard, to being fast and competent, it feels almost like the pipe between your brain and your hands has been completely cleaned out
and putting your thoughts into text on a screen becomes an effortless joy.
Not being able to type was like having a constant pain or an ache that you're so used to, you don't think about it nor notice it much. And only once it's gone, you realize how much better you feel!
Another funny thing that happened. Once I was able to type faster, I became more productive and just a better person lol.
I frequently used to procrastinate on replying to people. Emails, messages, etc but now I actually looked forward to it.
I was eager to reply to my co-workers, to my group members in school. Writing code, essays, papers, emails and documenetaion was now something I looked forward to because I could do type it fast!
Also, when I started having coding interviews for internships, (in tech interviews you share your screen with an interviewer and code a solution to a problem as they watch and grill you with questions) I was actually excited because
I could type things out faster - typing fast makes yo

data.title: Most new cars in Norway are EVs. How a freezing country beat range anxiety
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动汽车（EV）在寒冷地区的使用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• seanmcdirmid 认为，在极寒地区（如阿拉斯加、加拿大北部、俄罗斯远东地区），内燃机车（ICE）需要使用引擎加热器或车衣来防止油液和发动机冻结。相比之下，电动汽车（EV）只需在停车时插电保持电池温度，可能更有优势。不过，在-50°C的环境下，热泵可能不太有效。

• asdefghyk 指出，文章未提及寒冷天气下电动汽车的续航损失问题。根据他们的引用，研究表明在-7°C到-1°C之间，电动汽车的续航可能损失高达30%，且车型和电池大小对续航损失有影响。

• asdefghyk 还提到，挪威电动汽车普及的一个主要原因是政府对EV购买和租赁免除25%的增值税（VAT），以及进口税和注册税，这大大降低了EV的售价。

• andsoitis 补充说明，挪威虽然是欧洲最大的石油和天然气生产国，但通过利用化石燃料利润投资于世界上最大的主权财富基金，支持了绿色生活的税收优惠政策。

补充讨论：
• seanmcdirmid 对极寒地区内燃机车和电动汽车的对比，提出了对热泵在极低温下有效性的质疑。
• asdefghyk 通过引用研究数据，强调了寒冷天气对电动汽车续航能力的实际影响，指出了文章未涉及的范围损失问题。
• asdefghyk 和 andsoitis 共同讨论了挪威在推动电动汽车普及方面的政策背景，特别是税收优惠和政府财政支持的关系。

data.title: FLUX.1 Kontext
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: FLUX.1 Kontext是一套生成流匹配模型，支持文本和图像驱动的图像生成与编辑。与传统文本到图像模型不同，它可以通过文本和图像混合提示，理解并修改现有图像的元素，同时保持场景的连贯性。其核心功能包括角色一致性、局部编辑、风格参考和交互速度。用户可以通过简单的文本指令修改图像，无需复杂调整。FLUX.1 Kontext还支持迭代编辑，逐步优化创作，保持高质量和一致性。该套件包括三个版本：[max]（最高性能）、[pro]（快速迭代编辑）和即将推出的[dev]（开放权重版）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FLUX Kontext模型及其相关图像生成和编辑技术的使用体验、技术细节、应用场景以及可能的改进方向。

不同观点：
• [xnorswap] 提到在使用FLUX Kontext进行图像编辑时出现了“上下文滑失”的问题。尽管模型有对话历史，但在编辑图像时却丢失了上下文，把宇宙飞船换成了集装箱船。
• [minimaxir] 对FLUX Kontext的图像生成质量和速度给予了肯定，但也指出在特定风格或细节的编辑上，模型有时会忽略用户的特定要求。
• [vunderba] 对Kontext Apps的专业头像生成质量提出了质疑，表示在使用头像生成应用时，模型将其面部完全替换成了其他人，不过最终的头像质量确实显得专业。
• [vunderba] 还对比了FLUX Kontext与其他模型（如OpenAI的GPT-image-1）的性能，指出FLUX Kontext在图像编辑能力上表现较好，但在严格的文本到图像生成方面仍有差距。
• [sujayk_33] 对当前原生图像生成的多模态特性进行了分析，认为当前一些模型能够更好地结合音频、文本和图像信息，而无需依赖扩散模型。

补充讨论：
• [mdp2021] 提出是否可以输入多张图像进行编辑，例如将一张图片中的元素放入另一张图片中，以实现更复杂的图像生成任务。
• [ttoinou] 对在本地训练和调整FLUX Kontext模型的技术难度提出了疑问，特别是对于没有深厚技术背景的用户是否也能顺利使用。
• [nullbyte] 希望FLUX Kontext模型能在HuggingFace上发布，以供开源社区使用。
• [layer8] 和 [eamag] 分别提到了模型的潜在应用场景（如“增强”图像细节）和生成特定内容（如国际象棋棋盘）的能力。
• [fagerhult] 分享了一个基于FLUX Kontext的简单聊天界面，方便用户使用。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在FLUX Kontext模型在图像编辑中的上下文理解能力以及其在严格文本到图像生成任务中的表现是否能达到行业领先水平（如与OpenAI的模型对比）。

Character consistency

data.title: Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
data.author: jlaneve
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Anthropic公司在其可解释性研究中的最新进展，特别是通过生成归因图来揭示大型语言模型决策过程的方法。该公司开源了这一工具，使研究人员可以追踪模型内部步骤、可视化和分享归因图，并通过修改特征值来测试假设。该工具支持多种开放权重模型，并通过Neuronpedia提供交互式前端探索界面。Anthropic研究员Michael Hanna和Mateusz Piotrowski主导了这一项目，Decode Research则负责Neuronpedia的整合。通过开源这些工具，Anthropic希望促进社区对语言模型内部机制的理解和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Anthropic员工访谈中提到的电路追踪（circuit tracing）工具及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• **Rob-olmos**分享了Anthropic员工Sholto Douglas和Trenton Bricken的访谈链接，并特别提到电路追踪的相关见解。他引用了访谈中的一个例子，说明模型并非直接进行数学运算，而是通过推理得出答案。他还提供了相关资源的链接，鼓励大家查阅。

• **Sanex**表示对Dwarkesh访谈内容感兴趣，并很高兴能够获得相关工具的访问权限，同时提供了Spotify上的讨论链接。

• **Jexp**实践性地提到已经将图形json导入Neo4j，为其他人提供了实际操作的资源链接，方便他人使用和探索。

• **Ofou**对讨论中的工具是否为Garcon（先前已发布的一个工具）或新工具表示疑问，显示出对工具版本和新颖性的关注。

• **Eduard**最初误解讨论内容为PCB（印刷电路板）追踪，表达了一些失望情绪，说明讨论中存在对技术背景的不同预期。

• **Tostino**认为此类电路追踪工具的开源非常重要，能让更多学术界和研究人员参与到可解释性研究中，并预测这种开放性可能带来重要突破，提升模型架构的效率。

补充讨论：
• **Qtwhat**以幽默方式提问，是否通过感谢模型可以获得更好的回答，虽然带有调侃性质，但也反映了部分参与者对模型行为的好奇和期待。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中对工具的理解存在差异，例如Ofou对工具是否为新版本的疑问以及Eduard的误解，显示出信息传递中的模糊性和不同技术背景下的不同期望。

整体来看，讨论围绕电路追踪工具的实际应用、开源意义以及技术细节展开，参与者从不同角度分享了资源、实践经验和个人见解。

Interpretability
Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
May 29, 2025
In our recent interpretability research, we introduced a new method to
trace the thoughts
of a large language model. Today, we’re open-sourcing the method so that anyone can build on our research.
Our approach is to generate
attribution graphs
, which (partially) reveal the steps a model took internally to decide on a particular output. The open-source
library
we’re releasing supports the generation of attribution graphs on popular open-weights models—and a frontend hosted by Neuronpedia lets you explore the graphs interactively.
This project was led by participants in our
Anthropic Fellows
program, in collaboration with
Decode Research
.
An overview of the interactive graph explorer UI on Neuronpedia.
To get started, you can visit the
Neuronpedia interface
to generate and view your own attribution graphs for prompts of your choosing. For more sophisticated usage and research, you can view the
code repository
. This release enables researchers to:
Trace circuits
on supported models, by generating their own attribution graphs;
Visualize, annotate, and share
graphs in an interactive frontend;
Test
hypotheses
by modifying feature values and observing how model outputs change.
We’ve already used these tools to study interesting behaviors like multi-step reasoning and multilingual representations in Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b—see our demo
notebook
for examples and analysis. We also invite the community to help us find additional interesting circuits—as inspiration, we provide additional attribution graphs that we haven’t yet analyzed in the demo notebook and on Neuronpedia.
Our CEO Dario Amodei
wrote recently
about the urgency of interpretability research: at present, our understanding of the inner workings of AI lags far behind the progress we’re making in AI capabilities. By open-sourcing these tools, we're hoping to make it easier for the broader community to study what’s going on inside language models. We’re looking forward to seeing applications of these tools to understand model behaviors—as well as extensions that improve the tools themselves.
The open-source-circuit-finding library was developed by
Anthropic Fellows
Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey. The Neuronpedia integration was implemented by
Decode Research
(Neuronpedia lead: Johnny Lin; Science lead/director: Curt Tigges). Our Gemma graphs are based on transcoders trained as part of the
GemmaScope
project. For questions or feedback, please open an issue on GitHub.

data.title: Learning C3
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary:
本文记录了作者学习C3编程语言的体验。C3是一门基于C语言的现代系统编程语言，提供了诸如模块系统、运算符重载、泛型、编译时执行、语义宏、错误处理、延迟执行（defer）、关联枚举数据等高级特性。作者以实时记录的方式，逐步介绍了C3的基本语法和功能，包括"Hello World"程序、`foreach`循环、`while`循环、枚举与`switch`、结构体、错误处理、契约编程、宏、基本类型属性（如Base64和Hex字面量）、以及如何安装和创建新项目。

作者指出，C3旨在提高C语言的 ergonomics 和性能，同时修复C中的一些问题，如命名冲突和缺乏内置模块系统。C3的语法类似于C，但更明确和现代化，例如使用`fn`关键字定义函数，支持`foreach`循环，并允许格式化打印多种类型。

总体上，C3为C程序员提供了平滑的过渡体验，同时引入了许多有助于提高开发效率的新特性。

44125966.article_content:
2025-05-29 # Learning C3
In this article, I describe my experience learning the
C3
programming language.
I've always been an avid computer programmer. I would say that I am most familiar with low level systems
languages, though I have dipped into other programming languages from time to time. My journey here is
motivated by curiosity. I am always curious to try new programming languages, which has resulted in
learning a dozen or so within the past few years.
With each new programming language I learn, I encounter a never-before-seen paradigm. Each language has
it's own method of expressing ideas, and it's own status-quo for solving problems. I hope to learn what
this means for C3, and what projects I would be likely to use it for.
Here's the disclaimer: I'm writing this article in "real-time", which is to say I am typing it up as I
am learning C3. This means that I may have added insights about pain points and neat features that get
glossed over or forgotten in other articles, yet it may also mean that my explanations and conceptual
grasp of the language is reduced or faulty compared to other sources.
Contents:
What is C3?
Language Overview
Hello World
foreach
loops
while
loops
enum
and
switch
defer
keyword
struct
types
Error handling
Contracts
struct
methods
macro
s
Type Properties
Base64 & Hex Literals
Primitives
Much More
First Steps
Installing C3
Creating a new project
Making a calculator with C3
What will this require?
Getting user input
The tokenizer
The parser
Conclusion
What is C3?
According to the C3 website, C3 aims to build on and with C. It offers ergonomics, optimizations, and
features. Some of these features may be difficult or impossible to express in standard C. These features
include a module system, operator overloading, generics, compile time execution, semantic macros,
an integrated build system, error handling,
defer
, value methods, associated enum data,
distinct types & subtypes, gradual contracts, built-in slices,
foreach
, dynamic calls &
types,
and more
.
Here are two other perspectives on what C3 is:
Thank you to FoxKiana and the C3 creator Christoffer Lernö for replying :)
Language Overview:
It's hard for me to picture what the language is like without clear examples. For this section I will
review the language reference online and share my thoughts on the language features C3 offers. I will
not cover each and every feature of C3, as this isn't meant to be an introduction to C3.
Hello World:
import std::io;
fn void main()
{
io::printn("Hello, World!");
}
Hello world seems pretty straightforward. I can immediately see this reminds me of C, although I
personally prefer having the opening brackets on the same line as the function declaration. In any case,
it's best to follow the status-quo here as it helps you understand other C3 code, and helps other C3
developers understand your code.
Something to note about importing modules - According to the
modules
page
, imports will recursively import submodules. C of course would do the same, and you might
end up needing to deal with name collisions by renaming things deep down the
#include
chain. C3 fixes the name collision issue by requiring you to use a more full case to resolve collisions.
For example, you would use
abc::Context
instead of
Context
if both imported
modules
abc
and
de
have a structure named
Context
.
I find it curious that the language requires the
fn
keyword to define the function here. I
would think that the language could get away with avoiding that keyword like C does. On further thought,
perhaps it is better to be more explicit that this is a function. Some reasons this may be is that the
function declaration syntax could be used elsewhere, or C3 could allow nested function declarations. The
first possibility seems more likely than the second, given that C3 is an evolution of C.
The
standard
print function
will print most types that are passed to it. That seems pretty nice! Definitely a
step-up from C here. I can imagine that
print
debugging works great in this language.
Taking a look at
formatted printing
, it seems that C3 resembles C quite a bit here. For the
printf
function,
%s
is still used for strings,
%d
is still used
for decimals,
%f
is still used for floats. Truly C3 is easing the transition for C
programmers. Something unique to note here - it seems that the string formatter (
%s
) can be
used to format certain non-string types as well - so an enum of type
Heat
with a value of
REALLY_WARM
would format itself as
REALLY_WARM
when you use the
%s
formatter.
foreach
loops:
// Prints the values in the slice.
fn void example_foreach(float[] values)
{
foreach (index, value : values)
{
io::printfn("%d: %f", index, value);
}
}
// Updates each value in the slice by multiplying it by 2.
fn void example_foreach_by_ref(float[] values)
{
foreach (&value : values)
{
*value *= 2;
}
}
Hold up, hold up.
C3 has foreach
? That is interesting. According to the docs,
break
and
continue
work as you would expect. Iteration by refer

data.title: I'm starting a social club to solve the male loneliness epidemic
data.author: nswizzle31
data.article_summary: Wave3 Social是一个为在远程工作时代寻找真实友谊的平台，目前在波士顿、纽约和旧金山推出。它通过新成员混合聚会和专属活动帮助人们建立深厚友谊，活动包括扑克之夜、威士忌圆桌和私人厨师晚宴等。与Meetup.com或Facebook不同，Wave3专注于创建一个有凝聚力的社区，而不仅仅是线上互动。要加入Wave3，需先参加混合聚会，并获得现有成员的邀请。该平台欢迎任何希望建立真诚友谊的人，并鼓励会员带朋友参加活动，以增加互动和活力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：男性孤独感与现代社会中社交联系的缺失及其解决方式

不同观点：
• keiferski 认为，现代社交解决方案往往依赖于应用程序或服务，而过去的社交活动通常发生在具体的物理地点（如咖啡馆、酒吧），这些地点不需要预先计划或依赖技术。
• Multicomp 指出，缺乏深度友谊是多方面的问题，包括社交媒体的公开性、移动性增加导致面对面交流减少、以及现代文化中对真实联系的抑制。
• Telemakhos 希望恢复类似维多利亚时代的“绅士俱乐部”，作为限定性别的社交空间，以促进文明交流和深度联系。
• scoofy 认为纽约市提供了很好的社交机会，并将社交网络的建立归因于社区小商业的存在，而非住宅区划。
• cjohnson318 认为，男性之间的竞争性和不感兴趣的态度是导致缺乏深度友谊的主要原因。
• fiforpg 提出反面观点，认为现代社会仍有大量基于兴趣的社交机会，当前的讨论可能只是一种道德恐慌，缺乏数据支持。

Where have all my deep male friendships gone?
NY Times
Hear why the idea resonates
Paul C
To me this doesn't feel like some cheesy attempt to fix loneliness with tech. It's just creating a space for something that’s clearly missing for a lot of people.
Kyle H
Our grandfathers belonged to a club like this. They've disappeared due to rising individualism, but there's no reason we couldn't start building them again.
Erik C
Love this idea -  definitely miss having a community outside my doorstep for spontaneous things. Thanks for taking the initiative.

FAQ
Why not just use Meetup.com or Facebook?
Because these platforms weren't built for lasting friendships - they lack real curation and are built primarily for engagement, not belonging. Practically speaking, they don't offer the structure, consistency, or cultural focus needed to create a tight-knit, mission-driven community that actually sticks.
How do I join the club?
Start by attending one of our local mixers - open events where anyone can come meet current members and get a feel for the community. If the vibe is right and you're supported by existing members, you'll receive an invitation to join Wave3 as a full member with access to exclusive events and experiences.
What do members get access to?
Once you're invited into Wave3, you unlock access to curated events - everything from small-group hangouts and workshops to bigger socials. These are invite-only, thoughtfully planned, and focused on building real friendships and good times.
Is the club only for a specific type of person?
Not at all. Wave3 is for any guy looking to build solid, meaningful friendships. Whether you're new in town, going through a life shift, or just tired of shallow hangouts - we're here for it. Our only ask is that you show up open and respectful.
How does the invite system work?
After attending a mixer, current members can vouch for new attendees they believe would be a great fit. If you're supported by enough members, you'll get an official invite to join the club. It helps us keep the vibe strong and the community aligned.
Can I bring a friend to events?
Absolutely. In fact, we encourage it. The more energy and openness in the room, the better. Just make sure they're aligned with what we're building - real connection, good vibes, and mutual respect.
Is there a cost to attend?
Mixers are usually free or low-cost to cover venue or food. Once you're a member, some events may have a small fee to help with planning, food, or space - but we keep it accessible and always let you know ahead of time.

data.title: Why incels take the "Blackpill"–and why we should care
data.author: nreece
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了网络上的“非自愿独身者”（incel）亚文化，不仅局限于其极端的反女性言论和暴力倾向，还包括越来越多的人利用这一意识形态作为不工作或不学习的借口。根据发表在《Gender, Work, & Organization》期刊上的一篇论文，这种现象可能是他们应对失败的一种机制，不仅在恋爱方面，还包括教育和就业。

文章还对比了“红药丸”（Redpill）和“黑药丸”（Blackpill）两种不同的意识形态。前者强调自我提升和追求阳刚气质，而后者则更加虚无，认为外貌和基因决定一切，导致对社会的全面脱离。许多incels自称为“NEET”（不工作、不学习、不受培训），并以此为荣。

研究通过分析incels.is平台上的讨论，发现这些主题包括政治/意识形态争论、边界维护、歧视感知以及欺凌和边缘化。研究者提醒，应注意区分不同亚文化群体，以便采取有效的干预措施。文章还指出，关注男性青年面临的困境与关心女性和女孩的福祉并不矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“非自愿独身者”（involuntary celibate）术语的讨论及其背后的社会问题

不同观点：
• hd4认为，“非自愿独身者”这一带有贬义的术语反映了社会中的一种根本性虚伪。言下之意是，这一术语可能被用来嘲讽或贬低那些自认为在恋爱或性方面不顺利的人，而这种贬低本身是虚伪的，可能忽视了这些人所面临的更深层次的社会或心理问题。

• anovikov指出，过去社会中有一个有效的机制来利用这些年轻人的力量，即军队征兵。这种机制不仅能为社会做出贡献，也能为他们提供生活方向。然而，由于“自私的婴儿潮一代”为了避免参战（如越南战争）而取消了这些机制，如今的年轻人失去了这种有价值的途径，可能只能“躺平腐烂”。

补充讨论：
• hd4的观点中隐含了对社会标签和污名化的批评，认为“非自愿独身者”这一术语可能被滥用，而忽视了这些人所面临的结构性问题。

• anovikov则将问题归因于社会制度的变化，特别是征兵制度的取消，认为这种变化剥夺了年轻人通过参与社会机制（如军队）来获得生活意义的机会，从而导致他们陷入无所事事的状态。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于“非自愿独身者”这一术语的使用及其背后的社会现象。hd4质疑的是社会对这一群体的态度和标签化的虚伪性，而anovikov则关注的是社会机制的缺失如何导致年轻人失去方向。

• 另一个争议点在于社会责任的归属问题。hd4隐含地批评了社会对某些群体的偏见和不公正，而anovikov则明确地将责任归咎于特定的世代和制度变化。

总结：评论主要围绕“非自愿独身者”这一术语及其反映的社会问题展开，hd4质疑社会标签的虚伪性，而anovikov则关注社会机制的缺失对年轻人的影响。

The online incel ("involuntary celibate") subculture is mostly known for its extreme rhetoric, primarily against women, sometimes erupting
into violence
. But a growing number of self-identified incels are using their ideology as an excuse for not working or studying. This could constitute a kind of coping mechanism to make sense of their failures—not just in romantic relationships but also in education and employment, according to
a paper
published in the journal Gender, Work, & Organization.
Contrary to how it's often portrayed, the "
manosphere,
" as it is often called, is not a monolith. Those who embrace the "Redpill" ideology, for example, might insist that women control the "sexual marketplace" and are only interested in ultramasculine "Chads." They champion self-improvement as a means to make themselves more masculine and successful, and hence (they believe) more attractive to women—or at least better able to manipulate women.
By contrast, the "Blackpilled"
incel
contingent is generally more nihilistic. These individuals reject the Redpill notion of alpha-male masculinity and the accompanying focus on self-improvement. They believe that dating and social success are entirely determined by one's looks and/or genetics. Since there is nothing they can do to improve their chances with women or their lot in life, why even bother?
"People have a tendency to lump all these different groups together as the manosphere," co-author AnnaRose Beckett-Herbert of McGill University told Ars. "One critique I have of the recent Netflix show
Adolescenc
e
—which was well done overall—is they lump incels in with figures like Andrew Tate, as though it's all interchangeable. There's areas of overlap, like extreme misogyny, but there are really important distinctions. We have to be careful to make those distinctions because the kind of intervention or prevention efforts that we might direct towards the Redpill community versus the Blackpill community might be very different."
Incels constitute a fairly small fraction of the manosphere, but the vast majority of incels appear to embrace the Blackpill ideology, per Beckett-Herbert. That nihilistic attitude can extend to any kind of participation in what incels term "Soyciety"—including educational attainment and employment. When that happens, such individuals are best described by the acronym NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training).
"It's not that we have large swaths of young men that are falling into this rabbit hole," said Beckett-Herbert. "Their ideology is pretty fringe, but we're seeing the community grow, and we're seeing the ideology spread. It used to be contained to romantic relationships and sex. Now we're seeing this broader disengagement from society as a whole. We should all be concerned about that trend."
The NEET trend is also tied to the broader cultural discourse on how boys and young men are struggling in contemporary society. While prior studies tended to focus on the misogynistic rhetoric and propensity for violence among incels, "I thought that the unemployment lens was interesting because it's indicative of larger problems," said Beckett-Herbert. "It's important to remember that it's not zero-sum. We can care about the well-being of women and girls and also acknowledge that young men are struggling, too. Those don't have to be at odds."
“Lie down and rot”
Beckett-Herbert and her advisor/co-author, McGill University sociologist Eran Shor, chose the incels.is platform as a data source for their study due to its ease of public access and relatively high traffic, with nearly 20,000 members. The pair used Python code to scrape 100 pages, amounting to around 10,000 discussion threads between October and December 2022. A pilot study revealed 10 keywords that appeared most frequently in those threads: "study," "school," "NEET," "job," "work," "money," "career," "wage," "employ," and "rot." ("They use the phrase 'lie down and rot' a lot," said Beckett-Herbert.)
This allowed Beckett-Herbert and Shor to narrow their sample down to 516 threads with titles containing those keywords. They randomly selected a subset of 171 discussion threads for further study. That analysis yielded four main themes that dominated the discussion threads: political/ideological arguments about being NEET; boundary policing; perceived discrimination; and bullying and marginalization.
Roughly one-quarter of the total comments consisted of political or ideological arguments promoting being NEET, with most commenters advocating minimizing one's contributions to society as much as possible. They suggested going on welfare, for instance, to "take back" from society, or declared they should be exempt from paying any taxes, as "compensation for our suffering." data.title: Show HN: I wrote a modern Command Line Handbook
data.author: petr25102018
data.article_summary: 《The Command Line is for Everyone》是一本旨在帮助各类用户快速掌握Unix/Linux命令行的手册。无需阅读繁琐的指南，书中通过简明易懂的概念和常用命令帮助读者迅速上手，涵盖终端、shell、命令行应用和脚本编写等内容。书中包含100多个带注释的shell会话和代码示例，帮助读者自信运行命令。该手册经过四年编写和更新，于2025年推出最新版，已有超过5700名读者受益。作者Petr Stribny强调高效使用命令行及各类现代终端程序，提供精美的PDF版本供学习。书籍定价14美元，读者可自行决定支付价格。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一本关于Linux命令行书籍的评价与相关资源推荐

不同观点：
• [对书籍介绍页面信息的建议] mtlynch认为书籍的登陆页面缺乏对读者将学到什么的具体例子，导致无法判断这本书是面向完全初学者还是有经验的bash用户。他建议提供更多具体信息，并指出了页面上的几个小错误。
• [网站技术问题] charlie-83指出网站在移动端有显示问题，并支持提供样页或目录以便了解书籍的详细程度。他还提到不希望选择免费获取后付款的方式。
• [寻找项目或练习资源] swhite237需要为培训非命令行用户的项目或练习资源，认为这本书虽然很好，但缺乏练习项目，难以激励学习者。

补充讨论：
• [提供样页链接] petr25102018提供了Google Drive上的样页链接。
• [推荐其他资源] briandoll推荐了The Shell Haters Handbook，而 rochak推荐了linuxjourney.com作为补充资源。
• [工具选择的焦点] dkarl询问了书籍中工具选择的重点是旧工具还是新工具，或者两者兼有。

Software developers, sysadmins, tech workers, and regular Linux/macOS
users all use the modern Unix/Linux command-line shells to get things
done. What about you?

bibles to get going. Understand the most common concepts and commands

Terminals, shells, command-line applications, and shell scripting.

Run commands with confidence

Fresh out of press

I have been a long-time Linux and command-line user, but I didn't always use the command line to its full potential.

data.title: Beware of Fast-Math
data.author: blobcode
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了编译器选项"fast-math"的危险性，尤其是在追求计算速度时对数学运算正确性的潜在影响。文章解释了"fast-math"在不同编译器中的实现方式，例如GCC和Clang中的`-ffast-math`或`-Ofast`，以及Intel和Microsoft编译器中的类似选项。这些选项通过放宽IEEE 754浮点运算标准的一些规则来加速计算，但可能会导致精度损失和意外错误。

文章具体介绍了几个关键选项，如`-ffinite-math-only`允许假设输入不是NaNs或Infs，从而进行优化，但这可能导致必要的检查被忽略。另一个选项`-fassociative-math`允许改变浮点运算的顺序，这在某些情况下会导致不同的计算误差。

总的来说，文章警告开发者在使用"fast-math"时要谨慎，因为这些优化可能在提升速度的同时引入不易察觉的错误。

44142472.article_content:
Beware of fast-math
Beware of fast-math
One of my more frequent rants, both online and in person, is the danger posed by the "fast-math" compiler flag. While these rants may elicit resigned acknowledgment from those who already understand the dangers involved, they do little to help those who don't. So given the remarkable paucity of writing on the topic (including the documentation of the compilers themselves), I decided it would make a good inaugural topic for this blog.
So what is fast-math?
It's a compiler flag or option that exists in many languages and compilers, including:
-ffast-math
(and included by
-Ofast
) in
GCC
and
Clang
-fp-model=fast
(the default) in
ICC
/fp:fast
in
MSVC
--math-mode=fast
command line option
or
@fastmath
macro
in Julia.
So what does it actually do? Well, as the name said, it makes your math faster. That sounds great, we should definitely do that!
I mean, the whole point of fast-math is trading off speed with correctness. If fast-math was to give always the correct results, it wouldn’t be fast-math, it would be the standard way of doing math.
—
Mosè Giordano
The rules of floating point operations are specified in
the IEEE 754 standard
, which all popular programming languages (mostly) adhere to; compilers are only allowed to perform optimizations which obey these rules. Fast-math allows the compiler to break some of these rules: these breakages may seem pretty innocuous at first glance, but can have significant and occasionally unfortunate downstream effects.
In
GCC
,
-ffast-math
(or
-Ofast
) enables the following options:
-fno-math-errno
,
-funsafe-math-optimizations
,
-ffinite-math-only
,
-fno-rounding-math
,
-fno-signaling-nans
,
-fcx-limited-range
and
-fexcess-precision=fast
. Note that
-funsafe-math-optimizations
is itself a collection of options
-fno-signed-zeros
,
-fno-trapping-math
,
-fassociative-math
and
-freciprocal-math
, plus some extra ones, which we will discuss further below.
Now some of these are unlikely to cause problems in most cases:
-fno-math-errno
[1]
,
-fno-signaling-nans
,
-fno-trapping-math
disable rarely-used (and poorly supported) features. Others, such as
-freciprocal-math
can reduce accuracy slightly, but are unlikely to cause problems in most cases.
Krister Walfridsson
gives a very nice (and somewhat more objective) description of some of these, but I want to focus on three in particular.
-ffinite-math-only
Allow optimizations for floating-point arithmetic that assume that arguments and results are not NaNs or +-Infs.
The intention here is to allow the compiler to perform some
extra optimizations
that would not be correct if NaNs or Infs were present: for example the condition
x == x
can be assumed to always be true (it evaluates false if
x
is a NaN).
This sounds great! My code doesn't generate any NaNs or Infs, so this shouldn't cause any problems.
But what if your code doesn't generate any intermediate NaNs only because it internally calls
isnan
to ensure that they are correctly handled?
— based on
an example from John Regehr
(to explain what this is showing: the function is setting the return register
eax
to zero, by
xor
-ing it with itself, which means the function will always return
false
)
That's right, your compiler has just removed all those checks.
Depending on who you ask, this is either obvious ("you told the compiler there were no NaNs, so why does it need to check?") or ridiculous ("how can we safely optimize away NaNs if we can't check for them?"). Even compiler developers
can't agree
.
This is perhaps the single most frequent cause of fast-math-related
StackOverflow
questions
and
GitHub
bug
reports
, and so if your fast-math-compiled code is giving wrong results, the very first thing you should do is disable this option (
-fno-finite-math-only
).
-fassociative-math
Allow re-association of operands in series of floating-point operations.
This allows the compiler to change the order of evaluation in a sequence of floating point operations. For example if you have an expression
(a + b) + c
, it can evaluate it instead as
a + (b + c)
. While these are mathematically equivalent with real numbers, they aren't equivalent in floating point arithmetic: the errors they incur can be different, in some cases quite significantly so:
julia> a =
1e9
+
1
; b = -
1e9
; c =
0.1
;
julia> (a+b)+c
1.1
julia> a+(b+c)
1.100000023841858
Vectorization
So why would you want to do this? One primary reason is that it can enable use of vector/SIMD instructions:
For those who aren't familiar with SIMD operations (or reading assembly), I'll try to explain briefly what is going on here (others can skip this part). Since raw clock speeds haven't been getting much faster, one way in which processors have been able to increase performance is through operations which operate on a "vector" (basically, a short sequence of values contiguous in memory).
In this case, instead of performing a sequence of floating point additions (
addss
), it is able to make use of a SIMD i

data.title: What's working for YC companies since the AI boom
data.author: jseidel
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YC及AI初创公司的投资与发展趋势

不同观点：
• [xorcist] 认为AI公司通常追求解决通用性高但商业化不成熟的问题，而不是专注于有明确商业需求的细分领域。他以自动驾驶技术为例，指出公司应从资本密集型和特定场景入手，而非直接解决复杂、广泛的应用问题。他还质疑AI公司是否应专注于开发通用软件，而不是在特定领域（如CPU设计或专业软件）中寻找机会。

• [A_D_E_P_T] 对AI初创公司是否合理表示怀疑，指出许多AI初创公司依赖于现有的API（如OpenAI），但当这些大公司推出更成熟的版本时，初创公司往往失去竞争力。他还提到一些特定领域（如法律AI）可能存在机会，但大公司的快速发展让这些机会变得不明显。

• [adamsuskin] 指出在当前环境下，创业者在考虑是否接受风投资金时面临复杂选择，尤其是在公司能够自给自足、不需要大量员工的情况下，创始人可能不急于进行下一轮融资。

• [nkotov] 认为YC的资金增加让初创公司有更多时间验证产品可行性，且由于工具的进步，资金压力也减小，因此不再急于寻求A轮融资。

• [eddythompson80] 讨论了LLM（大型语言模型）相关的工具和垂直领域，认为这些领域仍然在快速变化，且目前仍难以判断哪些公司会成功。他还指出，AI在特定企业场景中可能更有机会。

• [mritchie712] 质疑Reducto（一家文档处理API公司）的独特性，认为其功能可以通过现有的LLM API实现，没有显著的差异化。

• [lubujackson] 认为YC过于狭窄地关注SaaS领域，而忽视了消费级产品。

• [cushychicken] 指出硬件初创公司难以获得VC的支持，因为VC的回报周期与硬件开发所需的长周期不匹配。

• [parsabg] 建议除了A轮融资，还应考虑累计融资额，以更全面地评估公司发展情况，因为有些公司可能通过大额种子轮融资而不急于进行A轮融资。

• [tzury] 认为YC应更多关注客户增长和流失率，而不是单纯依赖融资作为衡量标准，因为投资者的利益不一定与市场需求一致。

• [saubeidl] 批评YC在AI技术没有明确商业价值的情况下大量投资，认为这可能导致失败。

• [hn_throwaway_99] 指出YC公司中获得A轮融资的比例较低，怀疑是否因为VC环境恶化，或者YC的投资策略存在问题。

• [threeseed] 预测许多AI初创公司将在未来两年面临客户流失和生存挑战，并批评YC宣称只投资最优秀创始人的说法，认为这是对多样性和其他背景创业者的忽视。

data.title: Gradients Are the New Intervals
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了图形学研究中利用梯度和Lipschitz连续性来优化复杂模型渲染的方法。作者比较了传统区间算术和基于Lipschitz连续性的单点评估方法，后者通过修剪和远场剔除技术显著提高了渲染效率。具体来说，Lipschitz连续性为距离场的变化提供了界限，使得可以跳过不相关或无效的区域，简化表达式。作者还提到自己的2020年研究也涉及类似优化，但使用的是区间算术。相比之下，单点评估更便宜，且不受区间算术保守性的影响，但要求形状和变换必须是良好行为的。作者最终提出，利用Lipschitz连续性可以通过单点评估实现类似区间的效果，并应用于渲染工具中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于间隔算法和符号距离场（SDF）相关技术的讨论，包括其理论基础、应用及潜在问题。

不同观点：
• Kragen认为该技术实现了他六年前关于间隔光线行进的猜想，并计划仔细研究是否为相同的方法或使用了相同的代数。
• Guyomes指出，类似的思想在1998年被称为Taylor模型，甚至可以追溯到1984年的邻域算术，通过Taylor展开和余项边界进行推广。
• Diabllicseagull提到他曾参与过关于SDF CSG树剪枝和常半径圆角混合的专利，但专利不如期刊有可见度。
• Sfpotter解释了Lipschitz技巧依赖于梯度 magnitude为1的假设，并讨论了单调性间隔包含与Lipschitz性质的关系。
• Yorwba质疑标准化过程是否能确保结果为1-Lipschitz，尤其是对于不太规则的函数，高阶导数可能更重要。
• Ajkjk建议存储实际位移向量而不仅是SDF的 magnitude，认为这样可以简化递归过程，但不确定存储开销。
• 3abiton表示对文章中隐式曲面光栅化及间隔算术的假设不了解，请求简要说明。
• Fph指出间隔的一个优点是能确保结果不受浮点误差影响，但对梯度计算中的取消误差表示担忧。
• Constantcrying反驳文章中关于Lipschitz性质的解释，认为Lipschitz连续性不应与可微性混为一谈。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点包括Lipschitz性质的定义和应用，尤其是其与可微性的关系。
• 不同参与者对间隔算法的具体实现细节及其在SDF应用中的有效性存在不同看法。
• 有人提出专利与学术期刊在可见度上的差异，暗示技术传播中的问题。
• 对如何处理高阶导数及浮点误差的影响也有深入讨论，显示出理论与实际应用之间的差距。

44142266.article_content:
Matt Keeter
// blog
projects
research
blog
about
links
Gradients are the new intervals
At the
New England Symposium on Graphics
,
James Tompkin
compared graphics researchers to
magpies: they're easily distracted by shiny objects and pretty renderings.
While this is true, the analogy also holds from a different angle: when I'm
reading graphics papers, I'm constantly looking for ideas to
steal
bring back to my nest.
Researchers at
IRIT
and
Adobe Research
recently published a
paper
that's
full
of interesting ideas, and I'd like to talk about it.
This blog post assumes a vague understanding of implicit surface rasterization,
and how interval arithmetic is used to both skip regions of space and simplify
complex expressions.
See
this section of the Fidget writeup
for a short
introduction, or
my colloquium talk
for a longer explanation.
Here's the key sentence from the paper's abstract:
We introduce an efficient hierarchical tree pruning method based on the
Lipschitz property of SDFs, which is compatible with hard and smooth CSG
operators.
In this case, "the Lipschitz property" means that the gradient of the distance
value is bounded, e.g. $||\nabla f(x, y, z)|| \lt 1$.  You'll also see it
referred to as
Lipschitz continuity
.
Lipschitz continuity provides a
bound
on the maximum change in the distance
value between two points: if you have points $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$ in 3D
space, then
$$|f(\vec{p}) - f(\vec{q})| \le ||\vec{p} - \vec{q}||$$
Given this requirement on the distance fields, the authors present two core
tricks that can be applied to CSG-tree-flavored models:
Pruning
identifies primitives which are inactive within a particular
region of space, and builds a simplified shape with only active primitives
Far-field culling
finds primitives which are far from a particular
region (and therefore not relevant), and replaces them with a simpler
expression.
These optimizations make rendering dramatically cheaper, allowing for
interactive visualizations of complex models.
The first optimization also sounds familiar â I presented something
similar
back in 2020
(which
itself builds on
work from 1992
):
To render a model, its underlying expression is evaluated in a shallow
hierarchy of spatial regions, using a high branching factor for efficient
parallelization. Interval arithmetic is used to both skip empty regions and
construct reduced versions of the expression. The latter is the optimization
that makes our algorithm practical: in one benchmark, expression complexity
decreases by two orders of magnitude between the original and reduced
expressions.
Here's the big difference: my implementation used
interval arithmetic
on arbitrary math expressions, while this new paper uses single-point evaluation
on Lipschitz-continuous primitives.
Single-point evaluation is cheaper, and also doesn't suffer from the
conservative nature of interval arithmetic (where intervals tend to grow over
time).  However, their shapes are limited to a set of well-behaved primitives
and transforms; something as simple as scaling a model can break Lipschitz
continuity if not handled carefully.
After thinking about it for a few days, I ended up taking home a slightly
different conclusion than the paper presented:
If your distance field is Lipschitz-continuous, then you can use single-point
evaluation to get interval-ish results, then apply all the usual tricks which
normally require interval arithmetic.
I've now gone far too long without showing a pretty picture (the magpies in the
audience are growing rowdy), so let's dig into some examples.  I'm going to
take this idea â of using single-point evaluations to get pseudo-intervals â and
see how it applies to my usual box of tools.
Note that I'm not hewing to the implementation from the paper (which you should
go read, it's great!); I'm taking this idea and running in a slightly different
direction based on my background knowledge.
Basic rendering
Here's a circle of radius 1, $f(x, y) = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} - 1$:
It's rendered with orange / blue indicating whether we're inside or outside the
shape, and field lines showing the distance field values.  I'm not sure who
developed the original coloring strategy, but it's pervasive on Shadertoy; I
borrowed it from
Inigo Quilez
.
My typical strategy for rendering is to do several rounds of evaluation using
interval arithmetic, then pixel-by-pixel evaluation of the remaining ambiguous
regions.  The goal is to produce a binary image: each pixel is either inside or
outside, depending on sign.
Interval evaluation takes intervals for $x$ and $y$, and returns an interval
output.
For example, we can evaluate a region in the top-left quadrant:
$$f([0.5, 1.5], [0.5, 1.5]) = [-0.3, 1.12]$$
Because the interval result is ambiguous (contains 0), we can't prove this
region inside or outside the shape, so we subdivide and recurse.  If it was
unambiguously less than or greater than zero, we could stop processing right
away!
